 \sup_h\Pr(H=h\mid F_0)\le CQ^{-5/2}.                        \tag{138.24}
$$

This includes all preimages of each projected integer, not an assumed atom bound for a nonlinear image. No independent uniform fractional phase is used.

Choose fixed large D_w and W=D_wQ^(3/2)sqrt(log Q). On G_Q, the joint split window|k-K_+/2|,|l-K_-/2|<=W fails with conditional probability at most4Q^-204. On it,

 |H-H^0|\le CQ^{5/2}\sqrt{\log Q},\quad|\bar X|\le CQ^2,
 \quad|X-\bar X|\le\delta_X,
$$
$$
 \delta_X=CQ^{3/2}\sqrt{\log Q}(q/M+e^{-cQ^5}).                 \tag{138.25}
$$

Since|f'_t(X)|<=cosh t cosh X/(cosh t+cosh X)^2<=1/4, the hidden preimage changes f by at most delta_X/4. This is a uniform necessary-event error. H is not declared sufficient for the exact posterior, and the physical center is not altered.

### 138.5 实际平台区间及共同例外事件

The elementary136 saturation bounds are, for T>=2L,

 |X|\le T-L\implies0\le1-f_T(X)\le4e^{-L},\qquad

 p_*\in\bigcup_{z=-1}^1 I_z,\qquad

The union and its centers/width are F_0-measurable; the realized index may depend on the same allocations and central membership. The common failure probability for this assertion and its retained-region/window conditions is at most

 b_{env}(Q)+C(Q^{-3/2}\log Q+e^{-cQ})+4Q^{-204}.                \tag{138.28}

The broad polynomial plateau accuracy will only identify candidate rational levels. It will NOT replace the exact curved response in the exponentially thin strip calculation below.

### 138.6 整段谐波至多九个共同有理响应值

Keep the original half-integer energy

 E^{min}_{\ell,x}=4\pi^2\sum_{j\in J}d_j

If E_min(ell)<=Q^2 for some1<=ell<=N, its central term supplies an integer h and actual membership C in{n_0,n_0+1,n_0+2} with

Here c_1 is a fixed sufficiently large model constant from d_0 comparable C. Apply the joint-level lemma to the intervals(138.27). Its rational interval is centered at alpha_(C,z)=1/2-Cp_z and has radius

 R_{C,Q}=Cr_Q+\tau_C
 \le C_1[Q^{-23}+Q^{-3}\delta_X+Q^{-3}/q+Q^{5/2}/\sqrt q].     \tag{138.31}

Every term is controlled by the original floors(138.11–12); c_q and phi are fixed positive constants. The compensated score error is exp(-phi Q^3+O(log Q)), and the decimal tail is smaller. Thus, for each of the nine pairs(C,z), there is at most one rational value r_(C,z) with reduced denominator at most N in J_(C,z). If none exists, no corresponding harmonic is bad. If it exists, all h/ell in that interval equal r_(C,z), including all nonreduced multiples. The numerator can be of exponential size because C is large; (138.6) is independent of that size. All candidate intervals retain their exact real centers, including the common full-q offset. No Diophantine hypothesis on an empirical coefficient is imposed.

For any such candidate, (138.9),(138.21),(138.25) imply on the joint window the necessary event

 |f_t(\bar X)-c_{C,z}|\le\varepsilon_Q,\quad

$$

                                      +C_3\delta_X.            \tag{138.33}

The q multiplication of the full-q O(q^-2) remainder is included. The first term follows from D_o times Q/C^(3/2), using C comparable q/Q^3. We deliberately use the ell=1 tolerance, so the SAME level and width contain every multiple representation of the candidate rational. By(138.11–12),

$$

The hidden-score term is smaller for every original beta>1/2 because phi>c_q. Crucially there is no Q^-20 term in(138.33). Plateau accuracy located the rational; the exact response now controls closeness to it. Using the plateau error itself as the strip width would invalidate the next estimate.

### 138.7 单池曲率控制全部谐波

The exact second derivative is

$$
 f_t''(X)={\sinh t(\cosh^2X-\cosh t\cosh X-2)
                          \over(\cosh t+\cosh X)^3}.            \tag{138.35}
$$

Let r_t=(cosh t+sqrt(cosh^2t+8))/2, theta_t=arcosh r_t. As in136, |t|<=theta_t<=|t|+log6. For large Q the three retained intervals bar X<=-|t|-L, |bar X|<=|t|-L, bar X>=|t|+L are at least unit distance from the inflections. The sign is sign(t) on the outer intervals and -sign(t) in the middle.

Factor the numerator polynomial as(cosh X-r_t)(cosh X-s_t), where s_t in[-1,0). Unit separation bounds the first absolute factor below by a fixed positive constant, the second is at least1, and|sinh t|>=sinh1. On G_Q and the projected window, |t|,|bar X|<=CQ^2. The denominator is at most exp(C'Q^2). After differentiation with respect to H, whose score step is b_s/Q, this proves

$$
 |\partial_H^2 f_t((b_s/Q)(H-H^0))|
             \ge\kappa_Q:=cQ^{-2}e^{-C'Q^2}.                   \tag{138.36}
$$

Each retained interval intersected with the projected window is a convex real interval with a fixed nonzero curvature sign. Equations(138.34),(138.36) give4epsilon_Q<kappa_Q eventually. Hence(138.10) allows at most two integer H points in each of the three intervals for ANY level c_(C,z), for a total of at most six.

These levels are F_0-measurable, so the ORIGINAL conditional projected atom estimate(138.24) applies directly. For each candidate rational the probability of its necessary retained-window event is at most6C Q^-5/2. This counts every hidden (k,l) preimage; it does not assert that the full response is a function of H alone. Allocations outside the joint window were already paid, and allowing H with no central lawful preimage only enlarges the bound.

There are at most nine candidate pairs(C,z). Union over these pairs, NOT over ell, and add the common exceptional events(138.28) once. Negative harmonics have the same E_min. We obtain the quantitative original-law theorem

$$
 \boxed{\sup_S\Pr_S\{\exists1\le|\ell|\le N:
                            E^{min}_{\ell,x}\le Q^2\}
 \le b_{env}(Q)+C(Q^{-3/2}\log Q+e^{-cQ}+Q^{-5/2})+4Q^{-204}
                          \longrightarrow0.}                 \tag{138.37}
$$

No bad-environment term is multiplied by N. The actual finite conditional law, unique rational candidates, exact response and hidden-fiber errors all concern the SAME realization. The general high-dimensional convex-position exponent is no longer a premise. A single narrow rational interval can contain many resonant harmonic representations, but all of them now require one curved-response strip event. That is the joint restriction missing from the earlier harmonic union.

### 138.8 五次逆带宽下的计数回接

Arithmetic alone is not the target. Intersect(138.37) with the observed original regularity, direction and localization events reused in136, whose support-uniform failure tends to zero. They need not hold on every resampling fiber or be F_0-measurable. The two proof labels have never been removed from the physical count law, comparison array or scalar.

At(138.1), rho^-1<=CQ^5, sigma<=mathcal B^-1 eventually and log(1/sigma)=c_qQ^3+O(log Q). Keep J={j:d_j>=Q^3600} and every original remaining group E. The signed binomial/lattice comparison through exactly centered surprise degree4 costs Cd_j^-1/8<=CQ^-450 per bulk factor. $$
 h_2(t)=(1-\sigma^2t^2)e^{-\sigma^2t^2/2},\qquad

$$

These are polynomials in sigma t, not bare t; absorbing the polynomial and substituting v=rho theta in the period integral costs one inverse rho, not one per mark. The full real-axis signed Fourier estimate now is

$$
 \max_{h\le2}\|\widehat q_h^{prod}-\widehat q_h^{lat}\|_1
       \le C(1+\rho^{-1})Q^{-440}\le CQ^{-435}.                 \tag{138.39}
$$

q_h is the density of(s+G^2/2)^h with each law's exactly centered surprise s and the unchanged physical energy. Empirical-center phase factors have modulus1; no center displacement is divided by sigma. Fourier inversion on|y|<=Q^100 and the inherited fourth target norm CQ/bounded fourth output moment give global signed L1 error at most C(Q^-335+Q^-198)=O(Q^-198).

The direct signed-kernel check111.40–41 is stronger and independent of sigma: telescope the centered signed tuple measures through degree2 to TV error CQ^-444, then apply the common kernels

$$
 K_r(k,y)=((y-T(k))/\sigma)^{2r}\varphi_\sigma(y-T(k)),\qquad

$$

Their fixed L1 norms retain the same residual and all tuple coordinates. This is an explicit signed-mark comparison, not inference of unbounded moments from scalar TV.

For the complete nonlinear expression q_2-q_1^2/q_0, use q_1^2/q_0=sup_z(2zq_1-z^2q_0), clipped to|z|<=Q^10. Conditional Jensen and fourth moments pay O(Q^-16) for clipping, and the signed-density error times Q^20 vanishes. The original selected/full-q correction111.19–24, including its surprise log-density correction, is Ca_xQ^2=O_P(Q^-1/2), a_x=O_P(Q^-5/2), and contains no inverse sigma. Thus at the NEW bandwidth,

D_lat uses its own exact prior variance and the ORIGINAL A^2/Lambda-C_xy. The allocation coordinate and number of proof pools enter none of these physical estimates.

### 138.9 精确实倾斜、带标记别名和分母

Use the SAME normalized real tilt by W=s+G^2/2 at FIXED physical output y and fixed original energy/centers. Put tau=1-u,a_j=(mu_j-m_j)/sqrt(d_j),w_j=d_j/mathcal B. In the original half-integer strip t=pi ell mathcal B+s define

 \xi_{\ell k,j}=\sqrt{d_j}[\pi\ell(1-2\mu_j)-2\pi k_j],

 \quad\eta_\ell=\pi\ell\rho.

The exact normalized-temperature Poisson identity remains

 \Psi_{\ell k}(u,s)=c_{lat}(u)z_{\ell k}

$$
 \quad\times\exp\left[-\tfrac12\sum_J

P has bounded fixed Fourier moments. The residual derivatives are exactly the normalized h2/h4 factors; no new inverse noise occurs inside this bound. Use the integrated sufficient alias criterion

 C(1+\rho^{-1})Q^{-428}\le CQ^{-423}.                          \tag{138.45}

This covers the entire real Fourier axis; no frequency is discarded because the arithmetic cutoff exceeds the former Q^3 or Q^4 scale. For the same continuous-bulk reference g_u and Delta_j=partial_u^j(f_lat,u-g_u)|_0,

$$
 \max_{j\le2}\|\Delta_j\|_\infty
                \le CQ^8\mathcal A_x(\rho)+CQ^{-423}.          \tag{138.46}

On the actual event(138.37), split the alias sum at N. Below N use E_min>Q^2; above N use rho^2N^2>=10^6log Q. Gaussian summation with exponent slack gives

$$
 \mathcal A_x(\rho)\le C(1+\rho^{-1})
       [e^{-Q^2/1024}+e^{-\pi^2\rho^2N^2/1024}]
 \le CQ^5[e^{-Q^2/1024}+Q^{-10^6\pi^2/1024}].                  \tag{138.47}
$$

The numerical1000 cutoff pays the Q^5 period factor and the fixed derivative powers. Hence all three Delta_j are O(Q^-400). The arithmetic statement is uniform enough for the same two marked derivatives and residual, not only the unmarked marginal.

On|y|<=h_Q^out=sqrt(100nu log Q), the already established fixed-order reference local expansion gives g_0>=cQ^-60 and|g_1|+|g_2|<=CQ^4. It needs only sigma<=mathcal B^-1, not a positive lower rho.        +\Delta_0(2g_1^2/g_0^3-g_2/g_0^2).                     \tag{138.48}

The largest coefficient costs Q^188. Therefore F''/F-(F'/F)^2=O(Q^-200) uniformly on this interval. More generally(138.44) suffices through(138.46), since8+188<200. Positivity is established before division; the exponentially bad worst-case heat-kernel minimum is unused.

## 139. 移动双阱内的局部高斯波动与输出中心位移

第 137 章给出超临界介观窗口中的等权双阱。本章进一步在同一原始乘积计数后验中确定有限经验鞍点中心，证明井内波动与公平符号的联合极限。输出对主导作用量的修正虽可忽略，却在局部高斯尺度上留下有限位移；精确中心保留这项差别。

### 139.1 原始乘积计数律与局部高斯结论

**定理 139.1（移动双阱的局部高斯极限）。** Retain the exact objects of Chapter 137:
$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q\delta^5,\quad
 L=\log(1/\sigma)\to\infty,\quad
 \limsup L/Q^3<c_q/2,\qquad c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta,
$$
$$
 Q(n)=\prod_j\operatorname{Bin}(C_j,p_j)(n_j),\quad
 v_j=C_jp_j(1-p_j)/B^2,\quad V=\sum_jv_j,
 \quad C_2=\delta^{-1}\sum_jv_j^2,
$$
$$
 e_j=(\mu_j-C_jp_j)/B,\quad x_j=(n_j-\mu_j)/B,
 \quad E=\sum_jx_j^2,\quad D=\sum_j(x_j+e_j),
 \quad T=(E-V)/\sqrt\delta.
 \tag{139.1}
$$
The original legal amplitude, beta, all Q,M,q/group floors, full window, binomial multiplicities and calibrated mu,V,T remain fixed. Empty or zero-variance coordinates are deterministic. Q is the auxiliary PRODUCT count law with the original full-q calibration; it is not the original support-selection law P.

For EACH deterministic eta=eta_Q>0 such that eta->0 and t=eta/sqrt(delta)->infinity, put
$$
 v=\eta^2/\delta=t^2,\quad a=(2V)^{-1}+\eta,
 \quad h_y=V+\sqrt\delta y,
 \quad \pi_y(n)\propto Q(n)
           \exp\{aD(n)^2-(T(n)-y)^2/(2\sigma^2)\}.
 \tag{139.2}
$$
Sigma is positive at every finite level and may tend to zero arbitrarily slowly subject to (139.1). Let r_*(Q,y) be the canonical finite real-saddle center defined in (139.8), let S=sign(D), with sign(0)=0, and
$$
 W=2\sqrt\eta\{D-Sr_*(Q,y)\},\qquad
 m_Q=\sqrt{2V^4/C_2}.
 \tag{139.3}
$$
For each fixed R<infinity, the center satisfies uniformly |y|<=R
$$
 r_*(Q,y)/[\sqrt{\eta/\delta}\,m_Q]\to1.
 \tag{139.4}
$$
For each fixed continuous function F on {-1,0,1} times R, continuous in its real coordinate, with |F(s,w)|<=C(1+|w|^p) for some fixed finite p,
$$
 \sup_{|y|\le R}\left|
 E_{\pi_y}F(S,W)-\frac12\sum_{s\in\{-1,1\}}
               \int_{\mathbb R}F(s,w)\frac{e^{-w^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,dw
                 \right|\to0.
 \tag{139.5}
$$
In particular pi_y(D=0)->0 uniformly. All limits are in original actual-data probability, uniformly over deterministic size-q supports, separately for the original pair and path laws. Explicitly the supremum over those supports of the probability that a displayed same-fiber output supremum exceeds a fixed positive tolerance tends to zero. There is no added independence of actual path rows. All empirical coefficients remain those of the same realized data fiber.

Every fixed polynomial moment and mixed sign moment follows from (139.5). There is no discrete-to-continuous total variation assertion, growing-moment uniformity, entropy derivative or full-q P claim. The center and derivatives below concern auxiliary exact Gaussian transforms of that same empirical array; neither the physical count D nor the physical output T is recalibrated after observation.

### 139.2 同一实际数据类与既有接口

We work first on each fixed tight-constant class of Chapters 133, 135 and 137. The simultaneous bounds are
$$
 n_g\le C\delta^{-4},\quad p_j\in[1/4,3/4],\quad
 \sum C_j\le CB^2,\quad \log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),
$$
$$
 c\le V,C_2\le C,\quad v_*\le C\delta,\quad
 |e_j|\le C\delta^5\sqrt{v_j},\quad
 \|e\|^2\le C\delta^{10},\quad (\sum|e_j|)^2\le C\delta^6.
 \tag{139.6}
$$
A block of at least c/delta coordinates has variances in [c delta,C delta]. Their complements are exhausted support-uniformly in actual probability. All subsequent bounds hold on one common class and one common fiber, rather than separately selected environments.

Fix the high block used in Chapter 137: H={j:C_j>=exp(zeta Q^3)}, with fixed admissible l,zeta satisfying eventually L<=lQ^3, l<c_q/2, zeta<c_q/2, 2zeta<c_q-l. The choice is fixed once, before the y supremum. Put V_H=sum_H v_j and s_k=sum_H v_j^k. Then V-V_H>=0 and V-V_H+|s_2-delta C_2|<=P(Q)exp(-bQ^3), b>0; the variance block belongs to H. The exact low tuples are kept in the count return, not deleted. Canonical below means the specified finite transform for this fixed high block and original full V,h_y,sigma. It contains no optimization over data environments or choice based on the desired limiting law.

The applicable prior interfaces are (137.7) for the ordinary energy density, (137.20), (137.22), (137.23) for moderate logarithmic estimates and global weighted tails, (137.25)–(137.27) for relative actual-e versus centered Gaussian densities on compact rescaled-charge sets, and (137.30)–(137.34) for the exponentially accurate same-output cell lift and its fixed polynomial weights. Their scopes match alpha=1 and the present eta/noise range. They provide the outside-well and count payments below. None supplies the missing local derivatives, local normalization or prefactor-mode displacement; those are proved here.

### 139.3 有限经验实鞍点中心

Let C_H=diag(v_j)_{j in H}, w_H=(v_j)_{j in H}, d=w_H/V_H, and
$$
 A=C_H-w_Hw_H^T/V_H,\quad b_H=\|d\|^2=s_2/V_H^2,
 \quad r_H=(2V_H)^{-1}-(2V)^{-1},\quad \gamma=\eta-r_H.
 \tag{139.7}
$$
The symbol b_H is a scalar coefficient, not a binomial mass. It satisfies b_H~delta C_2/V^2; gamma/eta->1 and gamma>0 eventually. The latter uses the exponential bound on r_H and eta>=sqrt(delta) eventually. A has the retained block after rank-one interlacing, ||A||<=C delta and tr A^2=s_2+O(delta^2).

For real z below the first positive covariance pole define EXACTLY
$$
 K_0(z)=-\tfrac12\log\det(I-2zA)+\tfrac12\delta\sigma^2z^2,
 \qquad \Psi(z)=z\,d^T(I-2zA)^{-1}d.
$$
The canonical system and center are
$$
 \boxed{\ \Psi(z_*)=-\gamma,\qquad
 R_*(y)=\frac{h_y-K_0'(z_*)}{\Psi'(z_*)},\qquad
 r_*(Q,y)=\sqrt{R_*(y)}\ }.                         \tag{139.8}
$$
This is a one-dimensional REAL equation followed by an explicit positive square root. It is a definition by the finite empirical spectrum and noise, not by a limiting law or an assumed mode. The tilt z_* is independent of y; R_* depends affinely on physical y. All low groups still contribute to the original V in h_y and in gamma. The original e is retained in the actual posterior and paid by relative comparison in Section 139.7 and the count return in Section 139.8. Its omission in this centered analytic transform is not a change of physical mu.

Here is existence and uniqueness. On |z|delta<=a_0, for sufficiently small fixed a_0, diagonalization gives
$$
 \Psi'(z)=d^T(I-2zA)^{-2}d\asymp\delta,
 \quad |\Psi^{(k)}(z)|\le C_k\delta^k\ (k\ge1),
$$
$$
 K_0''(z)\asymp\delta,\quad
 |K_0^{(k)}(z)|\le C_k\delta^{k-1}\ (k\ge3).
 \tag{139.9}
$$
For example Psi^(k)(z)=2^(k-1)k! d^TA^(k-1)(I-2zA)^(-k-1)d. The second noise derivative is delta sigma^2 and is included in K_0''. No noise inverse appears. Since Psi(0)=0 and Psi'>0, evaluation on a bracket [-C eta/delta,0] proves a unique negative root in (139.8), with
$$
 z_*=-\gamma/b_H+O(\eta^2/\delta),\qquad |z_*|\delta=O(\eta).
 \tag{139.10}
$$
Strict positivity of Psi' throughout its real domain makes this root unique there as well.

Set k_H=K_0''(0)=2tr A^2+delta sigma^2. Since K_0'(0)=tr A=V_H-s_2/V_H,
$$
 h_y-K_0'(z_*)=-k_Hz_*+\sqrt\delta y
                   +V-V_H+s_2/V_H+O(\eta^2).
 \tag{139.11}
$$
The first term is positive and comparable to eta, whereas sqrt(delta)y and delta are o(eta). Thus R_*(y)>0 uniformly on each fixed y compact eventually. Equations (139.9)--(139.11) imply
$$
 R_*(y)=\frac\eta\delta\,
          \frac{V^4(2C_2+\sigma^2)}{C_2^2}
          \{1+O(\eta+t^{-1}+\sqrt\delta)+o_{\exp}(1)\}.
 \tag{139.12}
$$
Here o_exp denotes an exponentially small error times a fixed power of Q; eta^-1 is absorbed because eta>=sqrt(delta). Sigma is retained inside (139.12). Only after this calculation does sigma->0 give (139.4). No such expansion replaces the EXACT (139.8) in W. In particular its discarded relative terms can be much larger than1/t.

The center is a measurable function of the finite array, since the strictly monotone root is continuous on the common class. For completeness it may be defined as1 off the event where the negative root and positive numerator exist; the probability of that exceptional event tends to zero uniformly. This extension is not used in the theorem's estimates.

### 139.4 精确密度分解与前因子导数

Let Y_j~N(0,v_j), j in H, before observation, with D_G=sum_HY_j. Conditional on D_G=r, the CENTERED energy sum_HY_j^2 plus N~N(0,delta sigma^2) has cumulant
$$
 K(z,R)=K_0(z)+R\Psi(z),\qquad R=r^2.
 \tag{139.13}
$$
This follows from the exact conditional vector mean rd and covariance A. It is not a spherical model. Let f_r^0(h_y) denote this energy density, and define the unnormalized centered Gaussian charge density after the physical penalty, omitting an r-independent constant, by
$$
 g_y(r)=e^{\gamma r^2}f_r^0(h_y).
 \tag{139.14}
$$
It is exactly even. For R in any fixed moderate interval 0<=R<=M^2 eta/delta, the unique real solution z(R) of K_z(z(R),R)=h_y satisfies |z(R)|delta<=C_M(eta+sqrt(delta)); this follows from Chapter 137's real-saddle argument or directly from (139.9) and the mean displacement O_M(eta+sqrt(delta)). Sigma>0 ensures global existence; only this small real branch is needed.

Put
$$
 \mathcal W(R)=K_{zz}(z(R),R),\quad
 H_y(R)=\gamma R+K(z(R),R)-z(R)h_y.
 \tag{139.15}
$$
On this interval mathcal W~delta, K_{zzz}=O_M(delta^2), K_{zzzz}=O_M(delta^3), and the analogous vertical-line resolvent bounds hold. Implicit differentiation of the EXACT saddle equation gives
$$
 z_R=-\Psi'/\mathcal W=O(1),\quad
 z_{RR}=-(K_{zzz}z_R^2+2\Psi''z_R)/\mathcal W=O(\delta),
$$
$$
 H_R=\gamma+\Psi(z),\quad
 H_{RR}=-\frac{\Psi'(z)^2}{\mathcal W}\asymp-\delta,
 \qquad H_{RRR}=O_M(\delta^2).
 \tag{139.16}
$$
All functions on the right are evaluated at the same saddle and same R. In particular H_R(R_*)=0 exactly, by (139.8), and H is strictly concave as a function of R throughout the moderate interval. This proves local uniqueness of the positive action stationary point without assuming a mode or differentiating an error term.

We need the actual density prefactor, not just H. With omega=xi/sqrt(delta), define
$$
 L(R,\xi)=K(z(R)+i\omega,R)-K(z(R),R)-i\omega h_y,
 \quad p_y(R)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{L(R,\xi)}d\xi.
 \tag{139.17}
$$
Then p_y(R) is sqrt(delta) times the tilted density at its EXACT mean. The exact density-change formula is
$$
 g_y(r)=\delta^{-1/2}e^{H_y(r^2)}p_y(r^2).
 \tag{139.18}
$$
The real tilted covariance is A(I-2zA)^-1 and its mean is (I-2zA)^-1rd. It retains at least c/delta eigenvalues comparable to delta; the noncentral variance is O_M(delta eta). Thus
$$
 |e^{L(R,\xi)}|\le(1+c\delta\xi^2)^{-c'/\delta},
 \quad c_M\le p_y(R)\le C_M.
 \tag{139.19}
$$
The positive lower bound follows by the local Fourier limit at the mean, with variance mathcal W/delta bounded above and below: p_y(R)=(2pi mathcal W/delta)^(-1/2)+o_M(1). The fixed-frequency remainder is O_M(sqrt(delta)(1+|xi|^3)); the block envelope gives uniform integrability of every fixed xi power by splitting at |xi|=delta^-1/2. This also applies at R=0 and when the real saddle is slightly positive. No zero-free complex-order premise is needed; the Fourier integrand is the exact transform at a real tilt.

We now prove actual PARAMETER derivatives of p. Hold h_y,delta,sigma,A,d fixed. Differentiating the integrand's exponent gives exactly
$$
 L_R=\Psi(z+i\omega)-\Psi(z)
       +z_R\{K_z(z+i\omega,R)-K_z(z,R)\},
$$
$$
 L_{RR}=2z_R\{\Psi'(z+i\omega)-\Psi'(z)\}
       +z_R^2\{K_{zz}(z+i\omega,R)-K_{zz}(z,R)\}
       +z_{RR}\{K_z(z+i\omega,R)-K_z(z,R)\}.
 \tag{139.20}
$$
Each right side has zero constant AND zero linear term in omega. For the first, the linear coefficient is Psi'+z_R mathcal W=0. For the second it is 2z_R Psi''+z_R^2 K_{zzz}+z_{RR}mathcal W=0. Along the full vertical segment, the real part of z stays below the pole with |z|delta=o(1), so the spectral resolvents have norm at most a constant. Bounds (139.9) and the K derivative bounds therefore give, for every real xi,
$$
 |L_R|\le C_M\delta\xi^2,\qquad
 |L_{RR}|\le C_M\delta^2\xi^2.
 \tag{139.21}
$$
These are Taylor bounds along the exact vertical segment, not small-xi assertions. For example the second-order coefficient of L_R is bounded by Cdelta^2; that of L_RR by Cdelta^3, and omega^2=xi^2/delta.

The exact derivatives of exp L are L_R exp L and (L_RR+L_R^2)exp L. Equations (139.19),(139.21) justify differentiation under the integral on a neighborhood of each R and yield
$$
 |p_R|\le C_M\delta,\quad |p_{RR}|\le C_M\delta^2,
 \quad |(\log p)_R|\le C_M\delta,\quad
 |(\log p)_{RR}|\le C_M\delta^2.
 \tag{139.22}
$$
This supplies the missing derivative interface. The extensive determinant contribution has canceled through the saddle equation before estimating its derivative. A C0 approximation to p, or to Chapter 137's logarithm, would not imply (139.22).

### 139.5 局部模态、曲率和密度比

Write ell_y(r)=log g_y(r). In the R coordinate it equals H_y(R)+log p_y(R)-(1/2)log delta. By (139.16),(139.22), its second R derivative is at most -c delta throughout a fixed moderate interval containing R_*. Its first R derivative at R_* is O(delta). Taking two points R_*+/-C_0 with a sufficiently large constant C_0 makes the derivatives have opposite signs. Both points are positive eventually, since R_*~eta/delta->infinity. Hence a unique root R_mode in that interval exists, is a strict maximum, and
$$
 |R_{\rm mode}-R_*|\le C,
 \quad \widehat r=\sqrt{R_{\rm mode}},\quad
 2\sqrt\eta\,|\widehat r-r_*|\le C\sqrt\delta\to0.
 \tag{139.23}
$$
Strict concavity in R shows this is the unique positive local mode in any fixed small fractional neighborhood of r_* and therefore the corresponding exact centered-Gaussian local mode. Its negative partner follows from evenness. We use the explicit saddle center (139.8) in the theorem; (139.23) proves the prefactor shift is negligible rather than assuming it.

Let mathcal W_*=K_0''(z_*)+R_*Psi''(z_*). The key curvature identity is
$$
 \frac{R_*\Psi'(z_*)^2}{\mathcal W_*}
          =\eta\{1+O(\eta+t^{-1}+\sqrt\delta)+o_{\exp}(1)\}.
 \tag{139.24}
$$
Indeed R_*Psi'^2/mathcal W_*=(h_y-K_0'(z_*))Psi'/mathcal W_*; (139.9)--(139.11) give h_y-K_0'(z_*)=-k_Hz_*+O(sqrt(delta)+delta+eta^2), Psi'=b_H(1+O(eta)), mathcal W_*=k_H(1+O(eta)), and -z_*b_H=gamma(1+O(eta)). Since sqrt(delta)/eta=1/t, the displayed error follows. Finite sigma is in k_H and cancels at this leading curvature calculation; it was not set to zero.

In the r coordinate the action derivatives are
$$
 (H(r^2))'=2rH_R,\quad
 (H(r^2))''=2H_R+4r^2H_{RR},\quad
 (H(r^2))'''=12rH_{RR}+8r^3H_{RRR}.
 \tag{139.25}
$$
At r_* the first is zero and the second is -4eta(1+o(1)) by (139.24). The third is O(sqrt(delta eta)) on a fixed small fractional neighborhood of r_*; (139.16) gives the bound O(delta r+delta^2 r^3). The log-prefactor has first r derivative O(delta r_*) and second derivative O(delta+delta^2 r_*^2)=O(delta)=o(eta). Thus the EXACT centered-density curvature at r_* is -4eta(1+o(1)), and ell'_y(r_*)=O(sqrt(delta eta)).

Choose once a sufficiently small fixed epsilon_0>0. On |r/r_*-1|<=epsilon_0, H_RR differs from H_RR(R_*) by O(delta eta), by (139.16), while H_R=H_RR(R_*)(R-R_*)+O(delta^2(R-R_*)^2). The principal part of (139.25)'s second derivative is H_RR(R_*)(6R-2R_*). This is bounded above by -c eta on this band; the O(eta^2) action error and O(delta) prefactor error are smaller. Consequently
$$
 \ell_y''(r)\le-c\eta
       \quad\hbox{for }|r/r_*-1|\le\varepsilon_0.
 \tag{139.26}
$$
This is local concavity of the actual centered density, not a curvature bound inferred from a large-deviation rate.

For each fixed finite M and |w|<=M, r=r_*+w/(2sqrt(eta)) is in the band eventually because 2sqrt(eta)r_*~2tm_Q->infinity. Taylor's formula applied to the EXACT action, (139.24),(139.25), and the Lipschitz estimate (139.22) for log p give
$$
 \sup_{|y|\le R,|w|\le M}
 \left|\log\frac{g_y(r_*+w/(2\sqrt\eta))}{g_y(r_*)}
                      +\frac{w^2}{2}\right|\to0.
 \tag{139.27}
$$
The action's cubic remainder costs O_M(sqrt(delta)/eta)=O_M(1/t). The prefactor increment costs O_M(sqrt(delta)+delta/eta). An adequate local error bound is C_M(eta+t^-1+sqrt(delta)+delta/eta)+o_exp(1). Thus no eta^3/delta->0, t^2>>log Q or additional sigma rate is hidden in (139.27).

Integrating (139.26) from r_*, with ell'_y(r_*)=O(sqrt(delta eta)), also gives a uniform moving-scale envelope throughout the band:
$$
 \frac{g_y(r_*+w/(2\sqrt\eta))}{g_y(r_*)}
           \le C\exp(-c_1w^2),\qquad
 |w|\le2\varepsilon_0\sqrt\eta\,r_*.
 \tag{139.28}
$$
The harmless intermediate linear term is C sqrt(delta)|w| and is absorbed by a smaller quadratic coefficient. This supplies local tails strong enough for all fixed moments inside the well.

### 139.6 移动尺度上的完整尾部

Let u=sqrt(delta/eta)r and u_*=sqrt(delta/eta)r_*. On our common classes u_* stays bounded above and away from zero, and u_*-m_Q->0 uniformly in y. Write B_+={r>0:|r/r_*-1|<=epsilon_0}, B_-=-B_+. We need to control the complement on the W scale; concentration on the u scale alone does not do this.

The centered version of (137.18) is
$$
 w_Q^0(u,y)=\frac{g_y(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}
                   {\sqrt{2\pi V_H}\,f^0(h_y)}.
 \tag{139.29}
$$
Here f^0 is the unconditional high centered energy-plus-noise density with full original h_y. The factor is independent of u and cancels in every ratio used below. The proof of (137.20)–(137.23) permits e=0 with the same array and full h_y. Consequently, on every fixed compact u interval,
$$
 v^{-1}\log w_Q^0(u,y)=F_Q(u)+o(1),\quad
 F_Q(u)=u^2-\frac{C_2}{4V^4}u^4,
 \tag{139.30}
$$
uniformly, and outside a fixed large compact
$$
 w_Q^0(u,y)\le C\exp\left[v\left\{u^2-
                      \frac{c u^4}{1+\eta u^2}\right\}\right].
 \tag{139.31}
$$
For clarity, these inherited bounds retain the scaled saddle-density prefactor between two positive constants before any speed limit; they do not hide a power of Q. They include the finite Gaussian noise inside the real tilt. The maxima of F_Q are at +/-m_Q, with G_Q=V^4/C_2 uniformly positive. Since u_*-m_Q->0, (139.30) shows that on any fixed compact outside B_+ union B_-,
$$
 \frac{g_y(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}{g_y(r_*)}
       =\frac{w_Q^0(u,y)}{w_Q^0(u_*,y)}\le e^{-c_2v}
 \tag{139.32}
$$
for all large Q, with c_2>0 depending on the fixed band and class. This uses the uniformly positive gap of the quartic away from its two maxima, not a rate-limit claim about local fluctuations.

For any fixed power p, the far-u integral of (139.31), with weight1+|u|^p, is at most C exp(-Bv) for any prescribed B after enlarging the fixed cutoff. Indeed u^2/(1+eta u^2) is increasing; beyond that cutoff the braces in (139.31) are bounded by an arbitrarily large negative multiple of u^2, eventually. Dividing by w_Q^0(u_*,y)>=exp(vG_Q/2) only improves this tail. The same estimates hold for actual-e Gaussian densities, using Chapter 137's relative comparison on compact u and its global tail bound outside.

Equation (139.27) gives the local normalization lower bound
$$
 \int_{\mathbb R}g_y(r)\,dr\ge c\,g_y(r_*)/\sqrt\eta.
 \tag{139.33}
$$
The decisive scale payment is exact: dr=sqrt(eta/delta)du, so the ratio of the u Jacobian to the local normalization scale1/sqrt(eta) is t=eta/sqrt(delta). Also
$$
 W=2t\{u-\operatorname{sign}(u)u_*\},\qquad
 |W|^p\le C_p t^p(1+|u|^p).
 \tag{139.34}
$$
Combining (139.31)--(139.34), for each fixed p>=0 the normalized mass of the complement of B_+ union B_-, with weight1+|W|^p, is at most
$$
 C_p t^{p+1}e^{-c_3t^2}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{139.35}
$$
The constants may change after choosing a far cutoff. This tends to zero for EVERY arbitrarily slowly diverging t. Replacing the Jacobian ratio by a power of delta^-1 would invalidate this argument; we have not done so. No logQ term is divided by v.

Inside each band, (139.28) supplies an integrable bound for every fixed polynomial in w. Its endpoints in the w coordinate tend to +/-infinity because sqrt(eta)r_* is comparable to t. Dominated convergence using (139.27),(139.28), followed by (139.35), now yields
$$
 \int_{r>0}g_y(r)\,dr
     =\frac{g_y(r_*)}{2\sqrt\eta}\{\sqrt{2\pi}+o(1)\},
 \quad
 \int_{\mathbb R}g_y(r)\,dr
     =\frac{g_y(r_*)}{\sqrt\eta}\{\sqrt{2\pi}+o(1)\}.
 \tag{139.36}
$$
Both formulas, and their local versions with each fixed polynomial-growth continuous test, hold uniformly in y. Exact evenness gives equal masses for the centered Gaussian law. At the negative well write r=-r_*+w/(2sqrt(eta)); evenness replaces w by -w in (139.27), whose Gaussian limit is even. Thus this reference already has the fair-sign times standard-normal limit, including every fixed moment. Independence is the equality of the two conditional Gaussian limits, not just equality of two rate minima.

### 139.7 实际非中心项与相对反射

Let g_y^e(r)=exp(gamma r^2)f_r^e(h_y), where f_r^e uses the actual high-block center e_H in sum(Y_j-e_j)^2. This comparison is on the SAME charge r, h_y, covariance A and noise. Equations (137.25)–(137.27) give, for every fixed M,
$$
 \sup_{|u|\le M,|y|\le R}
 \left|\frac{g_y^e(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}
                  {g_y(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}-1\right|\to0.
 \tag{139.37}
$$
The precision is relative o(1), stronger than a logarithmic error o(v). To check its applicability here, at the centered real saddle z(R), with R_z=(I-2zA)^-1, the exact cumulant difference is
$$
 \Delta K(z,r)=z\{-2r d^TR_z e_H+e_H^TR_z e_H\}.
 \tag{139.38}
$$
Since ||d||=O(sqrt(delta)), ||e_H||=O(delta^5), |r|<=M sqrt(eta/delta) and |z|<=C_M(eta+sqrt(delta))/delta, its modulus is bounded by
$$
 C_M\frac{\eta+\sqrt\delta}{\delta}
                       (\sqrt\eta\,\delta^5+\delta^{10})=o(1).
 \tag{139.39}
$$
Under that same real tilt, the energy means differ by O_M(sqrt(eta)delta^5+delta^10)=o(sqrt(delta)), and the scaled variances differ by o(1). The common Fourier block proves a local density ratio tending to one at that vanishing standardized displacement. This is the precise relative argument behind (139.37), including the rare denominator; it never divides an additive untilted error by a tiny density.

The two full bands lie in one fixed u compact. Multiplying their integrals, local test integrals and normalization by the ratio in (139.37) costs o(1), because their normalized W moments have just been bounded in Section 139.6. Outside these bands, the actual-e logarithmic gap and global envelope give (139.35) again. Their lower normalization follows from (139.37) on |w|<=1. Hence the actual-e Gaussian posterior obeys (139.5), with exactly the center (139.8). We do not need an e-derivative estimate or an assumed noncentral mode: an o(1) relative comparison on the whole moderate interval already proves that any physical shift at the local scale is negligible for this theorem.

In particular (139.37) at r and -r proves asymptotic relative reflection on the two bands. Together with their local normalization it gives both sign probabilities1/2+o(1). This supplies the sign assertion at absolute probability order, which a two-minimum large-deviation principle could not supply.

### 139.8 回到原始完整乘积计数

This step uses the actual same-output, same-low-tuple interface of Chapter 137, not an unconditioned supercritical Gaussian exponential moment. Write mathcal E_Q=P(Q)exp(-bQ^3). On the central high cells, retaining every low tuple with its exact probability, (137.30) gives
$$
 |D-D_G|\le\mathcal E_Q,\qquad
 |T-T_G|/\sigma\le\mathcal E_Q,
 \quad T_G=(E_H-V)/\sqrt\delta,
 \tag{139.40}
$$
and a multiplicative lifted-density error exp(O(mathcal E_Q)). The exact original full V,mu and likelihood appear here. Stirling remainders, binomial multiplicities, floors and low groups are included. The choice of l,zeta in Section 139.2 pays the positive exponent margins c_q/2-l and c_q-2zeta-l after division by sigma. No relation between eta and sigma is added.

Let pi_y^{lift} denote the normalized law with charge D_G on the lifted central cells and the excluded mass kept separately, and pi_y^G the actual-e Gaussian tilted law. The weighted comparison (137.31)–(137.34) implies for each fixed p
$$
 \|\pi_y^{\rm lift}-\pi_y^G\|_{1+|U_G|^p}
              \le e^{-b_pQ^3},\qquad U_G=\sqrt{\delta/\eta}D_G,
 \tag{139.41}
$$
uniformly in y eventually. Its absolute unnormalized error is sigma P_p(Q)exp(-bQ^3+C_pv), whereas its normalizing Gaussian numerator is at least c sigma. Since v=o(Q^(1/2)), the error is exponentially small in Q^3 after normalization. Ordinary denominators have the same factor sigma. This is a relative rare-output estimate, not a crude tail divided by a rare event.

The strict-exponent payment remains valid for the NEW observable W. On the lifted charge set, (139.34) gives
$$
 1+|W_G|^p\le C_p(1+t^p)(1+|U_G|^p),
 \quad W_G=2\sqrt\eta\{D_G-\operatorname{sign}(D_G)r_*\}.
 \tag{139.42}
$$
Eventually eta<=1 and t<=delta^-1/2, so its additional factor is a fixed power of Q, absorbed by the exponential accuracy in (139.41). The norm in (139.41) takes a supremum over all measurable tests bounded by its weight; it therefore permits this Q-dependent rescaling and sign map. It is a norm between LIFTED measures, not a discrete-versus-continuous total variation assertion.

For completeness the omitted extreme count cells receive a joint bound before normalization. Put d_noise=delta sigma^2. For every full count tuple,
$$
 D^2\le2n_gE+2(\sum_j e_j)^2,
$$
$$
 e^{aD^2-(E-h_y)^2/(2d_{\rm noise})}
 \le e^{2a(\sum e_j)^2+2an_gh_y+4a^2n_g^2d_{\rm noise}}
                   e^{-(E-h_y)^2/(4d_{\rm noise})}.
 \tag{139.43}
$$
The first exponent is O(Q^(7/2)); a stays bounded. The raw central-cell complement has binomial tail P(Q)exp(-cQ^4). Every fixed polynomial W weight costs at most exp(C_pQ^3) on the original finite count box; the center itself is only polynomial. Division by sigma costs L=O(Q^3). Hence the excluded weighted mass is at most exp(-c'Q^4). The Gaussian complement has the same payment with Gaussian raw moments and a reserved part of the likelihood. The central count/likelihood perturbation uses the joint charge/modal/likelihood insertion bound (137.28); its width-change derivative is the exact kernel derivative, retaining the explicit factor sigma. These are all estimates on the same tuple and observation, not products of separately realizable marginal estimates.

If D and D_G have the same sign, (139.40) gives
$$
 |W-W_G|\le2\sqrt\eta\,\mathcal E_Q\to0.
 \tag{139.44}
$$
A possible sign mismatch requires |D_G|<=mathcal E_Q. This region is outside the two fractional bands eventually. Equations (139.35),(139.41)--(139.43) show its probability and every fixed W-weighted mass tend to zero; a factor of order t^p for the possible sign jump is already included. The event D=0 receives the same bound. For each F in (139.5), truncate W,W_G to a fixed compact, apply uniform continuity there and (139.44), and then use a higher fixed moment to remove the truncation. Thus (139.5) holds for the original discrete full count law itself. No physical recentering of T,D or low-count environment has occurred.

All arguments above are deterministic on the common classes of Section 139.2. Their complements have probability tending to zero uniformly over deterministic supports, separately for the original pair and path laws. Exhaust those tight classes to obtain exactly the actual-data probability statement in Section 139.1. There is no new row-independence assumption, faster eta divergence, faster noise decay, or unproved uniformity beyond those common classes.

### 139.9 物理输出导致的局部中心位移

The finite center gives a useful explicit correction beyond a leading well location. Since z_* is independent of y, (139.8) yields EXACTLY
$$
 R_*(y)-R_*(0)=\frac{\sqrt\delta y}{\Psi'(z_*)}.
 \tag{139.45}
$$
Consequently, uniformly on each fixed output compact,
$$
 2\sqrt\eta\{r_*(y)-r_*(0)\}
       =\frac{2\sqrt{\eta\delta}\,y}
                {\Psi'(z_*)[r_*(y)+r_*(0)]}
       =\frac{y}{\sqrt{2C_2}}+o(1).
 \tag{139.46}
$$
This follows from (139.9),(139.12) only after sigma->0; the EXACT center in the primary theorem always retains finite sigma. If one instead centers the local fluctuation at r_*(0), its conditional Gaussian mean at sign s is s y/sqrt(2C_2)+o(1), with the same finite empirical C_2. Thus ignoring the physical output creates an order-one local correction even though it does not change Chapter 137's speed-level action. Formula (139.46) is a corollary, not a replacement definition of the center.

Similarly a leading center sqrt(eta/delta)m_Q alone is not justified by (139.12): relative eta and sigma^2 corrections can induce local shifts of orders t eta and t sigma^2, neither constrained to vanish here. We make no actual-model counterexample claim from these error budgets. The exact real system (139.8) and the proved mode displacement (139.23) remove this obligation without extra rates.

The new bridge is (139.20)--(139.22), the differentiated exact prefactor with its saddle cancellations, together with (139.26)--(139.36), the moving-scale local tails and correct t Jacobian payment. The local Gaussian coefficient2 follows from the independently computed curvature (139.24), retaining the finite noise until it cancels. The final original-count passage checks that the stronger W weights and possible sign mismatch are paid by the already proved exponential interface. This is more than (137.A)–(137.C) and does not differentiate their asymptotic errors.

The scope remains fixed tests and compact outputs, eta->0 with t->infinity, the original strict half-exponent noise condition, actual pair/path probability and support uniformity, and the auxiliary PRODUCT count law. We do not assert a full-q P theorem, Shannon or other entropy derivatives, exact finite-count symmetry, total variation to a continuous law, growing test degrees, all positive eta, a global phase diagram or formal-kernel verification. Classical conditional Gaussian, Fourier, saddlepoint and Laplace tools are not claimed as new.

## 140. 超多项式窄带宽中的精确格点局部化与原始方差熵

同一整数元组上的带标记比较先通过共同残差核取得不含逆噪声的全输出界，再对精确格点辅助律进行全频轴局部化。这两个比较使用不同范数，使计数近似中的多项式误差不再乘上指数增长的谐波体积。本章在原始完整选择后验中得到 $\rho_Q\asymp e^{-Q^{1/4}}$ 下的加权方差熵极限。

### 140.1 原始完整计数律与超多项式窄带宽

**定理 140.1（伸展指数带宽下的原始加权方差熵极限）。** Fix the original admissible amplitude, beta in(1/2,1), and all original legal deterministic floor/scale sequences. Put

$$
 R_Q=Q^{1/4},\quad \mathcal B=q/Q^{11/4},\quad
 \rho_Q=\sigma\mathcal B,\quad
 0<c_-\le\rho_Qe^{R_Q}\le c_+<\infty.                 \tag{140.1}
$$

Then, separately for the actual pair and path experiments, uniformly over deterministic true supports of size q,

$$
 \boxed{\int_{\mathbb R}f_x(y)|D_x(y)-R_*(y)|\,dy\to0}
                                                               \tag{140.2}
$$

in the original raw-data probability. The count prior remains the complete selected full-q prior, not a known-support posterior or a Gaussian whole-law replacement. Retain exactly138.1–4's tuple, scalar and finite quantities:

$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q/Q^{5/2},\quad
 T=\mathcal B^{-1}\sum_j(R_j-\mu_j)^2-V/\sqrt\delta,
 \quad Y=T+\sigma G,
$$
$$
 A=V_H/\sqrt\delta,\quad \nu_0=2\sum_{j\in H}w_j^2,
 \quad\kappa_3=8\sum_{j\in H}w_j^3,\quad\Lambda=\nu_0+\sigma^2,
$$
$$
 C_x=A^2\kappa_3/\Lambda^3-2A\nu_0/\Lambda^2,
 \quad D_x(y)=Vpost_x(y)-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xy,
$$
$$
 R_*(y)=29/6-3\sqrt2+(3\sqrt2+8/\sqrt3-9)y^2/\nu,
 \qquad\nu=2g_0.                                      \tag{140.3}
$$

Vprior is the exact centered-surprise variance of the complete count law. With the exact m_x=E_xY, the integrated statement is

$$
 \int Vpost_x(y)f_x(y)dy-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xm_x
                      \to8/\sqrt3-25/6.               \tag{140.4}
$$

G is the same independent standard Gaussian before conditioning in every comparison; its posterior dependence is retained. All original groups and multiplicities remain. The auxiliary resampling pool has fixed dimension; the actual group array grows as prescribed and the bulk threshold remains unchanged. No endpoint, necessity, zero-noise, sharp-threshold, computational-efficiency or stronger-bandwidth assertion is included. Chapters 136 and 138 keep their established scopes.

The bound in (124.26), $C(1+\rho^{-1})Q^{-428}$, does not vanish at this bandwidth. Equations (111.13)–(111.15) instead compare signed count moments on the same integer energy through a kernel whose $L^1$ norm is independent of noise. Section 140.6 then retains exponential errors for exact lattice localization, separately from the count approximation. Define the enlarged transition width and harmonic cutoff by

$$
L_Q=10R_Q+20\log Q,\qquad
N_Q=\left\lceil1000\rho_Q^{-1}\sqrt{R_Q+\log Q}\right\rceil.
\tag{140.5}
$$

The $R_Q$ term in both quantities pays the new exponential frequency volume. A cutoff with only $\sqrt{\log Q}$ would leave an insufficient Gaussian tail.

### 140.2 同一原始计数池与精确响应

The actual count bridge retains the following hypotheses. The original floors give

$$
 \log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),\quad q/M=e^{-\phi Q^3+O(1)},
 \quad c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta\in(0,\phi),              \tag{140.6}
$$

where phi=((1+r)/2)log(1+r)+((1-r)/2)log(1-r)>0. The exact row scores and compensated coprime relation are

$$
 a_s=\log{1+r\over1-\epsilon_M}>0,\quad
 b_s=\log{1-r\over1+\epsilon_M}<0,\quad
 \epsilon_M={rq\over M-q},\quad B_0={M-q\over q},
$$
$$
 \gcd(P,Q)=1,\quad1/10\le P/Q<1/8,\quad
 h_Q=Qa_s+Pb_s,\quad
 |h_Q|\le CQ(q/M+e^{-cQ^5}).                           \tag{140.7}
$$

All floors and this nonzero defect are retained. The row likelihood is exp(a_sk+b_sl); no exact rational relation between the scores is asserted.

For each deterministic true support choose two distinct true signal labels u,v in the same positive parity class by a fixed pre-data ordering. Reveal all parities, their departure-slot pool membership mask, all outside labels, and the final path label or all pair arrivals. Denote this sigma-field by F_0, its positive/negative pool totals by K_+,K_-, and the unrevealed splits assigned to u by k,l.

The actual path kernel is[1+b_S(x)chi(y)]/(2M). Conditional on the parity sequence its departure weights factor as1_{chi(x)=s_t}[1+b_S(x)s_(t+1)]/M; each class sum of b_S is zero, and the final label is uniform in its class. A same-class reassignment preserves the preceding transition's parity argument. For pairs the same factorization follows from the exact pair density. Since b_S(u)=b_S(v)=r, the conditional slot choices are jointly fair, giving exactly

$$
 (k,l)\mid F_0\sim Bin(K_+,1/2)\otimes Bin(K_-,1/2).   \tag{140.8}
$$

This is the original raw-label operation, not a likelihood intervention. Neither outside calibration nor central membership is held fixed by assumption when it actually varies. The outside data are fixed, while both varying rows and the full-q normalizer co-vary through the exact response.

Remove only u,v to define the auxiliary outside family, let n_0 be its central count, and choose an outside central anchor c by a fixed F_0-measurable order. Remove c also and calibrate the remaining Bernoulli family at integer mean q-1. Write its multiplier t_o, variance D_o, third cumulant kappa_3^o; x=t_oL_0, p=x/(1+x),v=p(1-p),a_3=kappa_3^o/D_o. The original all-array event implies, by removing three bounded Bernoulli terms and integrating d(mean)/d(log odds)=variance,

$$
 D_o\asymp q,\quad n_0\asymp q/Q^3,\quad
 |\log(t_oB_0)|\le2q^{-1/4},\quad x\in[1/3,3].          \tag{140.9}
$$

It has support-uniform failure bounded by the bounds (132.19)–(132.20)

$$
 b_{env}(Q)=C\{q^{-1/2}+\zeta_Q\sqrt q+M^{-8}q^{-3/2}
                   +Q^3/q+Q/M+M^{-9}\},\quad\zeta_Q=CQ^9/M=o(q^{-1/2}).
                                                               \tag{140.10}
$$

The observation in(140.9) is F_0-measurable and follows from that original event; no independence from the pool totals is required. Its failure is charged once. Conditional only on parity, the positive and negative total arrays are independent multinomials and K_+,K_- have binomial marginals with means2a_0Q^3+O(Q),2b_0Q^3+O(Q). Hence, except with probability Ce^-cQ,

$$
 |K_+-2a_0Q^3|+|K_--2b_0Q^3|\le CQ^2,\quad
 cQ^3\le K_+,K_-\le CQ^3.                              \tag{140.11}
$$

Put t=log t_o+(a_sK_++b_sK_-)/2. The original floors imply|t|<=CQ^2 here. On(140.9), |t|<2L_Q implies

$$
 |a_sK_++b_sK_--2\log B_0|<4L_Q+4q^{-1/4}.             \tag{140.12}
$$

Conditional only on parity and K_-, this contains O(1+L_Q) integer K_+ values. Its binomial maximal atom is CQ^-3/2. Crucially we have removed t_o from this necessary condition before applying the marginal law; we do not condition on all of F_0 and then invent a fresh law for K_+. The common F_0-measurable event G_Q given by(140.9–11) and2L_Q<=|t|<=CQ^2 therefore satisfies

$$
 \sup_S P_S(G_Q^c)\le b_{env}(Q)+C[e^{-cQ}+Q^{-3/2}(1+L_Q)].
                                                               \tag{140.13}
$$

Since L_Q=O(Q^(1/4)+log Q), this is o(1), with no growing number of proof labels.

The exact full-q anchor probability, with E_s the outside elementary-symmetric coefficients and c_0=1,c_1=L_u+L_v,c_2=L_uL_v, is

$$
 p_*={L_0\sum_{h=0}^2c_hE_{q-1-h}\over
                  \sum_{h=0}^2c_h(E_{q-h}+L_0E_{q-1-h})}.
                                                               \tag{140.14}
$$

At the SAME outside calibration let

$$
 X=a_s(k-K_+/2)+b_s(l-K_-/2),\quad
 f_t(X)={\sinh t\over\cosh t+\cosh X},\quad
 p_{ref}=p+{v(a_3-1)\over2D_o}.
$$

Chapter 132's uniform local Bernoulli ratio at offsets s in[-2,1] is1-(s^2+a_3s)/(2D_o)+O(D_o^-2). Average against the common auxiliary anchor Z and pair occupancy U, with s=1-Z-U. The polynomial's difference at Z=1 versus0 is2U-1-a_3, whose mean is2f_t(X)+1-a_3. Its covariance with Z is v times that mean. Dividing the positive common normalizer gives the uniform exact response estimate

$$
 p_*=p_{ref}-{v\over D_o}f_t(X)+O(q^{-2}).              \tag{140.15}
$$

This uses fixed offsets only, not a growing-order or growing-deletion expansion. It is uniform over positive pair odds. It also ensures full-array recalibration within C/q throughout the fiber. Every central membership is retained:

$$
 C_0\in\{n_0,n_0+1,n_0+2\},\quad\mu_0=C_0p_*,\quad
 d_0\asymp C_0\asymp q/Q^3.                            \tag{140.16}
$$

The exact center identity is exchangeability of central equal-likelihood labels under the full-q law. The anchor was removed only in the auxiliary coefficient family. No varying label is assumed to lie on the selected line.

### 140.3 扩大过渡窗后的共同有理水平

The same lawful two-sign projection is

$$
 H=Ql-Pk\in\mathbb Z,\quad H^0=(QK_--PK_+)/2,
 \quad\bar X=(b_s/Q)(H-H^0),\quad
 X=\bar X+(h_Q/Q)(k-K_+/2).                            \tag{140.17}

Under(140.8), Ql-Pk=h fixes one k residue modulo Q. Finite cyclic inversion gives P(k equivalent a mod Q)<=Q^-1(1+Ce^-cQ), and the negative split's maximal atom is CQ^-3/2. Summing all preimages yields

$$
 \sup_hP(H=h\mid F_0)\le CQ^{-5/2}\quad\hbox{on }G_Q.   \tag{140.18}

This is not a law for an independent empirical phase. Choose a fixed large D_w. The joint split window of radius W=D_wQ^(3/2)sqrt(log Q) has conditional failure at most4Q^-204 and implies

$$
 |H-H^0|\le CQ^{5/2}\sqrt{\log Q},\quad|\bar X|\le CQ^2,

$$
 \delta_X=CQ^{3/2}\sqrt{\log Q}(q/M+e^{-cQ^5}).          \tag{140.19}
$$

All hidden preimages are included. Since|f'_t|<=1/4, this discrepancy changes f by at most delta_X/4.

Remove the two projected transition bands||bar X|-|t||<L_Q. Their total number of integer H sites is at most C Q(1+L_Q), because the score step|b_s|/Q is between fixed multiples of Q^-1. Equation(140.18) pays CQ^-3/2(1+L_Q) ONCE. We subsequently estimate under the original conditional law; avoidance of this event does not create a new product law.

For T>=2L, the elementary exact inequalities

$$
 |X|\le T-L\Rightarrow |f_T(X)-1|\le4e^{-L},\quad
 |X|\ge T+L\Rightarrow |f_T(X)|\le e^{-L}               \tag{140.20}
$$

follow from f_T=sinh T/(cosh T+cosh X). Use f_t=-f_|t| for t<0. On the retained window, (140.15) thus puts the SAME posterior scalar in the F_0-measurable union

$$
 p_*\in\bigcup_{z=-1}^1[p_z-r_Q,p_z+r_Q],\quad
 p_z=p_{ref}-vz/D_o,\quad
 r_Q={C\over q}(e^{-L_Q}+\delta_X+q^{-1}).              \tag{140.21}
$$

The realized plateau and membership may depend on the same allocations; all nine combinations are retained.

Use the original bulk J={j:d_j>=Q^3600}, containing group0 throughout this fiber. Its actual half-integer dual energy is

$$
 E^{min}_{\ell,x}=4\pi^2\sum_{j\in J}d_j
           \operatorname{dist}(\ell(1/2-\mu_j),\mathbb Z)^2.
                                                               \tag{140.22}
$$

If E_min(ell)<=Q^2 with1<=ell<=N_Q, the central term gives an integer h and actual C in{n_0,n_0+1,n_0+2} such that

$$
 |\ell(1/2-Cp_*)-h|\le\tau_C:=C_1Q/\sqrt C.           \tag{140.23}
$$

For each(C,z), h/ell then belongs to the interval centered at1/2-Cp_z of radius Cr_Q+tau_C. Distinct rational VALUES with denominators at most N_Q differ by at least N_Q^-2, since their cross-product numerator is a nonzero integer. Large or negative numerators cause no change. At the NEW cutoff,

$$
 N_Q^2\le C e^{2R_Q}(R_Q+\log Q),
$$
$$
 2N_Q^2\max_C(Cr_Q+\tau_C)
 \le C(R_Q+\log Q)\{Q^{-23}e^{-8R_Q}
   +e^{2R_Q}[Q^{-3}\delta_X+Q^{-3}/q+Q^{5/2}/\sqrt q]\}
                         \longrightarrow0.            \tag{140.24}
$$

The exponential q and compensated-score bounds(140.6–7) pay every term. In particular the original full-q O(q^-2) and hidden-fiber errors remain adequate; they were not discarded before comparing the enlarged band.

Eventually each of the nine intervals contains at most one rational value r_(C,z) with denominator at most N_Q. This value is F_0-measurable. All nonreduced representations h/ell remain included. They impose the SAME necessary condition|p_*-(1/2-r_(C,z))/C|<=tau_C/C, using ell>=1. Therefore(140.15),(140.19) imply

$$
 |f_t(\bar X)-c_{C,z}|\le\varepsilon_Q,
 \quad c_{C,z}={D_o\over v}\left(p_{ref}-{1/2-r_{C,z}\over C}\right),
$$
$$
 \varepsilon_Q=CQ^{11/2}/\sqrt q+C/q+C\delta_X
         \le e^{-c_qQ^3/2+O(\log Q)}.                  \tag{140.25}
$$

There is NO e^-L_Q plateau error in this thin-strip tolerance. That coarser error located the common rational; the exact response now determines its exponentially narrow preimage. No independent Diophantine premise is used.

On the three retained real intervals, the exact second derivative

$$
 f_t''(X)={\sinh t(\cosh^2X-\cosh t\cosh X-2)
                         \over(\cosh t+\cosh X)^3}     \tag{140.26}
$$

has one nonzero sign. Its inflections have absolute value between|t| and|t|+log6, so L_Q excludes them by more than1. Factoring the numerator quadratic in cosh X, using|t|,|bar X|<=CQ^2 and the score step b_s/Q, gives|partial_H^2 f_t(bar X)|>=cQ^-2e^-CQ^2=:kappa_Q. Thus4epsilon_Q<kappa_Q eventually.

A strongly convex or concave function with curvature magnitude at least kappa has at most two integer points in|F-c|<=epsilon when4epsilon<kappa. Three ordered integers would give, by the strong secant inequality, a middle value at most c+epsilon-kappa/2<c-epsilon in the convex case; negate F for concavity. This also covers the thin neighborhood, not only the exact level. Applied on the three intervals it leaves at most six H values per candidate. Equation(140.18) counts every hidden preimage of each H. Union over nine candidates, not N_Q harmonics, yields the NEW actual arithmetic theorem

$$
 \boxed{\sup_S P_S\{\exists1\le|\ell|\le N_Q:
                 E^{min}_{\ell,x}\le Q^2\}
 \le b_{env}(Q)+C[e^{-cQ}+Q^{-3/2}(1+L_Q)+Q^{-5/2}]
                         +4Q^{-204}\longrightarrow0.} \tag{140.27}
$$

Negative harmonics have the same energy. The new window payment is O(Q^-5/4+Q^-3/2 log Q), not a hidden constant. The common environment, pool law, full-q offset, all memberships and candidate levels concern one actual realization in each experiment. This arithmetic theorem alone is not the full conclusion; the following return is essential.

### 140.4 不含逆噪声的带标记计数回接

Keep J={j:d_j>=Q^3600} and E={j notin J:C_j>0}. The occupancy result (111.7) gives|J|=O(Q^2), |E|=O(1), H subset J and p_j in[1/4,3/4] on the original good events. No threshold increases with Q beyond this already fixed power. All E groups retain their original binomial factors, surprise, energy and physical centers.

Let Q_x be the calibrated binomial product. On J use the normalized lattice Gaussian g_j(k) proportional to exp[-(k-m_j)^2/(2d_j)], m_j=C_jp_j, d_j=C_jp_j(1-p_j); on E keep the exact binomial. This comparison Q_x^lat lives on the SAME integer tuple space, with zero-extension of binomial signed measures. Each side uses its exact coordinate-centered surprise. Equation (111.10) proves, for each fixed h<=4, full absolute signed-mass difference at most C_hd_j^-1/8; it follows from uniform Stirling on|k-m|<=d^(5/8), fixed-degree tails and exact centering. For h<=2 let eta_h(k)=Q_x(k)s_Q(k)^h and eta_h^lat(k)=Q_x^lat(k)s_lat(k)^h. Expand the sums of coordinate-centered surprises and telescope the products. There are at most CQ^4 mark terms and CQ^2 replacements; all remaining fixed marked factors have bounded total variation. Thus

 \max_{h\le2}\|\eta_h-\eta_h^{lat}\|_{TV}\le CQ^{-444},

where TV is full absolute mass. This is a signed-mark theorem, not scalar TV promoted to unbounded moments.

For every sigma>0 the common SAME-residual kernel is

$$
 K_r(k,y)=((y-T(k))/\sigma)^{2r}\varphi_\sigma(y-T(k)),

It is nonnegative and has the displayed noise-independent signed L1 operator norm. Expanding W=s+G^2/2 gives, with q_h(y)dy=E[W^h;Y in dy],

$$
 q_h^Q-q_h^{lat}=\sum_{r=0}^h{h\choose r}2^{-r}
                    K_r(\eta_{h-r}-\eta_{h-r}^{lat}),
 \quad\max_{h\le2}\|q_h^Q-q_h^{lat}\|_1\le CQ^{-444}.  \tag{140.29}
$$

The scalar T(k) and its original mu,V are exactly the same. A continuous tuple replacement changing T would not have this contraction. No 1/sigma, 1/rho, density division or frequency cutoff occurs.

For the complete conditional variance density q_2-q_1^2/q_0, clip the variational expression q_1^2/q_0=sup_z(2zq_1-z^2q_0) at|z|<=b. The difference is bounded in L1 by epsilon_2+2b epsilon_1+b^2 epsilon_0+(E|W|^4+E|W_lat|^4)/b^2. Both fourth target moments are CQ^4. At b=Q^10 this costs O(Q^-16)+O(Q^-424). Exact prior-variance difference is O(Q^-448). The exact Vprior=O(Q^2) mass payment and original A^2/Lambda=O(Q^(1/2)), C_x=O(Q^(1/4)) payments vanish. Bounded fourth output moments give weighted mass convergence through Cauchy–Schwarz, still independently of lower noise.

The original selected/full-q law is returned by(101.9), (101.15) and (111.16)–(111.17):0<=dP_x/dQ_x<=C and a_x=||dP_x/dQ_x-1||_2=O_P(Q^-5/2). Its SAME-channel centered variance-density difference, including the log-density surprise term, costs Ca_xQ^2=o_P(1); weighted output mass costs Ca_x. This proof precedes noise and does not divide by sigma. Consequently at(140.1),

$$
 \|f_xD_x-f_{lat}D_{lat}\|_1=o_P(1),\qquad
 \int(1+y^2)|f_x-f_{lat}|dy=o_P(1).                    \tag{140.30}
$$

D_lat subtracts its own exact prior variance and adds the ORIGINAL finite A^2/Lambda-C_xy. We do not claim decay of the old count/lattice Fourier-L1 bound here; it is bypassed by the stronger all-output signed-kernel relation actually needed for the return.

### 140.5 精确实温度格点模态

All statements below hold on a fixed localization of the original regularity constants. They are uniform in the support and actual centers; constants may depend on that localization and the fixed model parameters. The localization can be released after Q tends to infinity. Define

$$
 w_j=d_j/\mathcal B,\quad a_j=(\mu_j-m_j)/\sqrt{d_j},
 \quad\epsilon=\max_{j\in J}w_j\asymp Q^{-1/4},
$$
$$
 P(s)=\prod_{j\in J}(1-2isw_j)^{-1/2},\quad
 |P(s)|\le(1+c\epsilon^2s^2)^{-c'/\epsilon^2}.          \tag{140.31}
$$

At least c epsilon^-2 central coordinates have w_j between c epsilon and epsilon. Every fixed Fourier moment of|P| is bounded; beyond c/epsilon its tail with any fixed polynomial is at most a polynomial in Q times exp(-c sqrt Q). Also||wa||=O(Q^-5/2), so on|s|<=C/epsilon the noncentral translation s wa is O(Q^-9/4). These are same-array facts, unchanged by the proof labels.

Tilt the SAME joint prior by exp(uW), W=s_lat+G^2/2, and normalize for real u near0. Keep the original physical y,T,mu and intercept fixed. Write tau=1-u. The bulk factors are proportional to exp[-tau(k-m_j)^2/(2d_j)], E has its exact normalized surprise tilt, and G has variance1/tau. Centering constants cancel within the normalized tilt; none changes physical y. Let f_lat,u be this output density and g_u its continuous-J Gaussian reference with the SAME E factors, centers, intercept and residual.

The real positive lattice normalization is

$$
 c_{lat}(u)=\prod_{j\in J}{\sqrt{2\pi d_j/\tau}\over
                  \sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}e^{-\tau(n-m_j)^2/(2d_j)}}.
$$

Real Poisson summation gives, directly through two derivatives,

$$
 |c_{lat}(0)-1|+|c'_{lat}(0)|+|c''_{lat}(0)|
                           \le C Q^4e^{-cQ^{3600}}.    \tag{140.32}
$$

For each coordinate the differentiated nonzero-dual terms are polynomials of fixed degree in d_j times exp(-c d_j); absorb these polynomials into half the exponential, then multiply over O(Q^2) factors. No d_max factor or unproved complex zero-free region is needed. This explicit exponential bound, rather than the notation 'smaller than any fixed power', will be used when summing periods.

At t_ell=pi ell mathcal B and t=t_ell+s, retain exactly

$$
 \xi_{\ell k,j}=\sqrt{d_j}[\pi\ell(1-2\mu_j)-2\pi k_j],
 \quad E_{\ell k}=\sum_J\xi_{\ell k,j}^2,\quad
 \eta_\ell=\pi\ell\rho_Q,
$$
$$
 z_{\ell k}=e^{i\pi\ell(\sum_{all}\mu_j^2-B^2V)}
                e^{i\sum_J[\pi\ell(1-2\mu_j)-2\pi k_j]m_j},
$$
$$
 H_{E,\ell}(u,s)=E_{E,u}\exp\{i\sum_E\pi\ell(1-2\mu_j)R_j
                         +is\mathcal B^{-1}\sum_E(R_j-\mu_j)^2\}.
$$

The first two u derivatives of H_E retain its centered first/two surprise marks JOINTLY with the energy, and are bounded by a fixed constant. Completion of the same Gaussian squares gives the EXACT finite-array identity

$$
 \Psi_{\ell k}(u,s)=c_{lat}(u)z_{\ell k}
 e^{is(\sum_Jw_ja_j^2-V/\sqrt\delta)}
 \prod_J\left({\tau\over\tau-2isw_j}\right)^{1/2}
$$
$$
 \quad\times\exp\left[-\frac12\sum_J
 { (\xi_{\ell k,j}-2sw_ja_j)^2\over\tau-2isw_j}
               -{(\eta_\ell+\sigma s)^2\over2\tau}\right]
 H_{E,\ell}(u,s).                                     \tag{140.33}
$$

The inverse Fourier phase is exp[-i(t_ell+s)y]. It does not vary with u. Both signs in1-2mu and every outside term remain. In particular the residual is eta_ell+sigma s, not eta_ell followed by a different independent noise graph. The ell=k=0 integrand is EXACTLY c_lat(u) times the characteristic function of g_u. No approximate Gaussian leading term is substituted for that zero mode.

Differentiate(140.33) separately at u=0 for j=0,1,2. On|s|<=1/(8epsilon), Re(1-2isw_j)^-1>=16/17; also||xi-2swa||^2>=E/2-4s^2||wa||^2 and(eta+sigma s)^2>=eta^2/2-sigma^2s^2. Product-rule determinant losses are at most CQ^4; exponent derivatives have a fixed polynomial degree in E+eta^2. Including E marks and(140.32), a convenient uniform majorant is

The SAME residual derivatives are exactly the normalized h2/h4 polynomials; differentiating exp[-eta^2/(2tau)] at0 gives(-eta^2/2)e^-eta²/2 and(eta^4/4-eta^2)e^-eta²/2, with eta replaced by eta+sigma s in the actual formula. ### 140.6 无多项式体积误差的全频轴接口

therefore controls the complete quotient below. It does not require every coordinate or every alias independently large. We use the stronger actual event(140.27) only to verify this integrated condition here.

**Off the wide half-integer strips.** The uniform quadratic-Gauss calculation in (109.8)–(109.14) supplies a fixed contraction r_0<1 for each unmarked central factor outside dist(theta,(1/2)Z)<=R_0/D, with theta=t/(2pi mathcal B), D comparable q/Q^3 and fixed R_0. $$

To pass to NORMALIZED tilt derivatives use the exact formulas f'_0=q_1-(1/2)q_0 and f''_0=q_2-q_1-(V_lat+1/4)q_0. They follow because E W=1/2 and E W²=V_lat+3/4; V_lat=O(Q²). There is no separate O(Q^-430) approximation in this argument: all factors at this step are already exact lattice Gaussian or exact retained E factors. The count replacement was completed in L1 by(140.29).

**Annular part of each wide strip.** Choose a smooth cutoff chi(s), independent of u, supported on|s|<=1/(8epsilon) and equal to1 on|s|<=1/(16epsilon). The original wide strip has|s|<=C_0/epsilon for a fixed C_0. On the intervening annulus the exact Poisson identity(140.33) still holds. Re(1-2isw_j)^-1 has a positive lower bound depending only on C_0. The same two differentiations give CQ8 times a fixed polynomial in E+eta² times exp[-c(E+eta²)]|P(s)|, with different fixed c. The shifts s wa and sigma s remain small. Polynomial absorption and the nearest-dual-grid sum bound the total over k by CQ8e^-c eta²|P(s)|. Equation(140.31) makes the annular integral polynomial in Q times exp(-c sqrt Q). Summing ell costs C(1+rho^-1). This is the second exponential term on the whole line, not deletion of a frequency annulus without payment. The fixed finite polynomial powers are absorbed in Q10 or by decreasing c. No u derivative hits chi, because physical s and the cutoff are fixed.

**The inner strips.** Integrate(140.34). To sum all dual vectors, absorb its polynomial into a portion of the exponential and extract exp[-(E_min+eta²)/512]. For each coordinate, a Gaussian sum over the grid of spacing2pi sqrt(d_j), with arbitrary translate, is at most1+C exp(-c'd_j) after sufficient exponent slack. Its normalization error and its first two derivatives cost CQ8 exp(-cQ3600) by(140.32), since the reference transforms and their two derivatives have bounded polynomial Fourier moments. Neither cost is multiplied by an uncontrolled number of harmonics: it is one zero mode. Allowing the larger(1+rho^-1) factor on these exponential errors gives the stated convenient bound.

All four pieces prove(140.35). This proof did not import124.26's weakened polynomial error. Its only lattice localization costs are displayed exponentials. Use the established moderate interval|y|<=h_out=sqrt(100nu log Q). The same continuous-bulk reference lower bound g_0(y)>=cQ^-60 and normalized derivative bounds|g_1|+|g_2|<=CQ4 remain valid.
