This is the original coefficient interface (68.33), (68.38), and (70.6), used in Chapter 143. Outside labels supply q-k. The selected charge is not set to zero. The full-box support follows on the common data classes from N_J=sum_j C_j<q<M-N_J and 0<p_i<1. Cancelling mu_j in BD does not change its appearance in E or T.

Put d_c=sum_{i notin J}p_i(1-p_i), d_J=B^2 V, d_all=d_c+d_J and epsilon=B^2/(2d_c). Chapter 143's variance-based local Bernoulli estimate gives on the ENTIRE box
$$
 L_x(k)=\exp\{\tfrac12\log(d_{\rm all}/d_c)-\varepsilon D^2\}
                  +O(q^{-1/2}),\quad \varepsilon=O(\delta^5),
$$
$$
 0\le L_x(k)\le1+C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}),\quad
 |L_x(k)-1|\le C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\varepsilon D^2).
 \tag{146.11}
$$
Its hypotheses d_c,d_all comparable to q and d_J=O(B^2) hold on the same actual-data classes. The normalization in(146.10) is retained. We use(146.11) only after establishing the new region-conditioned charge moments.

The common data classes have c<=V,C2<=C, v_*<=C delta, n_g<=C delta^-4, p_j in[1/4,3/4], sum C_j<=CB^2, and a block of at least c/delta variances in[c delta,C delta]. They also have
$$
 |e_j|\le C\delta^5\sqrt{v_j},\qquad
 \|e\|^2\le C\delta^{10},\qquad
 (\sum_j|e_j|)^2\le C\delta^6.
 \tag{146.12}
$$
Choose l,zeta with eventually log(1/sigma)<=lQ^3, l<c_q/2, 0<zeta<c_q/2 and 2zeta<c_q-l. The high block H={j:C_j>=exp(zeta Q^3)} is fixed once on the whole parameter domain. Every low tuple remains in the exact count sum; H is only an analytic device. High/full variance differences are a fixed polynomial in Q times exp(-bQ^3), b>0. Below o_exp has this meaning. A fixed power of eta^-1 or h^-1 is only a polynomial cost, since eta>=sqrt(delta) eventually.

The precise reusable analytic inputs are Chapter 137's exact conditional Gaussian transform, global density/score estimates and relative noncentral comparison, Chapter 139's first two derivatives of its exact saddle prefactor, and Chapter 144's anchored finite-noise curvature and growing-field count-cell geometry. Their prior theorems outside this window are not being applied to the new conclusion. In particular, Chapter 144's fixed-gap endpoint envelope is not available here. Sections 146.3–146.8 prove the missing derivative, both competing normalizations and the region-relative return.

### 146.3 有限噪声剖面及 Fourier 前因子的三阶导数

Let Y_j be independent centered Gaussians of variances v_j for j in H. Write D_G=sum_H Y_j, V_H=sum_H v_j, C_H=diag(v_j), b=(v_j)_{j in H}, d=b/V_H and A_0=C_H-bb^T/V_H. Conditional on D_G=r, the centered vector has mean rd and covariance A_0. Use a separate independent Gaussian energy noise of variance delta sigma^2 and the FULL physical value H_y=V+sqrt(delta)y. Set
$$
 \mathcal K_0(z)=-\tfrac12\log\det(I-2zA_0)+\tfrac12\delta\sigma^2z^2,
 \quad \Psi(z)=z d^T(I-2zA_0)^{-1}d,
$$
$$
 \mathcal K(z,R_0)=\mathcal K_0(z)+R_0\Psi(z),\qquad
 \gamma=\eta-\{(2V_H)^{-1}-(2V)^{-1}\}.
 \tag{146.13}
$$
R_0 denotes squared charge, not the output cutoff. Let f_r^0(H_y) be the exact density of sum_H Y_j^2 plus this noise, conditional on D_G=r. Then the finite profile used here is exactly
$$
 g_y^0(r)=e^{\gamma r^2}f_r^0(H_y),\qquad
 \ell_y(R_0)=\log g_y^0(\sqrt{R_0}).
 \tag{146.14}
$$
The full V, the high covariance defect, finite positive sigma and the original output are all retained. The centering e=0 is confined to this comparator; it will not replace the original count calibration.

For 0<=R_0<=M^2 eta/delta, each fixed M, let z=z(R_0) solve the exact real equation mathcal K_z=H_y. Strict convexity and positive noise give existence and uniqueness; the small real bracket gives |z|delta<=C_M(eta+sqrt(delta)). Put W=mathcal K_zz. The spectral block gives W comparable to delta, and on the entire vertical line through z,
$$
 |\Psi^{(j)}|\le C_j\delta^j\quad(j\ge1),\qquad
 |\mathcal K^{(j)}|\le C_{j,M}\delta^{j-1}\quad(j\ge2).
 \tag{146.15}
$$
Only fixed derivatives through five are needed. These follow by resolving A_0 eigenvalue by eigenvalue, with operator norm O(delta), ||d||^2=O(delta), and |R_0|=O(eta/delta). The noise contributes delta sigma^2 only to the second derivative. For vertical arguments, |1-2(z+i omega)a_j|>=1-2za_j, so the same resolvent bounds hold. No inverse sigma occurs.

Write z_1,z_2,z_3 for actual R_0 derivatives. The saddle equation gives
$$
 z_1=-\Psi'/W=O(1),\quad
 Wz_2+\mathcal K_{zzz}z_1^2+2\Psi''z_1=0,
 \quad z_2=O(\delta),
$$
$$
 Wz_3+3\mathcal K_{zzz}z_1z_2+\mathcal K_{zzzz}z_1^3
       +3\Psi''z_2+3\Psi'''z_1^2=0,
 \quad z_3=O(\delta^2).
 \tag{146.16}
$$
This last identity is new at the needed precision. It is obtained by differentiating the exact saddle equation, not an asymptotic approximation.

Let
$$
 \mathcal H(R_0)=\gamma R_0+\mathcal K(z(R_0),R_0)-z(R_0)H_y,
$$
$$
 L(R_0,\xi)=\mathcal K(z+i\xi/\sqrt\delta,R_0)
                  -\mathcal K(z,R_0)-i\xi H_y/\sqrt\delta,
 \quad p_y(R_0)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^L\,d\xi.
 \tag{146.17}
$$
The exact density formula is g_y^0(r)=delta^-1/2 exp(mathcal H(r^2))p_y(r^2). Section 139.4 establishes p bounded above and below by positive constants and
$$
 |e^L|\le(1+c\delta\xi^2)^{-c'/\delta},\qquad
 |L_{R_0}|\le C_M\delta\xi^2,\quad
 |L_{R_0R_0}|\le C_M\delta^2\xi^2.
 \tag{146.18}
$$
The envelope is integrable against every fixed xi power uniformly at sufficiently small delta. The lower bound for p is the local Fourier limit at the real tilted mean, with W/delta bounded above and below, and applies also at R_0=0 and slightly positive real saddles.

To extend the genuine parameter derivative by one order, write Delta f=f(z+i omega)-f(z), omega=xi/sqrt(delta), with R_0 fixed in each such difference. Direct differentiation of the exact expressions in Section 139.4 gives
$$
 L_{R_0R_0R_0}=
 3z_2\Delta\Psi'+3z_1^2\Delta\Psi''
 +3z_1z_2\Delta\mathcal K_{zz}
 +z_1^3\Delta\mathcal K_{zzz}+z_3\Delta\mathcal K_z.
 \tag{146.19}
$$
Its constant frequency term is zero. Its linear term is exactly the left side of the last saddle identity in(146.16), so is also zero. Using(146.15)--(146.16), the second frequency derivative of this expression is bounded by C_M delta^4 along the WHOLE vertical segment. For example the five coefficients cost respectively z_2 Psi''', z_1^2 Psi'''', z_1z_2 mathcal K_zzzz, z_1^3 mathcal K_zzzzz, and z_3 mathcal K_zzz, all O(delta^4). Taylor's formula along that segment therefore yields
$$
 |L_{R_0R_0R_0}|\le C_M\delta^3\xi^2.
 \tag{146.20}
$$
Now (exp L)'''=(L'''+3L'L''+(L')^3)exp L. The common envelope in(146.18) justifies differentiating the integral on a neighborhood of every R_0 and gives p'''=O(delta^3). Together with the positive lower bound and Section 139.4's p'=O(delta), p''=O(delta^2), this gives
$$
 (\log p_y)'''=O_M(\delta^3).
 \tag{146.21}
$$
At R_0=0 the bounds give the required right derivatives by dominated convergence on the nonnegative interval; no negative squared charge is used.

Since mathcal H'=gamma+Psi(z), mathcal H''=-Psi'(z)^2/W and mathcal H'''=O(delta^2), we have ell'''=O(delta^2). The already exact first/second derivative estimates from Section 144.4, now supplemented by this third derivative, are
$$
 \ell'(0)=\eta+O_R(\sqrt\delta+\delta)+o_{\exp}(1),
$$
$$
 \ell''(R_0)=-\frac\delta{m^2}
     \frac{2C_2}{2C_2+\sigma^2}
        \{1+O_M(\eta+\sqrt\delta)\}
          +O_M(\delta^2)+o_{\exp}(1),
 \quad |\ell'''(R_0)|\le C_M\delta^2.
 \tag{146.22}
$$
In particular all finite-noise effects remain inside ell before any field is chosen. No formal derivative of an o(1) remainder has been taken.

### 146.4 内部驻点支、竞争坐标与可测外场

Put G(r)=ell(r^2). Integrating(146.22) and using sqrt(delta)/eta=1/t gives, uniformly on fixed w-compacts,
$$
 \frac{F(r_{\rm sc}w;\kappa h_{\rm sc},y)}{m^2v}
      \longrightarrow f_\kappa(w)=w^2-\tfrac12w^4-\kappa w
 \quad\hbox{in }C^2_w.
 \tag{146.23}
$$
This is used for geometry and action gaps, not to locate the narrow window. The exact finite profile remains in(146.5)--(146.6). Convergence follows from sigma->0, eta->0, 1/t->0 and delta/eta->0, without comparing their rates. Also
$$
 G'''(r)=12r\ell''(r^2)+8r^3\ell'''(r^2)
      =O_M(\sqrt{\delta\eta})
 \tag{146.24}
$$
for r in a fixed scaled neighborhood of w_0 r_sc.

For the limiting quartic, stationarity is kappa=2w(1-w^2), the larger positive stationary point is a maximum, and its value is w^2(3w^2/2-1). At w=w_0 its value is zero, kappa=kappa_c and f''=-2. Choose once sufficiently small positive epsilon and rho so that for |kappa-kappa_c|<=epsilon the larger root lies inside (w_0-rho,w_0+rho), its second derivative is at most a negative constant throughout that interval, and the first derivatives at its endpoints have opposite signs. This entire interval lies above1/sqrt3. The choices depend only on fixed class bounds, not Q,y.

Equation(146.23) implies the same derivative signs and strict concavity for F there eventually. Hence there is exactly one stationary point r_-(h,y) in that specified interval, it is a maximum, and K is comparable to eta. This constructs the branch without assuming mode existence. Its uniform limit is the larger quartic root w_+(kappa). Smooth implicit dependence on h and continuity in y and the finite coefficients give measurable functions; the discrete choice of H is itself measurable.

The exact branch identities are
$$
 (r_-)_h=-1/K,\qquad A_h=-r_-,\qquad
 K_h=G'''(r_-)/K.
 \tag{146.25}
$$
Thus
$$
 \Lambda_h=-r_-+1/h-G'''(r_-)/(2K^2)
          =-r_-\{1+O(v^{-1})\}<0.
 \tag{146.26}
$$
Indeed h r_- is comparable to v, and the last correction divided by r_- is O(delta/eta^2)=O(v^-1), using(146.24). The constants are uniform on the branch. These are exact derivatives of the profile, not derivatives of(146.23).

At kappa_c-epsilon and kappa_c+epsilon, respectively, A has signs positive and negative with magnitude at least c v by(146.23). Meanwhile
$$
 \log[h\sqrt{2\pi/K}]=\log t+O(1)=o(v)
 \tag{146.27}
$$
throughout the branch. Since A_h<0 and Lambda_h<0, each of A=0 and Lambda=lambda has exactly one root in this field interval, for every bounded lambda. Uniform existence follows from the same endpoint signs. The roots converge to kappa_c, and(146.23) then gives r_-/r_sc->w_0 and K/(2eta)->1. Unique roots of continuous strictly monotone functions are measurable; no post-observation independence is needed. This proves the field construction in Section 146.1.

### 146.5 同一精确剖面的边界和内部相对积分

All estimates in this section hold simultaneously for |Lambda|<=L, |y|<=R and xi in a fixed compact [xi_0,xi_1] contained in(0,w_0). These parameter sets contain the chosen fields h_Q(lambda,y). Write r_-=r_-(h,y), A=F(r_-), K=K(h,y). At those fields the exact definition gives
$$
 e^A\sqrt{2\pi/K}=e^\Lambda/h,\qquad A=-\log t+O(1).
 \tag{146.28}
$$
Define the profile integrals
$$
 J_B=\int_0^{\xi r_{\rm sc}}e^{F(r)}dr,\qquad
 J_I=\int_{\xi r_{\rm sc}}^\infty e^{F(r)}dr.
 \tag{146.29}
$$
We prove BOTH relative asymptotics
$$
 J_B=h^{-1}(1+o(1)),\qquad
 J_I=e^A\sqrt{2\pi/K}(1+o(1)),
 \tag{146.30}
$$
with common uniform remainders, and their polynomially weighted versions.

For the boundary set x=hr. The exact anchored bound following from(146.22) is
$$
 |G(r)-G(0)|\le C_M\{(\eta+\sqrt\delta+\delta)r^2+\delta r^4\}
                      +o_{\exp}(1)(r^2+r^4).
 \tag{146.31}
$$
Since h=kappa m eta^(3/2)/sqrt(delta) with kappa bounded above and below,
$$
 \eta/h^2=O(t^{-2}),\quad \sqrt\delta/h^2=O(t^{-3}),
 \quad\delta/h^4=O(t^{-6}),
 \tag{146.32}
$$
so F(x/h)=-x+o(1) uniformly for bounded x. This applies whether h tends to zero, a finite value or infinity.

Choose a small fixed d_0>0 below xi_0. The anchored upper bound G(r)-G(0)<=C eta r^2 on 0<=r<=d_0 r_sc, together with h r_sc comparable to eta r_sc^2, makes F(r)<=-c h r there if d_0 is small enough. On d_0<=r/r_sc<=xi_1 the limiting critical quartic is strictly negative: its only zero maxima on w>=0 are0 and w_0. Equation(146.23), and kappa->kappa_c on |Lambda|<=L, give F(r)<=-c_0 v on that whole middle interval. After the change x=hr its length is O(v), and x^p costs only O(v^p). Thus its contribution relative to 1/h, with any fixed x polynomial, is at most C_p v^(p+1)e^-c_0v, which tends to zero however slowly v diverges. Local uniform convergence and the near-zero exponential envelope prove
$$
 h\int_0^{\xi r_{\rm sc}} f(hr)e^{F(r)}dr
       \longrightarrow\int_0^\infty f(x)e^{-x}dx
 \tag{146.33}
$$
for every fixed continuous polynomial-growth f. No power of Q is divided by v in this argument.

For the interior, choose a small fixed fractional band |r-r_-|<=d_1 r_sc lying to the right of xi_1 r_sc. Equation(146.23) and the stationary equation give F''<=-c eta on this band, and(146.24) gives a third derivative O(sqrt(delta eta)). With z=sqrt K(r-r_-), Taylor's theorem at the EXACT stationary point yields
$$
 F(r_-+z/\sqrt K)-A=-z^2/2+O_M(|z|^3/t)
 \tag{146.34}
$$
for bounded z, and concavity gives the global band envelope exp(F-A)<=exp(-c z^2). The band endpoints in z tend to infinity in absolute value because sqrt K r_sc is comparable to t. This proves the Gaussian local integral and every fixed z moment on the band.

The rest of the interior interval inside a sufficiently large fixed U= sqrt(delta/eta)r compact has an action gap F<=-c v, uniformly away from this band and the boundary. This follows from the same limiting quartic and the positive separator xi_0. When divided by either leading mass in(146.30), the gap integral costs h r_sc=O(v), exp(-A)=O(t), and fixed moment factors at most O(t^p); all are powers of t, not Q. They are beaten by e^-cv.

For charges outside that compact, the joint real-energy-tilt density bound (137.21)–(137.23), valid also for e=0, is
$$
 \frac{g_y^0(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}{g_y^0(0)}
 \le C\exp\left[v\left\{u^2-\frac{c u^4}{1+\eta u^2}\right\}\right].
 \tag{146.35}
$$
Its denominator is bounded by c<=sqrt(delta)f_0^0(H_y)<=C; no polynomial-in-Q prefactor is hidden here. For any fixed B_0 choose a fixed large M. Since u^2/(1+eta u^2) is increasing, eta->0 makes the braces <=-B_0u^2 for all |u|>=M eventually. On the negative-charge side the field factor is exp(-hr)<=1, so it only helps. Integrating(146.35), with the Jacobian sqrt(eta/delta), and dividing by 1/h costs O(v) times fixed powers of t and a Gaussian tail in u at speed v. The resulting tail tends to zero with any fixed power of z or x. This proves that no remote negative saddle or extreme charge mass contributes to(146.30).

Combining these facts proves
$$
 \frac{\sqrt K}{e^A}
 \int_{\xi r_{\rm sc}}^\infty
  g\bigl(\sqrt K(r-r_-)\bigr)e^{F(r)}dr
       \longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R}g(z)e^{-z^2/2}dz.
 \tag{146.36}
$$
Equations(146.33),(146.36) are the common relative asymptotics and local laws. The widths are1/h and K^-1/2, with h/sqrt K comparable to t. No coalescence of stationary locations is being assumed: their separation measured in either local scale tends to infinity.

### 146.6 有限等高点与等权点的对数位移

Let h_A solve A(h_A,y)=0 and put r_A=r_-(h_A,y), K_A=K(h_A,y),
$$
 L_A=\log[h_A\sqrt{2\pi/K_A}]=\log t+O(1).
 \tag{146.37}
$$
Let h_W=h_Q(0,y). The following more precise parametrization is useful:
$$
 h_Q(\lambda,y)=h_A+\frac{L_A-\lambda}{r_A}+o(1/r_A),
 \tag{146.38}
$$
uniformly for bounded lambda and compact y. It retains the exact finite profile and is not a definition in terms of the sought integrals.

To prove it, (146.26) and monotonicity first give h_Q-h_A=O(log t/r_A). Since A_h=-r_-, A_hh=1/K=O(eta^-1), Taylor's theorem bounds the quadratic error in A by O(log^2t/(eta r_A^2))=O(log^2t/v)=o(1). The derivative of log[h sqrt(2pi/K)] is O(1/h)+O(sqrt(delta)/eta^(3/2)); over that displacement its change is O(log t/v)=o(1). Therefore Lambda(h_A+Delta)=L_A-r_A Delta+o(1) on this scale. Monotonicity with derivative comparable to -r_A proves(146.38).

In particular, with kappa_A=h_A/h_sc and kappa_W=h_W/h_sc,
$$
 \kappa_W-\kappa_A
   =\frac{L_A}{r_Ah_{\rm sc}}+o(v^{-1})
   =\frac{\log t}{m^2w_0t^2}\{1+o(1)\}>0.
 \tag{146.39}
$$
The first expression in(146.39), and(146.38), retain the precision of the actual window. The second is only its leading logarithmic displacement. At equal HEIGHT the wider interior well has mass larger by h_A sqrt(2pi/K_A), which is comparable to t; a larger positive field is required to reduce it to equal mass. This checks the sign independently.

The finite eta, sigma, output and empirical corrections to kappa_A-kappa_c may exceed log t/t^2. Nothing here replaces h_A by kappa_c h_sc at the narrow-window scale. Lambda=0 is a finite computable PROFILE center predicting asymptotic equal probabilities; it does not assert that the original finite count probabilities are exactly equal there. If an exact original equal-region-mass field is desired for a fixed separator, positivity and the strict decrease of N_I^P(h)/N_B^P(h) in h give uniqueness. Applying the uniform limits below at lambda=+epsilon and -epsilon brackets that field, and then epsilon->0 gives h_equal^P=h_W+o(1/r_A). This optional statement follows from(146.8), not from defining Lambda as that ratio.

### 146.7 逐区域返回实际非中心剖面和原始计数

Let g_y^e(r)=e^{gamma r^2}f_r^e(H_y), where f_r^e uses the ACTUAL energy sum_H(Y_j-e_j)^2 and the same noise. The relative comparison in Section 137.6, valid on every fixed U compact including zero, is
$$
 \sup_{|u|\le M,|y|\le R}
 \left|\frac{g_y^e(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}
                 {g_y^0(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}-1\right|\to0.
 \tag{146.40}
$$
The absolute-log precision is essential. In the SAME centered real energy tilt, the exact exponent difference is
$$
 \Delta\mathcal K_r(z)
  =z\{-2(r/V_H)b^T(I-2zA_0)^{-1}e_H
                    +e_H^T(I-2zA_0)^{-1}e_H\}.
 \tag{146.41}
$$
By(146.12), its absolute value is at most C_M(eta+sqrt(delta))/delta times (sqrt(eta)delta^5+delta^10)=o(1). The tilted energy-mean displacement divided by sqrt(delta) is o(1); the common Fourier block makes the two scaled tilted densities have the same positive local limit. This proves the relative nature of(146.40), rather than an o(v) logarithmic approximation. The same global density tail as(146.35) holds for actual e. Thus(146.33),(146.36), with their tail estimates, transfer to g_y^e(-r) without any inverse-small-component loss. Center derivatives of g_y^e are not required: its relative density comparison on the entire contributing region suffices.

The EXACT raw negative Gaussian region masses, with the original likelihood kernel rather than a density-normalized likelihood, are
$$
 N^B_G=\sigma\sqrt{\delta/V_H}
           \int_0^{\xi r_{\rm sc}}e^{-hr}g_y^e(-r)dr,
 \quad
 N^I_G=\sigma\sqrt{\delta/V_H}
           \int_{\xi r_{\rm sc}}^\infty e^{-hr}g_y^e(-r)dr.
$$
$$
 M_0(y)=\sigma\sqrt{\delta/V_H}\,g_y^0(0)\asymp\sigma,
 \quad
 N^B_G=\frac{M_0}h(1+o(1)),\quad
 N^I_G=\frac{M_0}h e^\Lambda(1+o(1)).
 \tag{146.42}
$$
The prefactor includes the charge and energy-noise normalizations. Both masses are directly comparable to sigma/h for bounded Lambda. The positive-charge majority never appears in a denominator in this proof.

For the count return re-establish the joint growing-field bound on the whole fixed kappa slab. On the SAME tuple,
$$
 hD\le\eta D^2+h^2/(4\eta),\qquad
 h^2/(4\eta)=\kappa^2m^2v/4=O(v).
 \tag{146.43}
$$
The law with a_+=(2V)^-1+2eta has the scope of Chapter 137. Its exact joint modal/likelihood/charge-score estimate gives, for each fixed j,k,p and widths in[sigma/2,2sigma],
$$
 E_y^G[e^{aD_G^2+hD_G}(1+S_G)^j
          (1+\mathcal L_y)^k(1+|U_G|^p)]
                  \le P_{j,k,p}(Q)e^{C_{j,k,p}v}.
 \tag{146.44}
$$
Here S_G=(1/2)sum_H Y_j^2/v_j, mathcal L_y=(E_H-H_y)^2/(2delta sigma^2), U_G=sqrt(delta/eta)D_G. These are insertions in ONE conditional energy Fourier integral. In that integral the real tilted covariance retains its block, standardized modal means cost a polynomial in Q and charge, and the normalized noise mean is bounded by C(z_charge^2+|xi|), with z_charge=delta^(1/4)D_G. The block absorbs fixed frequency polynomials. Thus no inverse sigma or product of independently optimized marginal bounds enters(146.44). Applying Chapter 137 at 2eta and(146.43) changes only the constants in its exp(Cv) bound, not the noise margin.

On all central high count cells, uniformly over EVERY low tuple with its exact product probability, the Stirling estimates and cell geometry of Section 144.6 give
$$
 |\log(\hbox{lifted high density}/\phi_C)|\le\mathcal E_Q,
 \quad |D-D_G|\le\mathcal E_Q,
 \quad |T-T_G|/\sigma\le\mathcal E_Q,
$$
$$
 |D_G|\le CQ^3,\quad T_G=(E_H-V)/\sqrt\delta,
 \quad\mathcal E_Q=P(Q)e^{-bQ^3},\ b>0.
 \tag{146.45}
$$
The positive exponent payments are c_q/2-l, c_q-2zeta-l and the high-cell Stirling margin. Low charge and energy bounds are applied before summing low probabilities. Full mu,V and all floors are unchanged.

The quadratic and linear exponent changes across a cell cost a polynomial times mathcal E_Q, since h is polynomially bounded. For the likelihood put b_0=(T-T_G)/sigma, u_0=(T_G-y)/sigma. Its log change is -b_0u_0-b_0^2/2. The mean-value estimate and Young's inequality absorb exp(C mathcal E_Q |u_0|) into a width sigma/sqrt(1-C mathcal E_Q). Formula(146.44) controls the integrated joint error. Integrating the exact log-width derivative 2mathcal L_y of the likelihood pays that width change too. This introduces no inverse-sigma derivative. The ordinary likelihood normalization is comparable to sigma. Therefore the central lifted signed-measure error with any fixed U weight is bounded by
$$
 \sigma P_p(Q)\exp[-bQ^3+C_pv].
 \tag{146.46}
$$
The comparison is before any region normalization, and may be restricted to any measurable charge region. Every low probability is summed inside this same comparison.

Extreme tuples are controlled jointly, not by an unconditioned supercritical Gaussian integral. Put d_noise=delta sigma^2. From D^2<=2n_gE+2(sum e_j)^2 and(146.43), completing the square in E gives on EVERY tuple
$$
 e^{aD^2+hD-(E-H_y)^2/(2d_{\rm noise})}
 \le e^{C v+2a_+(\sum e_j)^2+2a_+n_gH_y+4a_+^2n_g^2d_{\rm noise}}
            e^{-(E-H_y)^2/(4d_{\rm noise})}.
 \tag{146.47}
$$
The prefactor logarithm is O(Q^(7/2))+O(v). The raw excluded high-binomial cells have mass P(Q)e^-cQ^4. A fixed charge polynomial costs at most exp(C_pQ^3); division by sigma costs O(Q^3) in the logarithm. Thus the excluded count contribution remains exp(-c'Q^4) after normalization by sigma, with the field paid. Gaussian excluded cells obey the analogous bound. This keeps original count boundaries and the full tuple in the argument.

The new observable weights are also covered: |hD_G|=O(v)|U_G| and |sqrt K(-D_G-r_-)|<=Ct(1+|U_G|). All extra fixed powers are polynomial in Q since v=o(Q^(1/2)). Divide(146.46), and its excluded-cell extension, separately by the two lower bounds in(146.42). The resulting relative error for either region and either fixed polynomial weight is at most
$$
 hP_p(Q)e^{-bQ^3+C_pv}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{146.48}
$$
Here c delta^(1/4)<=h<=C delta^-1/2 eventually. There is no inverse-majority/minority probability, and no O(log Q) error divided by an arbitrarily slow v. The polynomial factors are paid only by the strict Q^3 exponential margin.

Region cuts and lattice atoms require one more payment. On central cells, a disagreement about D<0 requires |D_G|<=mathcal E_Q. Its raw Gaussian mass is at most C sigma mathcal E_Q by(146.31),(146.40); divided by either mass in(146.42) it is O(h mathcal E_Q). A discrepancy at the separator requires ||D_G|-xi r_sc|<=mathcal E_Q. The separator lies in a fixed action gap, so this strip costs at most C sigma mathcal E_Q e^-cv, with fixed polynomial weights. This also tends to zero relatively. A count atom exactly at a cut is covered by these strips. Equivalently the boundary variable has mesh h/B->0 exponentially, even if1/h shrinks; no integer alignment assumption on m_J is required. The interior scaled cell displacement is O(sqrt eta mathcal E_Q)->0 as well.

On a fixed compact of X or Z, uniform continuity transfers a continuous test from its lifted value to its count value. Higher fixed moments, already controlled in(146.33),(146.36),(146.46)--(146.48), remove the compact restriction. Consequently the ORIGINAL product COUNT law satisfies both relative mass formulas in(146.42) and both conditional limits in(146.9), before full-q selection is applied. All two-region estimates are simultaneous in the empirical field, physical output and separator.

### 146.8 在两个竞争归一化中恢复完整选择

Let nu_B and nu_I be the exact PRODUCT count posterior restricted and normalized to the two regions just proved. They have every fixed moment of X and Z respectively bounded uniformly. On nu_B, D^2=X^2/h^2, so(146.11) gives for each fixed p
$$
 E_{\nu_B}[(1+X^p)|L_x(k)-1|]
   \le C_p\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\varepsilon/h^2\}
   \le C_p\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\delta^6/\eta^3\}\to0.
 \tag{146.49}
$$
On nu_I, D^2<=2r_-^2+2Z^2/K, with r_-^2 comparable to eta/delta and K comparable to eta. Thus
$$
 E_{\nu_I}[(1+|Z|^p)|L_x(k)-1|]
 \le C_p\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}
                      +\eta\delta^4+\delta^5/\eta\}\to0.
 \tag{146.50}
$$
Both vanish for EVERY admissible sequence. For example delta^6/eta^3=delta^(9/2)/t^3 and delta^5/eta=delta^(9/2)/t. This controls the selection factor on the SAME conditional realization rather than through an untilted TV estimate.

Taking p=0 in(146.49)--(146.50) gives E_nuB L=1+o(1) and E_nuI L=1+o(1). Therefore the selected raw masses satisfy
$$
 N_P^B=\frac{M_0}h(1+o(1)),\qquad
 N_P^I=\frac{M_0}h e^\Lambda(1+o(1)),
 \quad\frac{N_P^I}{N_P^B}=e^\Lambda(1+o(1)).
 \tag{146.51}
$$
In particular both events are positive. For each polynomial-growth test, the identity E_P f=E_nu(Lf)/E_nu L and(146.49) or(146.50) transfers its conditional expectation. This proves(146.9), and(146.51) proves(146.8). The exact outside labels, count support and finite normalization from(146.10) remain present throughout.

Changing xi within a fixed permissible compact changes only the middle action-gap strip. Its mass, and each fixed local-variable moment, is o(M_0/h) under the product count law by the preceding gap/cell estimates. The global upper envelope for L in(146.11) pays the same strip under P. This proves separator invariance, including any fixed pair of permissible separators by choosing a compact containing them. It is not a claim uniform as the separator tends to0 or w_0 with Q.

### 146.9 新推导、文献归属与边界

本章的新推导包括 Fourier 前因子的三阶导数、严格单调的有限外场坐标、两个区域在任意缓慢速度下的共同相对尾界，以及分别以 $\sigma/h$ 为尺度的原始计数和完整选择回接。由两个正质量得到 logistic 比例、端点 Laplace 与内部 Gaussian 的主项，以及四次剖面的等高计算均为成熟机制；它们本身不替代 (146.40)–(146.51) 的模型内证明。

Borgs–Kotecký 的有限体积相权重保留表面、边和角的自由能贡献，为“次主项能改变有限相权重”提供文献参照，但其轮廓表示、Peierls 条件、维数与边界假设未在本模型中成立。Fernandez–Spence–Fokas 处理驻点接近端点的特定振荡积分；这里两处质量中心按各自局部宽度相隔发散，关注的是质量竞争。该文的 Fresnel 公式不直接应用于本章，所需一致误差由 (146.18)–(146.36) 给出。Temme 的 Watson／Laplace 方法、Siripraparat–Neammanee 的异质 Bernoulli 局部界，以及条件乘积表示保留第 143、144 章的归属与假设。具体版本和核对范围见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。

有限 $\eta$、噪声、输出及经验修正可大于 $\log t/t^2$；(146.38)–(146.39) 因此比较精确有限等高点与等权点，而不将中心直接替换为极限常数 $\kappa_c$。本章不涵盖无界竞争坐标、随 $Q$ 接近端点的分隔符、更强噪声范围、动力学亚稳态或熵导数；普通数学证明及有限检索不构成形式化或全局原创性认证。

## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）

## 147. 总数可测的稀有标签池选择与次二次对数带宽

当 $R/Q^{3/2}$ 增长时，固定标签池落入有利区域的概率趋于零。本章先观察各池总数，再选择一个池，最后才揭示它的内部拆分。条件核引理保证所选池仍服从原始的两个公平二项分配，因此可以使用 $\exp(o(Q))$ 个试验池而只支付一次算术失败概率。额外的分离宽度同时消除 $R=Q^{3/2}$ 端点处不消失的拆分尾部。

结论保留原始 pair/path 实验、确定支持的一致性、完整选择计数后验、有限参数、全部输出和共用残差。常数只依赖固定的原始幅度、$\beta$ 与正带宽比较常数，不依赖试验池数量或 $R/Q^{3/2}$ 的上界；原数据紧性局部化在 $Q\to\infty$ 后解除。以下为普通数学推导，未作形式化认证。

### 147.1 次二次对数带宽下的原始完整后验

**定理 147.1（次二次对数尺度的完整方差熵极限）。** Let R=R_Q be any deterministic sequence such that

$$
 Q^{3/2}\le R=o(Q^2),\qquad
 \mathcal B=q/Q^{11/4},\qquad \rho=\sigma\mathcal B,\qquad
 0<c_-\le\rho e^R\le c_+<\infty.                    \tag{147.1}
$$

Separately in the original independent-pair and path experiments, uniformly over deterministic true supports of size q,

$$
 \boxed{\int_{\mathbb R} f_x(y)|D_x(y)-R_*(y)|\,dy
          \longrightarrow0}                       \tag{147.2}
$$

in original raw-data probability. All definitions remain those of (145.2)–(145.4):

$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q/Q^{5/2},\quad
 T=\mathcal B^{-1}\sum_j(R_j-\mu_j)^2-V/\sqrt\delta,\quad
 Y=T+\sigma G,
$$
$$
 A=V_H/\sqrt\delta,\quad \nu_0=2\sum_{j\in H}w_j^2,\quad
 \kappa_3=8\sum_{j\in H}w_j^3,\quad \Lambda=\nu_0+\sigma^2,
$$
$$
 C_x=A^2\kappa_3/\Lambda^3-2A\nu_0/\Lambda^2,\quad
 D_x(y)=Vpost_x(y)-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xy,
$$
$$
 R_*(y)=29/6-3\sqrt2+(3\sqrt2+8/\sqrt3-9)y^2/\nu,
 \qquad \nu=2g_0.                                  \tag{147.3}
$$

Vprior is the exact selected full-count centered-surprise variance and m_x=E_xY is exact. In particular,

$$
 \int Vpost_x(y)f_x(y)\,dy-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xm_x
                   \longrightarrow8/\sqrt3-25/6.   \tag{147.4}
$$

Every original floor, scale, group, multiplicity, center, physical H, low/outside group, full-q selected prior and residual G is retained. Proof pools and a Fourier block do not change that array. No claim is made at R comparable to Q^2, at zero noise, about necessity, sharpness or computational efficiency. Earlier conclusions keep their scopes.



### 147.2 可测选择、端点分离与证明尺度

The first repair is a selection rule measurable from pool totals alone. It allows exp(o(Q)) trial pools while charging the arithmetic failure of just one selected pool. The second repair enlarges a proof-only separation width enough to make the selected split tail vanish even at the lower endpoint. Define

$$
 \lambda=Q^3,\quad \widehat R=R+\sqrt{\lambda\log Q},\quad
 L=10\widehat R+20\log Q.                            \tag{147.5}
$$

Then L>=10R+20log Q, L^2/lambda>=100log Q,
L=o(Q^2), and L^2/lambda=O(R^2/Q^3+log Q)=o(Q).
The additional width changes neither rho nor physical T. This avoids a hidden order-one split-tail failure when R/Q^(3/2) is bounded, and avoids invoking Chapter 145 with unproved uniformity in its fixed constant c.

The full-axis proof uses

$$
 n=\lfloor Q\sqrt R\rfloor,\quad Z=QR,\quad
 U=e^{10KZ},\quad
 N=\lceil1000\rho^{-1}\sqrt{R+\log Q}\rceil,          \tag{147.6}
$$

where K is fixed sufficiently large in the model parameters. In particular n/R tends to infinity, n/Q^2 tends to zero, n^2/Q<=Z=o(Q^3), and n is at least a constant times Q^(7/4). No little-o here assumes that R/Q^(3/2) is bounded.

### 147.3 联合槽位律与保留条件核的选池引理

Use the original aligned kernel, with parity chi,

$$
 P_S(x,y)=\frac{1+b_S(x)\chi(y)}{2M},\qquad
 b_S=r1_S-\epsilon_M1_{C_+\setminus S},\quad
 b_S|_{C_-}=0,\quad \epsilon_M=rq/(M-q).
$$

The class sums of b_S are zero. As proved in (120.14)–(120.17) and restated in (145.6)–(145.9), conditioning on the entire stationary-path parity record s gives independent departure labels with

$$
 P(X_t=i\mid s)=1_{\{\chi(i)=s_t\}}
                  [1+b_S(i)s_{t+1}]/M\quad(t<T_{\rm obs}),
 \qquad P(X_{T_{\rm obs}}=i\mid s)=1_{\{\chi(i)=s_{T_{\rm obs}}\}}/M.
                                                               \tag{147.7}
$$

Indeed the density factors over departures; summing over labels in each specified class gives M at every departure, so the parity record is exactly iid fair. Reassigning a departure within its class preserves the preceding transition's parity argument. For independent pairs, parity pairs are iid uniform, departure labels obey the same conditional formula and arrivals are uniform in their classes. Thus these are actual raw-data operations in each experiment, with no posterior intervention.

Given parity, positive and negative departure counts are two independent multinomial arrays with sample sizes N_+,N_-. Rows within each array remain dependent. Each size has mean T_obs/4, where T_obs=2Mlambda, and their variances sum to O(T_obs): for the path, adjacent parity-pattern indicators are1-dependent. Consequently

$$
 P_S\{|N_\pm-T_{\rm obs}/4|>M^{2/3}\}
                    \le C\lambda M^{-1/3}.          \tag{147.8}
$$

Preselect m disjoint pairs U_i={u_i,v_i} of true labels by a deterministic ordering under fixed S. Reveal parity, all pool-membership masks for departure slots, all labels outside their union, and final path label or pair arrivals. Call this field H_0. The totals K_{i,+},K_{i,-} are H_0-measurable. Conditional on H_0, the complete allocation vectors V_i are JOINTLY independent fair-bit strings, and hence

$$
 (k_i,l_i)_{i=1}^m\mid H_0
 \sim\bigotimes_{i=1}^m
       [Bin(K_{i,+},1/2)\otimes Bin(K_{i,-},1/2)].   \tag{147.9}
$$

This follows from the product slot density and equal true weights within each pair. It is not multiplication of unconditional row marginals.

**引理 147.2（总数可测选择保留隐藏分配核）。** Suppose the conditional law of V_1,...,V_m given a field H_0 is a product of kernels K_i, possibly on H_0-measurable finite spaces. If I is H_0-measurable and F reveals H_0 and every V_j with j!=I, then

$$
 E[h(V_I)\mid F]=\sum_i1_{\{I=i\}}K_i h.             \tag{147.10}
$$

More generally an F-measurable family of subsets of the selected allocation space is evaluated by that same selected kernel. To prove this, on {I=i} test against a bounded H_0-measurable function times a product of bounded functions of V_j,j!=i. Conditional product integration gives the claimed identity; a monotone-class argument extends the test functions to H_0 joined with all those V_j. Sum over the finite partition {I=i}. Random allocation lengths cause no difficulty: use the disjoint union of their finite spaces. The same proof first for rectangles proves the kernel statement for F-measurable subsets.

The eventual m is finite at every Q; the lemma is exact with no dimension constant. A hidden-split-based choice of I would not meet its hypothesis. Our choice is the first index whose totals meet the fixed test in Section 147.5; if none does, choose1 and retain a separate failure flag. After revealing every other allocation, (147.9) is still the EXACT two-binomial law for the selected pair. An F-measurable anchor and calibration may then depend on those other allocations without changing this kernel.

### 147.4 只用于有利总数存在性的稀疏比较

For one categorical vector taking values0,e_j with probabilities1-p,p_j, p=sum p_j, direct summation gives its event-total-variation distance to independent Pois(p_j) coordinates:

$$
 d_{\rm TV}=p(1-e^{-p})\le p^2.                     \tag{147.11}
$$

For verification, Poisson masses at0 and at total count>=2 exceed the categorical masses, whereas categorical singleton masses exceed e^-p p_j. Half the sum of the three absolute contributions is p(1-e^-p). Independent slot couplings and summing counts bound the mismatch by the sum of squared selected slot probabilities.

Conditional on parity, our2m labels have selected slot probability2m(1+r)/M or2m(1-r)/M. The joint count comparison error is therefore Cm^2lambda/M. On the parity event of(147.8), each mean differs from a lambda or b lambda by at most CM^-1/3, where a=(1+r)/2 and b=(1-r)/2. Coupling Poisson means by addition costs at most their absolute difference, so

$$
 d_{\rm TV}\left(\mathcal L_S((k_j,l_j)_{j\in\cup U_i}),
        \bigotimes_{j=1}^{2m}(Pois(a\lambda)\otimes Pois(b\lambda))\right)
 \le\tau_Q=C\{\lambda M^{-1/3}+mM^{-1/3}+m^2\lambda/M\}.        \tag{147.12}
$$

The constant has no dimension dependence hidden beyond the displayed m. This comparison is solely for the bounded existence event below. Neither its law nor a conditional Poisson law replaces the selected posterior, channel, surprise, calibration or exact kernel(147.10).

### 147.5 精确率函数下的稀有总数放大

Put alpha_0=log(1+r)>0 and beta_0=log(1-r)<0. The original floors give

$$
 \phi=a\alpha_0+b\beta_0>0,\quad
 \log M=(\phi/\beta)Q^3+O(1),\quad
 \log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),\quad c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta>0.
                                                               \tag{147.13}
$$

Fix the following explicit positive constants:

$$
 \delta_*=\{100(1+\alpha_0+|\beta_0|)\}^{-1},\quad
 D_*=9/\alpha_0+1,\quad
 C_*=D_*^2/(2a)+1/(2b)+1,
 \quad c_*=\min\{1/4,\delta_*^2/(64\sqrt{ab})\}.       \tag{147.14}
$$

Call pool totals favorable if

$$
 |K_+-2a\lambda-9L/\alpha_0|\le\delta_*\sqrt\lambda,
 \qquad |K_--2b\lambda|\le\delta_*\sqrt\lambda.       \tag{147.15}
$$

These are revealed-total conditions; neither internal split is inspected. For v>0 and |n-vlambda|<=vlambda/2, the Poisson rate J_v(x)=xlog(x/v)-x+v has J_v(v)=J_v'(v)=0 and J_v''(x)=1/x. Taylor's integral formula on this fixed interval gives

$$
 \lambda J_v(n/\lambda)\le(n-v\lambda)^2/(v\lambda).
$$

The elementary Stirling inequality n!<=3sqrt(n)(n/e)^n then gives

$$
 P\{Pois(v\lambda)=n\}\ge
       (4\sqrt{v\lambda})^{-1}
         \exp[-(n-v\lambda)^2/(v\lambda)].           \tag{147.16}
$$

Indeed3sqrt(3/2)<4. Every window in(147.15) contains at least delta_*sqrt(lambda) integers eventually. Since L=o(lambda), all its points satisfy the required relative-deviation restriction. Their positive and negative deviations are bounded respectively by D_*L and L. Applying(147.16) to v=2a,2b and multiplying yields

$$
 P_{\rm Pois}\{\hbox{one pool has favorable totals}\}
             \ge p_Q:=c_*e^{-C_*L^2/\lambda}.        \tag{147.17}
$$

The exact rate inequality, not a quadratic asymptotic with an uncontrolled cubic remainder, proves this throughout the growing range.

Choose the deterministic number of preselected pools

$$
 m=\lceil c_*^{-1}Q^2e^{C_*L^2/\lambda}\rceil.        \tag{147.18}
$$

Thus log m=o(Q), 2m<=q eventually, and every term of tau_Q tends to zero; their logarithms are dominated by the fixed positive Q^3 exponents in(147.13). The favorable-total events are independent in the product Poisson comparison. Returning just their union event to the actual law gives

$$
 \sup_S P_S\{\hbox{no favorable pool}\}
                       \le e^{-Q^2}+\tau_Q=o(1).    \tag{147.19}
$$

The joint sparse bound is paid once, not divided by the probability of rare totals.

### 147.7 同一完整数组的三标签删除与锚响应

It concerns the same complete array; it is not reconstructed independently for each pool. Delete the selected pair and one central anchor chosen by a deterministic F-measurable order. ### 147.10 整个实频率轴与两阶归一化实标记

for every fixed A, because n/R tends to infinity. This pays all non-half-integer rational arcs. Merely having many groups would not suffice without(147.37) and the reserved integrable envelope.

Inside strips use the exact real-tilt Poisson formula (145.43), restated to specify its interface. On J use normalized Gaussian integer weights and on E=J^c keep exact binomial weights; retain the same integer scalar, centers, intercept and G. Let s_lat be exact centered count surprise, W=s_lat+G^2/2, tilt the same joint law by e^(uW), normalize for real u near zero and hold physical y fixed. Put tau=1-u, m_j=C_jp_j,

### 147.12 无逆噪声损失的有符号矩与完整选择律

For clarity the physical return is recorded with its inherited quantitative interfaces, not inferred from an unmarked marginal. On J the coordinate estimate (111.10) is C_hd_j^-1/8 for mass times centered surprise to each fixed power h<=4. Its hypotheses are p_j in a fixed compact subinterval of(0,1), d_j large, fixed-order Stirling on |k-m_j|<=d_j^(5/8) and fixed moment tails. They are unchanged. E retains every exact binomial law. Telescoping at most CQ^2 coordinates and CQ^4 two-mark terms, with exact intermediate centering and d_j>=Q^3600, gives

$$
 \|\eta_h^Q-\eta_h^{\rm lat}\|_{\rm TV}\le CQ^{-444}
 \quad(h\le2),\qquad \eta_h(k)=Q_x(k)s_Q(k)^h.       \tag{147.49}
$$

TV here is full absolute signed mass; binomial laws are zero-extended on the common integer space. Both intermediate laws use the SAME T(k),mu,V and G. For r<=2, the nonnegative kernel

$$
 K_r(k,y)=((y-T(k))/\sigma)^{2r}\varphi_\sigma(y-T(k)),
 \qquad \int K_r(k,y)\,dy=EG^{2r}                  \tag{147.50}
$$

has a sigma-independent signed-L1 norm. If q_h(y)dy=E[W^h;Y in dy], W=s+G^2/2, then

$$
 q_h^Q-q_h^{\rm lat}
 =\sum_{r=0}^h{h\choose r}2^{-r}K_r
                  (\eta_{h-r}^Q-\eta_{h-r}^{\rm lat}),
 \quad\max_{h\le2}\|q_h^Q-q_h^{\rm lat}\|_1\le CQ^{-444}.
                                                               \tag{147.51}
$$

No exp(R), rho^-1 or sigma^-1 multiplies this fixed polynomial comparison error.

For the nonlinear conditional-mean-square density use q_1^2/q_0=sup_z(2zq_1-z^2q_0). Clipping |z|<=b bounds integrated variance-density differences by epsilon_2+2b epsilon_1+b^2epsilon_0 plus(E|W|^4+E|W_lat|^4)/b^2. Fourth moments are at most CQ^4. With b=Q^10 the cost is O(Q^-16)+O(Q^-424). The exact prior-variance difference is O(Q^-448). Thus the conditional-mean square is explicitly included.

The finite payments Vprior=O(Q^2), A^2/Lambda=O(Q^(1/2)), C_x=O(Q^(1/4)) and quadratic R_* multiply vanishing mass errors. Fixed fourth output moments and Cauchy–Schwarz give weighted mass control. For the ORIGINAL selected full-q law, the same-tuple density h from (111.6) satisfies0<=h<=C, ||h-1||_2=a_x=O_P(Q^-5/2), and surprise includes its exact log h correction. The common-kernel/clipped-moment argument in (101.9), (101.15), and (111.16)–(111.17) costs Ca_xQ^2=o_P(1) for every sigma>0. Consequently

$$
 \|f_xD_x-f_{\rm lat}D_{\rm lat}\|_1=o_P(1),\qquad
 \int(1+y^2)|f_x-f_{\rm lat}|\,dy=o_P(1).            \tag{147.52}
$$

D_lat subtracts its own exact prior variance but adds the ORIGINAL A^2/Lambda-C_xy. This is a signed-moment comparison on a common scalar, not whole-law replacement by a Gaussian posterior or a known-support prior.

### 147.13 中等输出的实商与全部输出尾部

Let h_out=sqrt(100nu log Q). On |y|<=h_out, the continuous-J reference from Chapters 101 and 142 with exact E and noncentral factors obeys

$$
 g_0(y)\ge c_0Q^{-60},\qquad |g_1(y)|+|g_2(y)|\le CQ^4,
 \quad g_h=\partial_u^hg_u|_0.
$$

The reference proof requires sigma<=mathcal B^-1 and sigma tending to zero, both true here. It has no lower noise condition. Its fixed sufficiently high expansion order is used for this one reference, not repeated over the harmonic band.

For F=f_lat,u/g_u, exact differentiation at physical y gives

$$
 F-1=\Delta_0/g_0,\quad
 F'=\Delta_1/g_0-\Delta_0g_1/g_0^2,
$$
$$
 F''=\Delta_2/g_0-2\Delta_1g_1/g_0^2+
                  \Delta_0(2g_1^2/g_0^3-g_2/g_0^2).            \tag{147.53}
$$

The largest coefficient is CQ^188. Equation(147.48) first proves the REAL denominator F>=1/2, then |partial_u^2log F|<=CQ^-200. Bayes at fixed physical output gives the exact identity

$$
 Vpost(y)-Vprior=\tfrac12+\partial_u^2\log f_u(y)|_0.           \tag{147.54}
$$

Posterior surprise is W plus a y-only constant, and Var(W)=Vprior+1/2. Hence D_lat-D_g=partial_u^2log F. The exact finite A,Lambda,C_x cancel only in this intermediate difference; none has been asymptotically substituted.

For tails complete every lattice square at real |z|<=Csqrt(log Q). Its normalization ratio to the continuous square is1+O(exp(-c_0d_j)), uniformly in the shifted mean. The full continuous-comparison log mgf is

$$
 -zV/\sqrt\delta-\tfrac12\sum_J\log(1-2zw_j)
 +\sum_J\frac{zw_ja_j^2}{1-2zw_j}
 +\sigma^2z^2/2+\log E_Ee^{zT_E}.                 \tag{147.55}
$$

The large trace cancels the ORIGINAL intercept. The remaining mean is O(a_x^2/sqrt(delta))+O(Q^7202/mathcal B), the variance tends to nu, and higher terms are bounded by
C[epsilon|z|^3+a_x^2z^2+sigma^2z^2+|z|Q^7202/mathcal B].
The exact low/outside energy and surprise are retained. The product lattice correction is1+O(Q^2exp(-c_0Q^3600)), so Chernoff gives

$$
 P_{\rm lat}(|Y|>h_{\rm out})+P_g(|Y|>h_{\rm out})
                                      \le CQ^{-40}.           \tag{147.56}
$$

Conditional Jensen and Cauchy–Schwarz with EW^4<=CQ^4 bound posterior-variance tails by O(Q^-18). The exact prior and finite A,C_x,R_* payments have vanishing tails by the same moments. This argument neither needs a tail density lower bound nor introduces inverse noise.

Finally retain the continuous-reference observation map of Chapter 101. Condition on every outside count/Gaussian and the SAME G. Translate outside ENERGY inside the independent core density BEFORE separating outside surprise. The derivative bound (101.19) is Cdelta^-1/2; the outside-energy error (101.18) gives O(Q^-199.5) joint variation, then the clipping (101.8) at Q^10 costs O(Q^-7). Only after this translation does outside surprise decouple and cancel its own exact prior variance. The noncentral comparison (101.22) and clipping (101.23) cost O(Q^-1/4[1+(log Q)^(3/4)]). No step divides by sigma. The proof-only occupancy block and pools change neither H nor these energy errors.

The reference calculation (101.25)–(101.31), keeping Lambda=nu_0+sigma^2 exact, proves integral g|D_g-R_*| tends to zero. Its discarded old quantile-coupling lower-noise restriction is not an input to this reference statement. Equations(147.53–56) return it on every output to the lattice law; (147.52) returns it to the selected full-q original law, proving(147.2). The same weighted comparisons give E_xY^2 tending to nu. Integrating the exact R_* gives8/sqrt3-25/6 and proves(147.4), with exact C_xm_x.

Every newly growing cost is displayed. The proofs require only R>=Q^(3/2), R/Q^2 tending to zero, and fixed original parameters. Constants in the exact selected kernel, rare-total rate, response, projection and marked analysis do not depend on m or a putative fixed c=R/Q^(3/2). The eventual thresholds may depend on the deterministic sequence through R/Q^2; this is the claimed sequencewise theorem, not a uniform assertion over all unbounded finite-Q choices of R.

The only inverse-rho costs are the Gaussian sum over frequency periods and the harmonic tail, both explicitly paid. Fixed polynomial signed-measure errors remain noise-free. Raw bad environments are removed in probability; no claim averages unbounded posterior errors over those rare environments. No growing-order expansion, generic transcendence or independent-center law is used.

### 147.15 方法归属与二次尺度的未解边界

本章的核心是 (147.10) 的条件乘积核结论：选择指标只依赖已揭示总数时，揭示其余池的内部信息仍不改变所选池的核。它与 (147.17)–(147.19) 的精确 Poisson 率下界接合，将“存在稀有好池”的成本与“所选池的算术失败”分开支付。该分离通过同一完整数组的 (147.34)、(147.36)–(147.48) 以及有符号矩、实商和全输出回接，得到定理 147.1。经典条件乘积积分、Stirling、耦合、Gauss 和 Poisson 求和保留成熟方法归属。

Liu–Xia 的 Poisson 中等偏差定理控制具有局部依赖或 size-bias 耦合的单个整数变量的相对右尾，不能直接给出这里的联合池矩形，也不保证事后选择保留隐藏分配。Gross 的 fractional query 定理在乘积布尔输入、适应停止时刻与各子集乘积鞅条件下给出 revealment/Fourier 权重界，不能直接替代本模型的经验相位估计。本章使用有限分割证明 (147.10)，并直接计算联合槽位耦合与精确率不等式；文献提供可迁移的方法关系，不承担缺失的模型前提。版本、原文条件与源文缺陷见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。

原始行估计承接第 68 章，槽位律承接第 120 章，固定偏移概率比承接第 132 章，完整带标记回接承接第 101、111、140、142、145 章。这里所有增长误差都按每条确定序列 $Q^{3/2}\le R=o(Q^2)$ 结算；不宣称对所有有限 $Q$ 的无界 $R$ 选择一致。$R\asymp Q^2$、零噪声、必要阈值、锐性、环境期望收敛及算法效率仍未由本章解决，有限文献检索不构成全局原创性证明。

## 148. 有限共存权重的首项修正与实际等质量外场

本章沿用第 146 章的原始完整选择计数律、精确有限噪声剖面和共同数据条件。边界与内部阱的首项积分修正之差为负，因此实际等质量外场相对有限宽度坐标 $\Lambda=0$ 的外场向下移动。该位移小于第 146 章中等高点到等权点的正向对数位移；两个比较使用不同的精确有限中心。

### 148.1 原始选择计数的首个有限共存修正

**定理 148.1（原始完整选择计数的有限相权重修正）。** On the original full-q selected count law, with every scope condition of Chapter 146 retained,
$$
 \log\frac{N_P^I(h,y)}{N_P^B(h,y)}
 =\Lambda(h,y)+C_I(h,y)-C_B(h,y)+o(t^{-2}),
 \tag{148.1}
$$
where all terms on the right are the exact finite noisy-profile quantities
$$
 C_B=\frac{2\ell_y'(0)}{h^2},\qquad
 C_I=\frac{F_{rrrr}(r_-;h,y)}{8K^2}
       +\frac{5F_{rrr}(r_-;h,y)^2}{24K^3}.
 \tag{148.2}
$$
The prime on ell is a squared-charge derivative; the derivatives of F are charge derivatives at fixed h,y and empirical array. Their distinction matters.

Let m=sqrt(2V^4/C2) and w0=sqrt(2/3). The coefficient calculation gives the finite-empirical asymptotic statement
$$
 t^2 C_B-\frac{27}{4m^2}\to0,\qquad
 t^2 C_I-\frac{17}{8m^2}\to0,\qquad
 t^2(C_I-C_B)+\frac{37}{8m^2}\to0.
 \tag{148.3}
$$
This does not require m to converge to a deterministic constant. The exact expressions (148.2) are retained in(148.1) and in the corrected coordinate before (148.3) is derived. In particular no limiting quartic field is used as a window center.

For a fixed permissible separator, let h_equal^P(y) be the field where the two original negative-region raw masses are exactly equal. Let h_W be Chapter 146's exact Lambda=0 field, with r_W=r_-(h_W,y). Then
$$
 h_{\rm equal}^P
 =h_W+\frac{(C_I-C_B)(h_W,y)}{r_W}
                  +o\bigl((r_Wt^2)^{-1}\bigr)
 =h_W-\frac{37}{8m^2r_Wt^2}
                  +o\bigl((r_Wt^2)^{-1}\bigr).
 \tag{148.4}
$$
The first correction is negative. It is much smaller than Chapter 146's positive displacement of h_W from the EXACT finite equal-height field. That earlier result retains its stated scope. Separator dependence of the equal-mass field is below the remainder in(148.4).

Here is the precise probability and parameter scope. Retain
$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q\delta^5,\quad
 Q_x(n)=\prod_j\binom{C_j}{n_j}p_j^{n_j}(1-p_j)^{C_j-n_j},
 \quad v_j=C_jp_j(1-p_j)/B^2,
$$
$$
 V=\sum_jv_j,\quad C_2=\delta^{-1}\sum_jv_j^2,\quad
 e_j=(\mu_j-C_jp_j)/B,\quad x_j=(n_j-\mu_j)/B,
$$
$$
 E=\sum_jx_j^2,\quad D=\sum_j(x_j+e_j),\quad
 T=(E-V)/\sqrt\delta,
 \quad a=(2V)^{-1}+\eta.
 \tag{148.5}
$$
Q is the level; Q_x is the auxiliary product COUNT law, not the actual selected prior P_x. The exact posterior weight is
$$
 P_x(n)\exp\{aD^2+hD-(T-y)^2/(2\sigma^2)\}.
 \tag{148.6}
$$
Each deterministic eta=eta_Q>0 with eta->0 and t=eta/sqrt(delta)->infinity is admitted, with arbitrarily slow divergence of t. Sigma>0 tends to zero at any rate subject solely to
$$
 \limsup\frac{\log(1/\sigma)}{Q^3}<c_q/2,
 \quad \log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),\quad c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta.
 \tag{148.7}
$$
Write v=t^2, r_sc=m sqrt(eta/delta), h_sc=eta r_sc, kappa=h/h_sc and kappa_c=(2/3)sqrt(2/3). Use the exact centered Gaussian profile of Chapter 146, defined again in Section 148.3:
$$
 F(r;h,y)=\ell_y(r^2)-\ell_y(0)-hr,
 \quad F_r(r_-;h,y)=0,\quad K=-F_{rr}(r_-;h,y)>0,
$$
$$
 A=F(r_-;h,y),\qquad
 \Lambda=A+\log h+\tfrac12\log(2\pi/K).
 \tag{148.8}
$$
The branch is the unique maximum in Chapter 146's fixed scaled neighborhood of w0 r_sc near kappa_c. For a separator xi in a fixed compact [xi0,xi1] contained in(0,w0), define
$$
 B_\xi=\{0<-D\le\xi r_{\rm sc}\},\qquad
 I_\xi=\{-D>\xi r_{\rm sc}\}.
 \tag{148.9}
$$
N_P^B and N_P^I sum (148.6) over these regions, without division by any total posterior normalizer. They are positive on the common good events. This fixes the meaning of the raw masses in(148.1).

For each fixed L,R and separator compact, the supremum of t^2 times the absolute remainder in(148.1) over |Lambda(h,y)|<=L and |y|<=R tends to zero in ORIGINAL actual-data probability, uniformly over deterministic size-q supports, separately for the pair and path experiments. The same quantifier applies to(148.3), with its displayed scaling, and to r_W t^2 times the remainder in(148.4). Work first on each tight-constant actual-data class and then exhaust those classes. Every empirical center, field and region is defined on the same realization. Uniformity over those parameter sets covers empirical field choices; independence of a chosen field is not assumed. The claim is for every admissible sequence, not for one universal convergence rate across all such sequences.

The corrected coordinate Psi_coex=Lambda+C_I-C_B has a unique measurable local field solving Psi_coex=lambda for every bounded lambda. At that field the original log odds are lambda+o(t^-2). If p(lambda)=e^lambda/(1+e^lambda), then at the original Lambda=lambda field the interior sign-conditioned weight is
$$
 p(\lambda)+p(\lambda)(1-p(\lambda))(C_I-C_B)+o(t^{-2}).
 \tag{148.10}
$$
The remainder in this formula is simultaneous over the same sets. The formulas concern static region weights, not dynamical metastability or a phase diagram. The preceding results retain their stated scopes.

### 148.2 完整选择系数与共同定量条件

The original support posterior weights a size-q support by exp(sum of its original row scores W_i). The calibrated independent labels are p_i=logistic(W_i-log((M-q)/q)+theta_M), with sum_i p_i=q. Conditioning their TOTAL count on q gives precisely that posterior. Let J be the union of the full original count groups, k=sum_j n_j and m_J=sum_j C_jp_j. The exact coefficient relation (68.33), (68.38), and (70.6), used in Chapter 143, is
$$
 P_x(n)=L_x(k)Q_x(n),\quad BD=k-m_J,
 \quad
 L_x(k)=\frac{[z^{q-k}]\prod_{i\notin J}(1-p_i+p_i z)}
                  {[z^q]\prod_i(1-p_i+p_i z)}.
 \tag{148.11}
$$
Outside labels supply q-k; D is not constrained to vanish. All low groups, floors and multiplicities remain present. The exact full calibration mu in E is not replaced by product means. On the common classes N_J=sum C_j<q<M-N_J and all p_i lie strictly between0 and1, so the count box has full support.

Set d_c=sum_{i notin J}p_i(1-p_i), d_J=B^2V and d_all=d_c+d_J. The exact finite normalization and the variance-based Bernoulli local bound in Chapter 143 give, on EVERY count tuple,
$$
 \varepsilon=B^2/(2d_c)=O(\delta^5),\qquad
 L_x(k)=\exp\{\tfrac12\log(d_{\rm all}/d_c)-\varepsilon D^2\}
                       +O(q^{-1/2}),
$$
$$
 0\le L_x(k)\le1+C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}),\qquad
 |L_x(k)-1|\le C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\varepsilon D^2).
 \tag{148.12}
$$
Here d_c,d_all are comparable to q. We will multiply the resulting region-specific bounds by t^2, rather than assume that an o(1) selection error is sufficient.

The common data classes have c<=V,C2<=C, v_*<=C delta, n_g<=C delta^-4, p_j in[1/4,3/4], sum C_j<=CB^2, and at least c/delta coordinates with variances in[c delta,C delta]. Noncentrality satisfies
$$
 |e_j|\le C\delta^5\sqrt{v_j},\quad
 \|e\|\le C\delta^5,\quad (\sum_j|e_j|)^2\le C\delta^6.
 \tag{148.13}
$$
Choose l,zeta with log(1/sigma)<=lQ^3 eventually, l<c_q/2, 0<zeta<c_q/2 and 2zeta<c_q-l. Fix H={j:C_j>=exp(zeta Q^3)} throughout the parameter domain. Every low tuple is retained exactly in the count return. High/full discrepancies are a polynomial in Q times exp(-bQ^3), written o_exp, with b>0 depending on these strict margins.

The proof uses Chapter 146's proved branch, absolute same-fiber profile geometry and global density tails; its explicit exponentially small count-cell bound; and its bounded region moments. Its noncentral comparison was only o(1) and is NOT cited at the new precision: Section 148.5 proves a quantitative replacement. Sections 148.3–148.4 prove exact higher derivative and integration bounds. This identifies what is new beyond the leading logistic theorem of Chapter 146.

### 148.3 变化数组上精确鞍点前因子的高阶导数

For j in H let Y_j be centered independent Gaussians of variance v_j. Write V_H=sum_H v_j, C_H=diag(v_j), b=(v_j), d=b/V_H and A_0=C_H-bb^T/V_H. Given D_G=sum_H Y_j=r, the centered conditional vector has mean rd and covariance A_0. Add an independent Gaussian energy noise of variance delta sigma^2 and retain H_y=V+sqrt(delta)y with FULL V. Define
$$
 \mathcal K_0(z)=-\tfrac12\log\det(I-2zA_0)+\tfrac12\delta\sigma^2z^2,
 \quad \Psi(z)=z d^T(I-2zA_0)^{-1}d,
$$
$$
 \mathcal K(z,R_0)=\mathcal K_0(z)+R_0\Psi(z),\quad
 \gamma=\eta-\{(2V_H)^{-1}-(2V)^{-1}\},
$$
$$
 g_y^0(r)=e^{\gamma r^2}f_r^0(H_y),\qquad
 \ell_y(R_0)=\log g_y^0(\sqrt{R_0}).
 \tag{148.14}
$$
Here f_r^0 is the exact conditional centered energy-plus-noise density. R_0 is squared charge. Sigma, the high covariance defect, full original calibration and physical output are retained in this definition before taking any limit. Setting e=0 defines only this analytic comparator.

For 0<=R_0<=M^2 eta/delta let z(R_0) solve the real equation mathcal K_z=H_y. The bracket from Chapter 146 gives |z|delta<=C_M(eta+sqrt(delta)); W=mathcal K_zz is comparable to delta. The real saddle and density decomposition are EXACT:
$$
 \mathcal H(R_0)=\gamma R_0+\mathcal K(z(R_0),R_0)-z(R_0)H_y,
$$
$$
 L(R_0,\xi)=\mathcal K(z+i\xi/\sqrt\delta,R_0)
              -\mathcal K(z,R_0)-i\xi H_y/\sqrt\delta,
 \quad p_y(R_0)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^L d\xi,
$$
$$
 g_y^0(r)=\delta^{-1/2}e^{\mathcal H(r^2)}p_y(r^2),\quad
 c_M\le p_y\le C_M,
 \quad |e^L|\le(1+c\delta\xi^2)^{-c'/\delta}.
 \tag{148.15}
$$
The retained variance block gives the envelope and its integrability against every fixed frequency power. The lower bound comes from the local Fourier limit at the real tilted mean, not a complex-order zero-free assumption.

Here is a reusable fixed-order derivative argument extending Chapter 146's third derivative, with no differentiation of an asymptotic error. Set rho=delta R_0, tau=delta z and
$$
 \widetilde{\mathcal K}(\tau,\rho)
      =\delta\mathcal K(\tau/\delta,\rho/\delta).
 \tag{148.16}
$$
On the relevant real branch, its second tau derivative W/delta is bounded above and below. Its fixed higher tau derivatives and mixed derivatives needed through order seven are bounded uniformly; dependence on rho is affine. Indeed ||A_0||=O(delta), ||d||^2=O(delta), and spectral resolvents on the full vertical line obey |1-2(z+i omega)a_j|>=1-2za_j. The noise contributes only sigma^2 to the second rescaled tau derivative. In particular no inverse noise width occurs. For vertical estimates only derivatives with at least two frequency derivatives are needed; no bound on an unbounded linear imaginary noise term is asserted.

The rescaled saddle satisfies tildeK_tau(tau(rho),rho)=H_y. Implicit differentiation, with tildeK_tautau bounded below, gives bounded derivatives of tau(rho) through order five. This follows inductively: the highest derivative is multiplied by tildeK_tautau; all remaining terms are finite products of already bounded lower derivatives and bounded mixed derivatives. Hence
$$
 |z^{(j)}(R_0)|\le C_{j,M}\delta^{j-1},\qquad 1\le j\le5.
 \tag{148.17}
$$
For the Fourier exponent write q0=sqrt(delta)xi. In rescaled variables it is delta^-1 times
$$
 \widetilde{\mathcal K}(\tau(\rho)+iq_0,\rho)
  -\widetilde{\mathcal K}(\tau(\rho),\rho)-iq_0H_y.
 \tag{148.18}
$$
Its constant and linear q0 terms vanish identically for EVERY rho by the saddle equation. All rho derivatives preserve those cancellations. After j rho derivatives, the second q0 derivative is uniformly bounded along the entire vertical segment by the preceding resolvent and implicit-derivative bounds. Taylor's integral remainder, with partial_R0=delta partial_rho, therefore gives
$$
 |\partial_{R_0}^j L|\le C_{j,M}\delta^j\xi^2,
                   \qquad1\le j\le5.
 \tag{148.19}
$$
For each j, the derivative of exp L is exp L times a finite polynomial in the derivatives in(148.19). Every monomial of total derivative order j has a factor delta^j and a fixed polynomial in xi. The common envelope in(148.15) justifies differentiation under the integral, yielding
$$
 |p_y^{(j)}|+|(\log p_y)^{(j)}|\le C_{j,M}\delta^j,
                         \qquad1\le j\le5.
 \tag{148.20}
$$
Right derivatives at R_0=0 follow by the same dominated bounds. We never use negative squared charges. This is exact parameter control of the prefactor, not an inferred derivative of its leading local Gaussian approximation.

Since mathcal H'=gamma+Psi(z) and mathcal H''=-Psi'(z)^2/W, the rescaled action and(148.17) give
$$
 |\ell_y^{(j)}(R_0)|\le C_{j,M}\delta^{j-1},\quad2\le j\le5.
 \tag{148.21}
$$
The first and second derivative formulas of Chapter 146 are
$$
 \ell_y'(0)=\eta+O_R(\sqrt\delta+\delta)+o_{\exp}(1),
$$
$$
 \ell_y''(R_0)=-\frac\delta{m^2}\frac{2C_2}{2C_2+\sigma^2}
      \{1+O_M(\eta+\sqrt\delta)\}+O_M(\delta^2)+o_{\exp}(1).
 \tag{148.22}
$$
We keep these finite terms inside ell, not as replacements for it in(148.2).

For G(r)=ell(r^2), direct differentiation gives
$$
 G'''=12r\ell''+8r^3\ell''',\quad
 G''''=12\ell''+48r^2\ell'''+16r^4\ell'''',
$$
$$
 G'''''=120r\ell'''+160r^3\ell''''+32r^5\ell'''''.
 \tag{148.23}
$$
At all r in a fixed fractional neighborhood of r_-, K is comparable to eta, and(148.21)--(148.23) give
$$
 |F^{(3)}|/K^{3/2}\le C/t,\quad
 |F^{(4)}|/K^2\le C/t^2,\quad
 |F^{(5)}|/K^{5/2}\le C/t^3.
 \tag{148.24}
$$
The last bound can be improved by a factor eta but is sufficient here. Equivalent bounds follow by scaling r=r_sc w: F/(m^2t^2) has bounded derivatives through order five on the moderate region. These estimates apply on a band, not only at the stationary point, and are the needed Taylor-remainder control.

### 148.4 边界与内部积分的共同相对余项

Work uniformly on bounded |Lambda| and compact y and separator sets. The exact branch of Chapter 146 has r_-/r_sc->w0 and K/(2eta)->1. It also has
$$
 A=-\log t+O(1),\qquad
 e^A\sqrt{2\pi/K}=e^\Lambda/h.
 \tag{148.25}
$$
The anchored derivative bounds, strict local concavity and global density tail used below are simultaneous on this same profile. Define
$$
 J_B=\int_0^{\xi r_{\rm sc}}e^{F(r)}dr,\qquad
 J_I=\int_{\xi r_{\rm sc}}^\infty e^{F(r)}dr.
 \tag{148.26}
$$
We will prove the stronger explicit local statements
$$
 hJ_B=1+C_B+O(t^{-4}),\qquad
 e^{-A}\sqrt{K/(2\pi)}J_I=1+C_I+O(t^{-3}).
 \tag{148.27}
$$
Constants are uniform on the stated fixed parameter sets and common data classes. All exact finite derivatives in(148.2) are retained.

For the endpoint write x=hr, beta=ell'(0)/h^2. By(148.21)--(148.22), beta=O(t^-2) and
$$
 F(x/h)=-x+\beta x^2+O(\delta x^4/h^4),\qquad
 \delta/h^4=O(t^{-6}).
 \tag{148.28}
$$
The first formula is Taylor's theorem in squared charge with its genuine second derivative bound, valid on the needed moderate interval. On0<=x<=t^(1/4), expanding the exponential gives an integrated error at most C(beta^2+t^-6)=O(t^-4): the error is bounded by this coefficient times a fixed polynomial in x and exp(-x/2). Integrating1+beta x^2 against exp(-x) gives1+2beta=1+C_B.

For a small fixed d0>0 the anchored upper bound ell(r^2)-ell(0)<=C eta r^2 ensures F(r)<=-c hr on0<=r<=d0 r_sc. Thus the omitted part with x>t^(1/4) inside this band is smaller than every fixed inverse power of t. Between d0 r_sc and xi1 r_sc, the limiting critical quartic is strictly negative, uniformly away from0 and w0. The exact profile has F<=-c t^2 there eventually. Its normalized length h r_sc=O(t^2) introduces only powers of t. These bounds prove the first formula in(148.27), including its remainder, for arbitrarily slow t. No polynomial in Q has been discarded against this speed.

For the interior set z=sqrt K(r-r_-), b3=F'''(r_-)/K^(3/2) and b4=F''''(r_-)/K^2. The exact stationary equation and(148.24) give on a fixed fractional well band
$$
 F(r_-+z/\sqrt K)-A
  =-z^2/2+b_3z^3/6+b_4z^4/24+O(t^{-3}|z|^5).
 \tag{148.29}
$$
The band is strictly to the right of every permitted separator and F''<=-c eta there. Take the symmetric local range |z|<=t^(1/12), contained in that band eventually. There |b3|<=C/t and |b4|<=C/t^2; the perturbation of -z^2/2 is bounded by a small multiple of z^2. Expansion of its exponential through total order t^-2 has an integrable remainder O(t^-3) times a fixed polynomial in |z| and exp(-z^2/4). The terms retained are
$$
 1+\frac{b_3z^3}{6}+\frac{b_4z^4}{24}
                           +\frac{b_3^2z^6}{72}.
 \tag{148.30}
$$
The cubic integrates to zero on the symmetric range. Extending these Gaussian polynomial integrals to the real line changes them by less than any fixed inverse power of t. Their fourth and sixth moments are3 and15, so the correction is b4/8+5b3^2/24, exactly C_I. These are classical Gaussian moment identities, derived here within the uniform remainder bound.

Local concavity bounds the rest of the fractional band by exp(-c z^2). Outside it but in a fixed moderate charge compact, the exact critical geometry gives F<=-c t^2 after excluding the boundary by the separator. Normalizing by e^A/sqrt K, comparable to1/h, costs only powers of t by(148.25). For the remaining charges the density bound (137.21)–(137.23) is
$$
 \frac{g_y^0(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}u)}{g_y^0(0)}
 \le C\exp\left[t^2\left\{u^2-\frac{c u^4}{1+\eta u^2}\right\}\right],
                    \qquad |u|\ge M.
 \tag{148.31}
$$
Choosing fixed M sufficiently large makes the braces <=-B0 u^2 for any prescribed fixed B0, eventually for all |u|>=M. The negative-side field exp(-hr) only helps. The Jacobian divided by1/h is O(t^2); fixed polynomial charge weights cost powers of t and u. The tails are therefore smaller than every fixed inverse power of t, with no Q prefactor. This proves the second formula in(148.27). The same proof bounds any fixed local-variable moment, as needed later.

Since C_B,C_I=O(t^-2), taking logarithms in(148.27) gives
$$
 \log(J_I/J_B)=\Lambda+C_I-C_B+O(t^{-3}).
 \tag{148.32}
$$
This statement alone is a comparator result. The next two sections supply the new quantitative original-model return.

### 148.5 同一实鞍点上的非中心插值

The o(1) relative local-limit argument in (146.40) is insufficient. We instead interpolate the exact noncentral transforms at the SAME centered real energy saddle z=z(r^2). For theta in[0,1] put m_theta=rd-theta e_H and
$$
 \mathcal K_\theta(w)
 =-\tfrac12\log\det(I-2wA_0)+w m_\theta^T(I-2wA_0)^{-1}m_\theta
                                    +\tfrac12\delta\sigma^2w^2.
 \tag{148.33}
$$
Let f_r^theta(H_y) be its exact energy density. Theta=0 is centered and theta=1 is the actual e_H. The determinant, noise, observation H_y and real tilt are identical for all theta. With R_w=(I-2wA_0)^-1,
$$
 \partial_\theta\mathcal K_\theta(w)=-2w e_H^T R_w m_\theta,
 \quad
 \partial_w\partial_\theta\mathcal K_\theta(w)=-2 e_H^T R_w^2m_\theta.
 \tag{148.34}
$$
The second identity uses (wR_w)'=R_w^2. It is exact even when A_0 is singular.

For |r|<=M sqrt(eta/delta), ||m_theta||<=C_M(sqrt eta+delta^5). Set b_e=C_M delta^5(sqrt eta+delta^5). The vertical resolvent bound yields
$$
 |\partial_\theta\mathcal K_\theta(z)|\le C|z|b_e,
 \quad
 |\partial_\theta\mathcal K_\theta(z+i\xi/\sqrt\delta)
       -\partial_\theta\mathcal K_\theta(z)|
                        \le Cb_e|\xi|/\sqrt\delta.
 \tag{148.35}
$$
In particular |z|b_e<=C_M delta^4 eventually, since eta<=1 and |z|<=C(eta+sqrt delta)/delta. This already bounds the real exponential change at absolute log precision.

For the prefactor define
$$
 L_\theta(\xi)=\mathcal K_\theta(z+i\xi/\sqrt\delta)
                -\mathcal K_\theta(z)-i\xi H_y/\sqrt\delta,
 \quad p_\theta=\frac1{2\pi}\int e^{L_\theta}d\xi.
 \tag{148.36}
$$
This uses the SAME z for all theta; it is not a separately optimized energy saddle. Although H_y need not be the theta-tilted mean, its phase factor has modulus one. The real tilted covariance is independent of theta and retains the same variance block. Noncentrality only adds a nonpositive term to the modulus of its quadratic-form characteristic function. Hence |exp L_theta| is bounded by the SAME block envelope in(148.15), for every theta and frequency.

Differentiate exp L_theta in theta and use(148.35) UNDER this common envelope. Integrating first in theta and frequency gives
$$
 |p_1-p_0|\le Cb_e/\sqrt\delta\le C_M\delta^{9/2}.
 \tag{148.37}
$$
There is no uncontrolled exp(|Delta K|) at large frequency: interpolation bounds the derivative of each actual normalized tilted transform instead. The positive lower bound in (148.15) p0>=c makes (148.37) a relative bound. The exact density-change formula at that same real tilt then proves
$$
 \sup_{|r|\le M\sqrt{\eta/\delta},|y|\le R}
 \left|\frac{f_r^e(H_y)}{f_r^0(H_y)}-1\right|
 \le C_M\delta^4,
 \qquad t^2\delta^4=\eta^2\delta^3\to0.
 \tag{148.38}
$$
This is a quantitative replacement of (146.40). It includes r=0 and both charge signs. No inverse sigma, independent mean optimization, unknown local-limit rate or Gaussian energy-charge independence is used.

The global density tail (148.31) also holds for actual e. Its proof uses the same real negative energy tilt and full noise, and its denominator at zero is comparable to delta^-1/2. Thus the omitted tails, relative to either competing mass, are below every fixed t power. On the fixed moderate region (148.38) multiplies both integrals by1+O(delta^4). Let
$$
 M_0(y)=\sigma\sqrt{\delta/V_H}\,g_y^0(0)\asymp\sigma.
$$
The exact Gaussian raw region numerators with the ACTUAL e are sigma sqrt(delta/V_H) times the corresponding integrals of exp(-hr)g_y^e(-r). Therefore
$$
 N_G^B=\frac{M_0}h\{1+C_B+O(t^{-4}+\delta^4)\},
$$
$$
 N_G^I=\frac{M_0}h e^\Lambda
                    \{1+C_I+O(t^{-3}+\delta^4)\}.
 \tag{148.39}
$$
Superpolynomially small t tails are absorbed in the displayed remainders. These are direct region normalizations of size sigma/h, without division by the positive-sign majority.

### 148.6 逐区域的原始计数和完整选择回接

The growing-field domination remains pointwise on every original tuple:
$$
 hD\le\eta D^2+h^2/(4\eta),\qquad h^2/(4\eta)=O(t^2).
 \tag{148.40}
$$
At a_+=(2V)^-1+2eta, the joint energy-Fourier estimate of Chapter 137 controls fixed modal, likelihood-score and charge moments by P(Q)exp(Ct^2), uniformly for widths in[sigma/2,2sigma]. The score insertions refer to ONE conditional energy integral: the variance block pays frequency powers and the normalized Gaussian noise insertion has only polynomial charge/frequency cost. Thus the same bound at(148.40) introduces no inverse sigma. This is the joint interface already stated quantitatively in (146.44), not its mere leading conditional convergence.

The original central high-cell lift, uniform over EVERY exact low tuple, obeys
$$
 |\log(\hbox{lifted density}/\phi_C)|\le\mathcal E_Q,
 \quad |D-D_G|\le\mathcal E_Q,
 \quad |T-T_G|/\sigma\le\mathcal E_Q,
 \quad \mathcal E_Q=P(Q)e^{-bQ^3}.
 \tag{148.41}
$$
Here T_G=(sum_H(Y_j-e_j)^2-V)/sqrt(delta), with full V and original e. The positive payments are c_q/2-l, c_q-2zeta-l and the high Stirling margin. Full low probabilities are summed only after this uniform comparison; no separate low tuple or environment is selected for different bounds.

Across a central cell the linear/quadratic insertion changes by a polynomial times mathcal E_Q. Writing b0=(T-T_G)/sigma and u0=(T_G-y)/sigma, the likelihood log change is -b0u0-b0^2/2. Young's inequality absorbs its exponential absolute error into a width sigma/sqrt(1-C mathcal E_Q). The exact derivative of the likelihood with respect to log width is twice its normalized squared-residual score; integration of that identity and the joint bound after(148.40) pay the width change without an inverse-sigma derivative. Consequently the absolute lifted measure error, with any fixed polynomial charge weight, is at most
$$
 \sigma P(Q)\exp[-bQ^3+Ct^2].
 \tag{148.42}
$$
This explicit estimate is the count bound of Chapter 146; its new precision payment is given below.

For excluded tuples use D^2<=2n_gE+2(sum e_j)^2. Completing the square in the SAME E and using(148.40) bounds the full quadratic/field/likelihood insertion by
$$
 \exp\{Ct^2+2a_+(\sum e_j)^2+2a_+n_gH_y
                         +4a_+^2n_g^2\delta\sigma^2\}
       \exp\{-(E-H_y)^2/(4\delta\sigma^2)\}.
 \tag{148.43}
$$
Its prefactor log is O(Q^(7/2))+O(t^2). The raw excluded-binomial tail is P(Q)exp(-cQ^4). Fixed count polynomials cost at most exp(C_pQ^3), and dividing by sigma costs only O(Q^3) by the original noise margin. The excluded contribution remains exp(-c'Q^4) after normalization by sigma. Gaussian excluded cells obey the same payment. This bound is on every tuple; no unconditioned supercritical Gaussian integral is substituted.

Both region denominators in(148.39) are comparable to sigma/h. The h,h^-1 factors and t^2 are polynomially bounded in Q: eventually eta is between sqrt(delta) and1, c delta^(1/4)<=h<=C delta^-1/2 and t^2=o(Q^(1/2)). Thus the central/excluded relative error, multiplied by t^2, still tends to zero exponentially. More explicitly it is bounded by P(Q)exp(-bQ^3+Ct^2), after changing the fixed polynomial and b. No O(log Q) is divided by arbitrarily slow t^2.

A cut disagreement at D=0 occupies |D_G|<=mathcal E_Q and has raw mass O(sigma mathcal E_Q), hence relative mass O(h mathcal E_Q). At the separator it occupies a strip of the same width in a fixed action-gap interval, with an additional exp(-ct^2). Multiplication by t^2 leaves both negligible. This covers cut atoms and all lattice offsets; h/B and sqrt K/B are exponentially small. Each region comparison is therefore relative to its OWN mass with error o(t^-2). The same reasoning with higher fixed moments retains the uniform moment bounds needed for selection. Neither an inverse minority probability nor the total-law TV error is used.

Now let nu_B,nu_I be the exact PRODUCT count posterior normalized to the two regions. The just-established bounds, or the region moment theorem of Chapter 146 on the same sets, give uniformly bounded fixed moments of X=-hD on B and Z=sqrt K(-D-r_-) on I. From (148.12),
$$
 E_{\nu_B}|L_x(k)-1|
 \le C\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\varepsilon/h^2\}
 \le C\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\delta^6/\eta^3\},
$$
$$
 E_{\nu_I}|L_x(k)-1|
 \le C\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\eta\delta^4+\delta^5/\eta\}.
 \tag{148.44}
$$
The second follows from D^2<=2r_-^2+2Z^2/K. These SAME-law estimates are sufficient at the new precision, because
$$
 t^2\delta^5=\eta^2\delta^4\to0,\quad
 t^2\delta^6/\eta^3=\delta^5/\eta=\delta^{9/2}/t\to0,
$$
$$
 t^2\eta\delta^4=\eta^3\delta^3\to0,\quad
 t^2\delta^5/\eta=\eta\delta^4\to0,
 \qquad t^2q^{-1/2}\to0.
 \tag{148.45}
$$
No cancellation of independent bounds is needed. The exact selected normalizers are N_P^B=N_Q^B E_nuB L and N_P^I=N_Q^I E_nuI L. Hence each differs from its original product count counterpart by relative o(t^-2), with the outside labels and full finite coefficient (148.11) retained. The global upper bound on L pays all tail strips as well.

Combining(148.27),(148.38)--(148.45) proves both selected-region expansions
$$
 N_P^B=\frac{M_0}h\{1+C_B+o(t^{-2})\},\qquad
 N_P^I=\frac{M_0}h e^\Lambda\{1+C_I+o(t^{-2})\}.
 \tag{148.46}
$$
For clarity, a simultaneous bound for the absolute log-odds remainder in(148.1), on each fixed class and parameter compact, is
$$
 C\{t^{-3}+\delta^4+\delta^5+q^{-1/2}
                +\delta^6/\eta^3+\eta\delta^4+\delta^5/\eta\}
                  +P(Q)e^{-bQ^3+Ct^2}.
 \tag{148.47}
$$
The superpolynomially small local and global t tails have been absorbed in t^-3. Multiplying every term by t^2 gives zero in the limit by(148.38),(148.45) and the strict exponential margin. This is a quantitative original-model bridge, not a reference-Gaussian formula alone. Taking logarithms in(148.46) proves(148.1).

### 148.7 修正系数与实际等质量外场

At bounded Lambda the exact geometry of Chapter 146 gives kappa->kappa_c, r_-/r_sc->w0 and K/(2eta)->1. From (148.21)--(148.23), uniformly there,
$$
 \ell'(0)/\eta\to1,\quad \ell''(r_-^2)=-\delta m^{-2}(1+o(1)),
$$
$$
 F'''(r_-)=-12w_0\sqrt{\delta\eta}/m\,(1+o(1)),\qquad
 F''''(r_-)=-12\delta/m^2\,(1+o(1)).
 \tag{148.48}
$$
For the third derivative the term8r_-^3 ell''' is smaller than the displayed term by O(eta); for the fourth the additional terms48r_-^2 ell''' and16r_-^4 ell'''' have relative sizes O(eta) and O(eta^2). The finite-noise factor2C2/(2C2+sigma^2) tends to1 only here, after its exact presence in the profile and coefficient definitions has been respected. No faster sigma rate is required.

For the boundary, kappa_c^2=8/27 gives t^2 C_B=2/(kappa_c^2 m^2)+o(1)=27/(4m^2)+o(1). The two interior terms separately give
$$
 t^2\frac{F''''}{8K^2}=-\frac3{8m^2}+o(1),\qquad
 t^2\frac{5(F''')^2}{24K^3}=\frac5{2m^2}+o(1).
 \tag{148.49}
$$
Their sum is17/(8m^2); subtracting27/(4m^2) gives -37/(8m^2). This independently verifies (148.3), including its sign. These limiting numbers interpret the exact finite coefficients; they do not justify replacing h_W by a limiting quartic field.

It remains to justify field inversion at the finer scale. The exact branch identities from Chapter 146 are r_h=-1/K, K_h=G'''/K and
$$
 \Lambda_h=-r_-+1/h-G'''/(2K^2)
                 =-r_-\{1+O(t^{-2})\}.
 \tag{148.50}
$$
The fifth-derivative bound proves that C=C_I-C_B has a genuine field derivative satisfying
$$
 |C_h|\le C/(h_{\rm sc}t^2).
 \tag{148.51}
$$
One direct check is to scale r=r_sc w and h=h_sc kappa. On the branch w_kappa is bounded because its scaled curvature is bounded away from zero. The normalized third and fourth derivatives b3,b4 and their kappa derivatives are O(t^-1), O(t^-2), respectively; differentiating them uses F'''' and F'''''. Thus partial_kappa C_I=O(t^-2). Also partial_h C_B=-2C_B/h with h comparable to h_sc. This proves(148.51) without differentiating an o(1) formula.

Consequently Psi_coex=Lambda+C is strictly decreasing on the fixed local branch for sufficiently large levels: its derivative is -r_-(1+O(t^-2)), since r_-h_sc is comparable to t^2. Its endpoint values straddle every bounded lambda, as in Chapter 146, because the action difference is of order t^2 while the log width is O(log t) and C=O(t^-2). It therefore has a unique measurable root h_corr(lambda,y). Formula(148.1) gives actual log odds lambda+o(t^-2) there. Smoothness of the logistic map on bounded arguments proves(148.10).

For lambda=0, (148.50)--(148.51) first give h_corr(0)-h_W=O(1/(r_Wt^2)). On this interval r_-/r_W=1+O(t^-4), since r_h=-1/K and eta r_W^2 is comparable to t^2. Thus integrating (148.50), while using(148.51) to control the change in C, yields
$$
 h_{\rm corr}(0)-h_W=C(h_W,y)/r_W+o((r_Wt^2)^{-1}).
 \tag{148.52}
$$
For fixed empirical data,y,xi, the exact finite ratio N_P^I(h)/N_P^B(h) is strictly decreasing wherever these positive sums are defined: its log derivative is -E_I(-D)+E_B(-D)<0, because all I charges exceed all B charges. No derivative approximation to the original count error is needed. Apply (148.1) at the two fields solving Psi_coex=+epsilon/t^2 and -epsilon/t^2. Their exact log odds have opposite signs for sufficiently large levels, uniformly on the good classes. Hence there is one exact equal-region-mass field between them. Equation(148.50) makes the bracket width O(epsilon/(r_Wt^2)). Taking the uniform remainder limit and then epsilon->0 proves h_equal^P-h_corr(0)=o((r_Wt^2)^-1). Combining with(148.52) proves(148.4).

All estimates are uniform over xi in its permissible compact, while h_W,r_W and C are separator-independent. Thus any two such exact equality fields differ by o((r_Wt^2)^-1). The stronger intuitive reason is the exponentially suppressed middle action gap, but no unproved derivative of that error is needed for this conclusion.

Let h_A denote the exact finite equal-height field, A(h_A,y)=0, with r_A,K_A its branch quantities. The statement (146.38)–(146.39) of Chapter 146 is
$$
 h_W-h_A=\frac{\log[h_A\sqrt{2\pi/K_A}]}{r_A}+o(1/r_A),
 \quad
 \kappa_W-\kappa_A=\frac{\log t}{m^2w_0t^2}(1+o(1))>0.
 \tag{148.53}
$$
The correction (148.4) is negative of order1/(r_Wt^2), far smaller than that positive leading shift. Equation(148.53)'s coarser remainder is not silently upgraded to the precision of(148.4); we do not combine it into an unjustified high-order expansion around h_A or kappa_c. Finite eta, output or noise corrections to kappa_A-kappa_c can still be much larger than the coexistence window.

### 148.8 适用范围与文献对应

端点展开与内部 Laplace 积分的四阶导数、三阶导数平方系数属于经典渐近方法，分别参照 Nemes 和 Kirwin；本章的数组依赖剖面、收缩曲率与指数窄噪声要求 (148.17)–(148.24) 的一致导数控制，不能由逐个固定剖面的渐近式直接替代。两篇论文的条件、版本与适用边界见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。完整选择的条件乘积表示与总方差局部界保留第 143 章的文献归属。

结论同时适用于有界 $\Lambda$、紧输出范围和紧含于 $(0,\sqrt{2/3})$ 的分隔符集合，允许 $t\to\infty$ 任意缓慢、$\eta\to0$，噪声仅受 (148.7) 的原严格余量约束。没有要求经验参数 $m$ 收敛到确定常数，也不将精确有限等高点或等权点替换为极限四次剖面的中心。无界竞争坐标、趋近区间端点的分隔符、其它先验和动力学亚稳态不在本定理范围内。

## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）

## 149. 有限有理共振网格与任意固定二次对数带宽

固定的逐坐标收缩常数只能抵消有限范围的 $\exp(cQ^2)$ 频率体积。本章将收缩常数按固定 $c>0$ 选取，把仍须保留的有理共振纳入一个固定公共网格。每个 Gauss 系数与 Poisson 模式一起进入细化对偶网格；先求这个高精度 Gaussian 网格的和，就不必支付“网格分母的坐标数次方”。原数据中的总数可测选池则为整个频带提供同一组中心的算术控制。

以下推导保留实际 pair/path 实验、原始确定支持的一致性、完整选择计数后验、经验中心、全部低频／外部坐标、有限噪声校正与共用残差。常数可依赖固定原始参数、固定 $c$ 与两个正带宽比较常数；结论不对随 $Q$ 增长的 $c$ 作一致性断言。这里给出普通数学证明，未作 Lean 形式化认证。

### 149.1 任意固定二次对数带宽下的完整后验

**定理 149.1（固定二次对数尺度的完整方差熵极限）。** For every fixed c>0, every original legal deterministic floor sequence and

$$
 R=cQ^2,\quad \mathcal B=q/Q^{11/4},\quad \rho=\sigma\mathcal B,
 \qquad 0<c_-\le\rho e^R\le c_+<\infty,             \tag{149.1}
$$

the SAME original selected full-q posterior-varentropy law satisfies, separately for actual independent pairs and paths, uniformly over fixed true supports of size q,

$$
 \boxed{\int_{\mathbb R}f_x(y)|D_x(y)-R_*(y)|\,dy
                     \longrightarrow0}            \tag{149.2}
