## 151. 分离有理弧与次立方对数带宽的完整后验

第 149 章把有限有理共振嵌入固定公共倍数网格。本章在 $R/Q^2$ 增长时直接保留既约分数：不同弧以分母平方的倒数分离，不支付所有分母的最小公倍数。非零弧只展开一个指数占据的宏观坐标块，其余坐标保留为精确的带标记期望；零弧展开原来的全部 $J$，因此仍得到完整连续参考律。这是同一个特征函数在不同频区上的两种精确表达。

结论覆盖每个确定的 $Q^2\le R=o(Q^3)$ 序列与 $\rho\asymp e^{-R}$。下文逐项控制分母、选池、共同经验响应、完整 Fourier 积分以及原始后验的非线性回接，所有常数仅依赖原始固定参数和两个固定正带宽比较常数。未显式标明依赖的常数 $C$ 不依赖 $R/Q^2$、分母截止或池数。本章给出普通数学推导，未作 Lean 形式化认证。

### 151.1 次立方对数带宽的完整后验结论

**定理 151.1（次立方对数带宽下的完整方差熵极限）。** Let R=R_Q be any deterministic sequence with

$$
 Q^2\le R=o(Q^3),\qquad 0<c_-\le\rho e^R\le c_+<\infty,
 \qquad \rho=\sigma\mathcal B,\quad\mathcal B=q/Q^{11/4}.       \tag{151.1}
$$

For every original legal deterministic floor sequence, separately in the actual independent-pair and actual path experiments, uniformly over deterministic admissible true supports of size q,

$$
 \int_{\mathbb R} f_x(y)|D_x(y)-R_*(y)|\,dy\longrightarrow0
                                                        \tag{151.2}
$$

in original raw-data probability. All objects are the original ones:

$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q/Q^{5/2},\quad
 T=\mathcal B^{-1}\sum_j(R_j-\mu_j)^2-V/\sqrt\delta,\quad
 Y=T+\sigma G,
$$
$$
 A=V_H/\sqrt\delta,\quad \nu_0=2\sum_{j\in H}w_j^2,\quad
 \kappa_3=8\sum_{j\in H}w_j^3,\quad \Lambda=\nu_0+\sigma^2,
$$
$$
 C_x=A^2\kappa_3/\Lambda^3-2A\nu_0/\Lambda^2,\quad
 D_x(y)=Vpost_x(y)-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xy,
$$
$$
 R_*(y)=29/6-3\sqrt2+(3\sqrt2+8/\sqrt3-9)y^2/\nu,
 \qquad \nu=2g_0.                                      \tag{151.3}
$$

Here Vprior is the exact selected full-count prior surprise variance, m_x=E_xY is exact, and G is the SAME residual throughout. The full selected-q prior, all count multiplicities, low/outside coordinates, empirical centers, physical H and finite coefficients are retained. In particular

$$
 \int Vpost_x(y)f_x(y)\,dy-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xm_x
                  \longrightarrow8/\sqrt3-25/6.          \tag{151.4}
$$

This proves each sequence in(151.1) by explicit bounds, not by diagonalizing Chapter 149's fixed-c theorem. It makes no claim at R of order Q^3, no zero-noise claim, no sharpness or necessity claim.

### 151.2 按频区选择展开坐标与固定正则性

The fixed-c proof embedded rational arcs in a common lcm grid. That embedding is unnecessary. Reduced fractions with denominator at most B_Q have separation at least B_Q^-2, whereas the lcm can be much larger. On nonzero arcs we expand ONLY an exponentially occupied macroscopic block; every remaining coordinate stays in an exact marked expectation. At the zero arc we expand the original full J. These are two identities for the SAME characteristic function on disjoint frequency regions, not two different probability models. This distinction removes the obstruction from small J variances divided by a growing denominator.

To avoid conflict with physical B^2, write the denominator cutoff as $\mathfrak b$. Put lambda=Q^3, a_0=(1+r)/2, b_0=(1-r)/2 and alpha=lim P/Q. The original scales are

$$
 \phi=a_0\log(1+r)+b_0\log(1-r)>0,\quad
 c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta>0,
$$
$$
 \log q=c_q\lambda+O(1),\quad
 \log M=(\phi/\beta)\lambda+O(1),\quad q/M=e^{-\phi\lambda+O(1)}.
                                                               \tag{151.5}
$$

Use the explicit fixed constants justified from the exact original count-line rate in (149.6)–(149.9):

$$
 \kappa=\min(1,c_q,\phi)/1000,\quad H_I=2/a_0+2\alpha^2/b_0,
$$
$$
 a=\min\{1/4,a_0/4,b_0/(4\alpha),\sqrt{\kappa/(4H_I)}\},
 \quad\mathcal C=\{|j|\le\lfloor aQ^2\rfloor\}.                \tag{151.6}
$$

This is a proof block inside the original fixed count truncation, not a changed H. Chapter 68's rate has I(0)=I'(0)=0 and
I''(u)=1/(a_0+u)+alpha^2/(b_0+alpha u). Thus I<=kappa/8 on this interval. Its exact relative one/two-row estimates give

$$
 b_{occ}\le CQ^2\{q^{-1}e^{\kappa\lambda/4}+Q^9/M\},\qquad
 d_j\ge d_*:=qe^{-\kappa\lambda}\quad(j\in\mathcal C),         \tag{151.7}
$$

outside an event of that probability and the once-paid common calibration failure. These bounds include actual path dependence. No row-independence assumption is added. The line stays in a fixed positive neighborhood of its original lambda-scaled count coordinates, so its floor and rate hypotheses do not depend on R.

Keep J={j:d_j>=Q^3600}, E=J^c exactly as in Chapter 149. The block is contained in J. There are at most CQ^2 physical groups. After16 central envelope factors and any two marked factors, at least aQ^2 block factors remain. The same-array estimates (145.39) and Section 147.9 give

$$
 d_{max}\le Cq/Q^3,\quad \epsilon=\max_j w_j\asymp Q^{-1/4},\quad
 \sum_Jw_j^2=O(1),\quad w_j=d_j/\mathcal B,
$$
$$
 a_x=\|dP_x/dQ_x-1\|_2=O_P(Q^{-5/2}),\quad
 a_j=(\mu_j-m_j)/\sqrt{d_j},\quad |a_j|\le a_x,
 \quad \|wa\|\le Ca_x.                                      \tag{151.8}
$$

As usual one first localizes a_x<=KQ^-5/2 for fixed K, proves bounds uniform there, and releases K. No R-dependent localization is imposed. The central core inside C gives
$\int\prod_{j\in\mathcal C}(1+4s^2w_j^2)^{-1/4}ds\le C$.
Indeed it contains c sqrt(Q) indices with w_j comparable Q^-1/4; their product is at most (1+cs^2/sqrt(Q))^-c' sqrt(Q). This also gives the one-reference tail used below. Constants depend only on the original regularity event.

### 151.3 增长分母下的统一收缩和分离有理弧

For the normalized integer Gaussian quadratic sum

$$
 F_{d,m,\mu}(\theta)=
 \frac{\sum_n e^{-(n-m)^2/(2d)}e^{2\pi i\theta(n-\mu)^2}}
      {\sum_n e^{-(n-m)^2/(2d)}},
$$

the elementary Gaussian/Gauss proof (149.10)–(149.11) gives, with absolute constant100,

$$
 |F_{d,m,\mu}(p/b+v)|\le100\{b^{-1/2}(1+d^2v^2)^{-1/4}+d^{-1/4}\}
                                                               \tag{151.9}
$$

for gcd(p,b)=1, b<=floor(sqrt d), |v|<=1/[b floor(sqrt d)], uniformly in both real shifts. This statement has no fixed-b or fixed-eta qualification. Its proof uses the complete Gauss bound sqrt(2/b), Gaussian Poisson summation and
sum_k exp[-A(k/b-x)^2]<=1+b sqrt(pi/A). Dirichlet's bound on v turns the second contribution into an absolute multiple of d^-1/4. Thus the explicit estimate, rather than a hidden threshold depending on eta, is what is reused.

Set

$$
 \eta=\exp[-(R+2Q^2)/(aQ^2)],\quad
 \mathfrak a=(400/\eta)^2,\quad \mathfrak b=\lceil\mathfrak a\rceil,
 \quad \zeta=\mathfrak a/d_* .                              \tag{151.10}
$$

Then log(mathfrak a)+log(mathfrak b)<=C+C R/Q^2=o(Q). In particular mathfrak b<=sqrt(d_*)/2 and 100d_*^-1/4<=eta/4 eventually, since log(d_*)=(c_q-kappa)lambda+O(1). Outside the union of the intervals

$$
 |\theta-p/b|\le\zeta,\qquad
 b\le\mathfrak b,\quad b\ge1,\quad p\in\mathbb Z,\quad (p,b)=1,
                                                               \tag{151.11}
$$

each block factor is at most eta. To see this, use its own d_j in Dirichlet's approximation. If that denominator exceeds mathfrak b, the first term of(151.9) is <=eta/4. Otherwise its rational center belongs to(151.11), and being outside gives |d_jv|>mathfrak a. The same first term is <=eta/4; the d_j^-1/4 term is <=eta/4. The use of the common wider radius mathfrak a/d_* is legitimate because d_j>=d_*.

Two distinct reduced fractions in(151.11), on the full real line rather than modulo one, have distance at least mathfrak b^-2. Thus all arcs are disjoint eventually, because

$$
 2\zeta\mathfrak b^2
 \le \exp[-(c_q-\kappa)\lambda+O(R/Q^2)+O(1)]\to0.           \tag{151.12}
$$

The unique zero fraction is0/1. There is no duplicate numerator convention, no discarded overlap and no lcm. The physical centers and widths are

$$
 t_{p,b}=2\pi(p/b)\mathcal B,\qquad
 S=2\pi\mathfrak a\mathcal B/d_*
   =2\pi\mathfrak a Q^{-11/4}e^{\kappa\lambda}.              \tag{151.13}
$$

For each sequence(151.1), eventually kappa lambda/2<=log S<=(5/4)kappa lambda. This is an explicit consequence of log mathfrak a=o(Q), not a fixed-c constant. The physical arcs I_{p,b}=[t_{p,b}-S,t_{p,b}+S] are disjoint by(151.12).

### 151.4 次立方偏移下的实际可测选池

Put

$$
 L=10(R+\sqrt{Q^3\log Q})+20\log Q.
                                                               \tag{151.14}
$$

Now L=o(lambda), L>=10Q^2, and L^2/lambda=o(lambda). Retain the explicit model constants from (149.16)–(149.22):

$$
 \alpha_0=\log(1+r),\quad\beta_0=\log(1-r),\quad
 \delta_*=[100(1+\alpha_0+|\beta_0|)]^{-1},
$$
$$
 D_*=9/\alpha_0+1,\quad C_*=D_*^2/(2a_0)+1/(2b_0)+1,\quad
 c_* =\min\{1/4,\delta_*^2/(64\sqrt{a_0b_0})\},
$$
$$
 m=\lceil c_*^{-1}Q^2e^{C_*L^2/\lambda}\rceil.                \tag{151.15}
$$

Consequently log m<=C+C log Q+C_*L^2/lambda=o(lambda). The original support contains the requisite predetermined disjoint lawful pairs for large Q, because2m/q tends to zero and the required class supplies a fixed positive fraction of the admissible true labels. The choices can depend on the fixed true support for a theoretical probability proof; they do not intervene in its posterior.

For clarity, the actual conditional law is re-stated. Reveal the complete parity record, all these pools' masks and positive/negative totals, all labels outside the pools and, in paths, the terminal label (in pairs, the arrivals). The original conditional slot weights are constant within each lawful pair. Jointly under this single sigma-field H_0,

$$
 (k_i,l_i)_{i\le m}\mid\mathcal H_0\sim
 \bigotimes_{i\le m}\{Bin(K_{i,+},1/2)\otimes Bin(K_{i,-},1/2)\}.
                                                               \tag{151.16}
$$

This follows from the exact original slot law: conditional path departure weights are
1_{chi(i)=s_t}[1+b_S(i)s_{t+1}]/M; class sums of b_S vanish and within-class reassignment preserves the preceding transition's parity. Pair departures have the same weights. Hence independent slot choices conditional on this common parity record disintegrate into the product kernel(151.16). It is not multiplication of separately derived marginals.

Choose the first pair whose REVEALED totals satisfy

$$
 |K_+-2a_0\lambda-9L/\alpha_0|\le\delta_*\sqrt\lambda,\qquad
 |K_--2b_0\lambda|\le\delta_*\sqrt\lambda .                  \tag{151.17}
$$

Then reveal every other pair's allocations. The chosen index is H_0-measurable and remains measurable. On {I=i}, integrate any bounded test function against the product kernel, first in all coordinates except i. The resulting conditional kernel for i is exactly its two factors in(151.16). Summing over the finite partition {I=i} proves the selected statement, also for measurable candidate target sets. There is no union over hidden allocations.

The success probability of the totals rule is quantitative throughout L=o(lambda). For a Poisson mean v lambda and |n-vlambda|<=v lambda/2, the exact rate has second derivative1/x, giving

$$
 P(Pois(v\lambda)=n)\ge(4\sqrt{v\lambda})^{-1}
                     e^{-(n-v\lambda)^2/(v\lambda)}.          \tag{151.18}
$$

This follows from the rate bound and the fixed Stirling inequality n!<=3sqrt(n)(n/e)^n. It does not truncate a moderate-deviation Taylor series. Every point in(151.17) meets this condition eventually, since L/lambda tends to zero. Summing the two windows gives one-pool success at least c_*exp(-C_*L^2/lambda).

The actual joint slot-to-Poisson bounded-event comparison costs

$$
 \tau_Q=C\{Q^3M^{-1/3}+mM^{-1/3}+m^2Q^3/M\}.                \tag{151.19}
$$

Indeed conditional categorical-to-independent-Poisson coupling in one slot has distance p(1-e^-p)<=p^2, for total selected probability p; summing over slots gives the m^2Q^3/M term. The parity pattern counts have the original1-dependent path bound, so deviations M^(2/3) cost CQ^3M^-1/3, and addition coupling of the means costs CmM^-1/3. Thus the existence event fails with probability at most exp(-Q^2)+tau_Q. The three logarithms in(151.19) are respectively -(phi/(3beta))lambda+O(log Q), the same plus o(lambda), and -(phi/beta)lambda+o(lambda). All tend to minus infinity. This comparison is not used as a posterior replacement.

With a_s,b_s,B_0 as in (149.21), favorable totals imply
t_raw=(a_sK_++b_sK_-)/2-log B_0 in[4L,5L], with K_+ in[a_0lambda,3a_0lambda] and K_- in[b_0lambda,3b_0lambda]. The errors are O(sqrt lambda)+O((q/M)(lambda+L))+O(1)=o(L). For the selected split,

$$
 X=a_s(k-K_+/2)+b_s(l-K_-/2),\quad
 P(|X|>L/2\mid\mathcal F)\le2e^{-L^2/(2C_s\lambda)},
$$
$$
 C_s=12(a_0\alpha_0^2+b_0\beta_0^2+1).                      \tag{151.20}
$$

This is the fair-binomial exponential-moment bound. It is at most2exp(-50Q/C_s) and tends to zero even at the lower endpoint. It is paid ONCE after measurable selection; multiplication by m would be unjustified and unnecessary.

### 151.5 固定删除的共同校准与全频带有理目标

The once-paid original all-array environment failure is

$$
 b_{env}=C\{q^{-1/2}+(CQ^9/M)\sqrt q+M^{-8}q^{-3/2}
                       +Q^3/q+Q/M+M^{-9}\}=o(1).            \tag{151.21}
$$

Only the chosen pair and a central anchor are deleted for the response calculation. All other pools stay in the outside family. The derivative of the Bernoulli mean equation in log multiplier is its variance, comparable q. Removing three terms changes the equation by at most3, and variance changes by at most an exponential of the multiplier displacement. Hence the outside calibration at integer mean q-1 differs from the full calibration by O(q^-1), uniformly for EVERY three-label deletion. This deterministic implication avoids any m-fold environment union. Use the resulting F-measurable outside enlargement, rather than conditioning the binomial kernel on the original nonmeasurable good-array event.

Let t_o,D_o be its multiplier and variance, p=t_oL_0/(1+t_oL_0), v=p(1-p), a_3=kappa_{3,o}/D_o. Then D_o asymp q, p in[1/4,3/4], |log(t_oB_0)|<=2q^-1/4, and the outside central membership n_0 asymp q/Q^3. The EXACT full-q inclusion is

$$
 p_*={L_0\sum_{h=0}^2 c_hE_{q-1-h}\over
                 \sum_{h=0}^2c_h(E_{q-h}+L_0E_{q-1-h})},
 \quad(c_0,c_1,c_2)=(1,L_u+L_v,L_uL_v).                     \tag{151.22}
$$

The fixed-order, fixed-offset Bernoulli ratio expansion in (132.14)–(132.16) and Section 147.7 uses only s in[-2,1]:
1-(s^2+a_3s)/(2D_o)+O(D_o^-2). Positive averaging of these four offsets preserves its uniform remainder even for the rare large pair odds. It yields

$$
 p_*=p_{ref}-(v/D_o)f_t(X)+O(q^{-2}),\quad

 f_t(X)={\sinh t\over\cosh t+\cosh X},
$$
$$
 t=\log t_o+(a_sK_++b_sK_-)/2.                              \tag{151.23}
$$

There is no growing deletion or growing local expansion order. Every actual central membership n in{n_0,n_0+1,n_0+2} is retained, with exact mu_0=np_* and d_0 asymp n.

The original compensated defect satisfies
|Qa_s+Pb_s|<=CQ(q/M+exp(-c_0Q^5)), gcd(P,Q)=1. For

$$
 H=Ql-Pk,\quad H^0=(QK_--PK_+)/2,\quad
 \bar X=(b_s/Q)(H-H^0),\quad
 |X-\bar X|\le\Delta_X:=CQ^3(q/M+e^{-c_0Q^5}),               \tag{151.24}
$$

the last bound holds on the whole selected support, not only typical fibers. Cyclic Fourier inversion for the positive binomial gives mass at most Q^-1(1+Ce^-cQ) for each residue modulo Q, and the negative binomial maximal atom is CQ^-3/2. Summing all preimages proves

$$
 \sup_hP(H=h\mid\mathcal F)\le CQ^{-5/2}.                   \tag{151.25}
$$

The constants are uniform in(151.17), because both totals remain within the same fixed multiples of lambda. No hidden projection fiber is lost.

For one sufficient common event define

$$
 U=e^{10\kappa\lambda},\quad
 V_R=R+\log\mathfrak b+\log Q,\quad
 N=\lceil1000\mathfrak b\rho^{-1}\sqrt{V_R}\rceil,
$$
$$
 \mathcal E(p)={4\pi^2\over\mathfrak b^2}
          \sum_{j\in\mathcal C}d_j\,dist(2p\mu_j,\mathbb Z)^2.
                                                               \tag{151.26}
$$

This artificial worst-spacing energy implies every needed b-specific block energy lower bound, since b<=mathfrak b. It is not an lcm grid or a new physical statistic. Notice log N=R+O(R/Q^2+log Q)=o(lambda).

On the selected good split,3L<=t<=6L and |bar X|<=L. A coarse plateau bound puts p_* near one of p_z=p_ref-vz/D_o, z in{-1,0,1}, with radius
r_Q=(C/q)(exp(-L)+Delta_X+q^-1). All three plateau candidates and all three memberships are retained. If E(p)<=U for1<=|p|<=N, the central term implies

$$
 |2pnp_*-h|\le C\mathfrak b\sqrt U/\sqrt n
                                                               \tag{151.27}
$$

for an integer h. Thus h/(2p) lies in an F-measurable interval about np_z of radius
w_Q=C n r_Q+C mathfrak b sqrt(U)/sqrt(n). Different rational VALUES with denominators at most2N are at least(2N)^-2 apart. Quantitatively

$$
 (2N)^2w_Q\le C\mathfrak b^2e^{2R}V_R
 \{Q^{-3}(e^{-L}+\Delta_X+q^{-1})
                 +\mathfrak b Q^{3/2}e^{5\kappa\lambda}/\sqrt q\}=o(1).
                                                               \tag{151.28}
$$

For the four terms, logarithmic upper bounds are respectively
-8R+O(log mathfrak b+log Q),
-phi lambda+2R+O(log mathfrak b+log Q),
-c_q lambda+2R+O(log mathfrak b+log Q), and
-(c_q/2-5kappa)lambda+2R+O(log mathfrak b+log Q).
All tend to minus infinity. This explicitly checks the enlarged N^-2 condition. There are at most nine target VALUES for the ENTIRE band, regardless of denominator b, numerator sign or unreduced representation. There is no B-fold or N-fold raw-data probability union.

For each target return to the exact response(151.23). Equation(151.27), including its O(q^-2) remainder and(151.24), gives a value interval for f_t(bar X) of radius

$$
 \varepsilon_Q=C\mathfrak b Q^{9/2}e^{5\kappa\lambda}/\sqrt q
                                      +C/q+C\Delta_X.         \tag{151.29}
$$

No plateau error is used at this thin scale. Direct differentiation gives

$$
 f_t''(X)={\sinh t(\cosh^2X-\cosh t\cosh X-2)
                        \over(\cosh t+\cosh X)^3},\quad
 -\partial_H^2 f_t(\bar X)\ge{\beta_0^2\over128Q^2}e^{-6L}.
                                                               \tag{151.30}
$$

Indeed cosh t>=2cosh X and sinh t>=cosh t/2 here. The ratio of(151.29) to the curvature lower bound tends to zero: its first log bound is
-(c_q/2-5kappa)lambda+6L+log mathfrak b+O(log Q); the other two have margins c_q and phi. Since L=o(lambda), all are strict. Three integer H sites in the same value interval would contradict the strong-concavity secant gap at the middle site, at least one half of the curvature lower bound. Combining(151.25), the measurable selected kernel and once-paid failures proves

$$
 \sup_S P_S\{\min_{1\le|p|\le N}\mathcal E(p)\le U\}
 \le e^{-Q^2}+\tau_Q+2e^{-L^2/(2C_s\lambda)}
                         +b_{env}+b_{reg}+CQ^{-5/2}=o(1).     \tag{151.31}
$$

The regularity localization b_reg is the original one and is released in the usual fixed-K order. The occupancy event(151.7) is intersected afterwards. Both experiments satisfy these separate uniform bounds. No random independent empirical phase or separately chosen calibration appears.

### 151.6 每条非零有理弧上的精确混合恒等式

Work first in the SAME lattice comparison law Q_x^lat: independent normalized integer Gaussians on J and the original exact binomials on E, with original T and G. Let s_lat be its exactly centered count surprise, W=s_lat+G^2/2, and tilt this SAME law by exp(uW), normalized for real u near zero. Hold physical output y fixed. Write tau=1-u.

On a nonzero reduced arc p/b, expand only C and put K=all coordinates outside C, including J minus C as integer Gaussians and E as exact binomials. Its exact tilted expectation is

$$
 H_{K,p,b}(u,s)=E_{K,u}\exp\{(2\pi ip/b)\sum_K(R_j^2-2\mu_jR_j)
                   +(is/\mathcal B)\sum_K(R_j-\mu_j)^2\}.
                                                               \tag{151.32}
$$

The quadratic rational phase in this factor is essential. Neither its low groups nor its Gaussian coordinates are dropped. It has modulus at most1 at u=0. Its first two normalized real derivatives are centered-surprise expectations with a unit-modulus phase, so their absolute values are bounded by CQ^4 from the original fixed moment estimates, uniformly in b,p,s. Centering a sum of independent surprises removes their deterministic log normalizers. No factor exp(C|K|) is required.

Define the exact coefficients and modes

$$
 \gamma_{p,b}(r)=b^{-1}\sum_{z\bmod b}e^{2\pi i(pz^2-rz)/b},
 \quad |\gamma_{p,b}(r)|\le1,
$$
$$
 \xi_{p,b,h,j}=(2\pi\sqrt{d_j}/b)(h_j-2p\mu_j),\quad
 \eta_{p,b}=2\pi p\rho/b,\quad h\in\mathbb Z^{\mathcal C},
$$
$$
 c_{\mathcal C}(u)=\prod_{j\in\mathcal C}
 {\sqrt{2\pi d_j/\tau}\over\sum_n e^{-\tau(n-m_j)^2/(2d_j)}},
$$
$$
 z_{p,b,h}=e^{(2\pi ip/b)(\sum_{all}\mu_j^2-B^2V)}
                    e^{i\sum_{\mathcal C}\xi_{p,b,h,j}m_j/\sqrt{d_j}}.
$$

For t_phys=t_{p,b}+s the exact summand is

$$
 \Psi_{p,b,h}(u,s)=\left(\prod_{\mathcal C}\gamma_{p,b}(h_j\bmod b)\right)
 c_{\mathcal C}(u)z_{p,b,h}
 e^{is(\sum_{\mathcal C}w_ja_j^2-V/\sqrt\delta)}
 \prod_{\mathcal C}\left({\tau\over\tau-2isw_j}\right)^{1/2}
$$
$$
 {}\times\exp\left[-\frac12\sum_{\mathcal C}
 { (\xi_{p,b,h,j}-2sw_ja_j)^2\over\tau-2isw_j}
              -{(\eta_{p,b}+\sigma s)^2\over2\tau}\right]
 H_{K,p,b}(u,s).                                             \tag{151.33}
$$

To prove it, expand exp(2pi ipR_j^2/b) in its finite Fourier series, leave its linear term -4pi ipmu_jR_j/b intact, and apply real Gaussian Poisson summation in each j in C. The residue r and Poisson index k combine bijectively as h=r-bk. Gaussian integration supplies the displayed determinant, displacement and phase. The global intercept uses mathcal B V/sqrt(delta)=B^2V and contains every mu_j^2. All normalizations are those of the same real tilt. The inverse phase exp[-i(t_{p,b}+s)y] is independent of u. This establishes the identity for each finite Q before any estimate.

At the zero arc0/1 use the SAME identity with C replaced by the whole original J and K replaced by E. Then gamma_{0,1}=1. Its h=0 term is precisely the continuous-J reference with exact E, all noncentral shifts, original intercept and SAME G, multiplied by c_J(u). No continuity of the choice of expansion is needed: the frequency partition is disjoint and independent of u. This proves the hybrid representation without substituting a partial Gaussian physical law.

### 151.7 两个实标记与细化对偶网格的统一求和

Write

$$
 P_{\mathcal C}(s)=\prod_{\mathcal C}(1-2isw_j)^{-1/2},\qquad
 A_{p,b,h}(s)=\sum_{\mathcal C}
 {(\xi_{p,b,h,j}-2sw_ja_j)^2\over1+4s^2w_j^2},\quad
 a_{p,b}(s)=\min_h A_{p,b,h}(s).
$$

Differentiate the exact real identity(151.33), through order2. Each determinant log derivative is bounded by an absolute constant per expanded coordinate. For a real z, the modulus of the derivative of -z^2/[2(tau-2isw)] is at most z^2/[2(1+4s^2w^2)], and its second derivative at tau=1 is at most z^2/(1+4s^2w^2). Summing these gives a polynomial in A of fixed degree. Residual differentiation gives a fixed polynomial in eta_{p,b}+sigma s. Both are absorbed in half the Gaussian decay. The normalized outside derivatives were bounded in(151.32). Real Gaussian Poisson differentiation gives

$$
 |c_{\mathcal C}(0)-1|+|c'_{\mathcal C}(0)|+|c''_{\mathcal C}(0)|
                            \le CQ^4e^{-c_0d_*},             \tag{151.34}
$$

where fixed polynomial factors in d_* are absorbed by decreasing c_0. All individual d_j>=d_*. Thus, conservatively,

$$
 |\partial_u^k\Psi_{p,b,h}(0,s)|
 \le CQ^{12}|P_{\mathcal C}(s)|
             e^{-[A_{p,b,h}(s)+(\eta_{p,b}+\sigma s)^2]/4},
 \qquad k=0,1,2.                                           \tag{151.35}
$$

This bound is uniform in the growing b and every p. No derivative of gamma occurs, and no derivative of a C0 approximation is used. The same proof at zero gives C Q^12 with J in place of C, including c_J's error at scale exp(-cQ^3600). These are normalized real-temperature derivatives of the SAME W, not separately selected noise or surprise marks. For each finite Q, positive sigma, Gaussian tuple tails and finite E sums justify the real derivatives before taking limits; no complex zero-free region is required.

For |s|<=S the one-coordinate precision on the nonzero-arc fine grid satisfies

$$
 T_j(s,b):={d_j\over b^2(1+4s^2d_j^2/\mathcal B^2)}
 \ge c\mathfrak b^{-2}
       \min\{d_*,\mathcal B^2/(S^2d_{max})\}
$$
$$
 \ge c\mathfrak b^{-2}
       \min\{qe^{-\kappa\lambda},\,qQ^3e^{-2\kappa\lambda}/\mathfrak a^2\}
 \ge e^{(c_q-3\kappa)\lambda}=:T_*                         \tag{151.36}
$$

eventually. The first inequality follows by considering whether4s^2d_j^2/mathcal B^2<=1. The second uses the EXACT S in(151.13) and d_max<=Cq/Q^3. The last uses log mathfrak a+log mathfrak b=o(Q). This is why only the occupied block is expanded on nonzero arcs. It would not follow uniformly from d_j>=Q^3600 when b grows exponentially in o(Q).

For any translated integer grid with precision T, the Gaussian sum is maximized at an integer translate, by its positive Poisson cosine coefficients, and is at most1+Ce^-cT when T>=1. Split the exponent in(151.35), keeping its minimum in one part and summing the other over ALL h. The product over at most CQ^2 coordinates is bounded by
(1+Ce^-cT_*)^{CQ^2}<=2. Consequently

$$
 \sum_{h\in\mathbb Z^{\mathcal C}}|\partial_u^k\Psi_{p,b,h}(0,s)|
 \le CQ^{12}|P_{\mathcal C}(s)|
                e^{-a_{p,b}(s)/8-(2\pi p\rho/b+\sigma s)^2/8}.
                                                               \tag{151.37}
$$

The residue r and Poisson index k were summed as ONE grid, so no b^|C|, no fixed constant to the power|C|, and no implicit denominator-dependent prefactor remains. This also explains why an unmarked theta bound alone would be insufficient.

At zero the denominator is1 and every J coordinate instead has precision

$$
 {d_j\over1+4s^2d_j^2/\mathcal B^2}
 \ge c\min\{Q^{3600},qQ^3e^{-2\kappa\lambda}/\mathfrak a^2\}
 \ge cQ^{3600}.                                            \tag{151.38}
$$

The displacement in its integer h coordinate is s(mu_j-m_j)/(pi mathcal B), bounded by

$$
 C S a_x\sqrt{d_{max}}/\mathcal B
 \le\exp[-(c_q/2-\kappa)\lambda+O(R/Q^2+\log Q)]\to0.       \tag{151.39}
$$

It is eventually <=1/4. Thus all nonzero zero-arc modes and their two marks contribute at most CQ^14exp(-cQ^3600) after integration. The h=0 normalization error has the same size. Extending the ONE complete reference from |s|<=S to the real line costs
exp(-c sqrt(Q) log S)<=exp(-c_1kappa Q^(7/2)), using the original central core. This tail is not repeated for each nonzero arc and has no inverse-rho multiplier.

### 151.8 整个实轴上的弧外收缩和非零弧估计

Outside(151.11), at least aQ^2 untouched block factors have modulus<=eta. Two real derivatives of the product expand into at most CQ^4 terms. The empirical center is common to all these vectors. The arithmetic event was not separately optimized for each denominator. The residual displacement obeys

sum_{b<=mathfrak b}sum_p exp[-c_0(rho p/b)^2]
<=C mathfrak b^2(1+rho^-1), by the elementary Gaussian integer-sum estimate. No interval of physical length or numerator range is omitted. For |p|>N split the Gaussian exponent and use b<=mathfrak b; its tail is at most
C mathfrak b^2(1+rho^-1)exp[-c_0 rho^2N^2/mathfrak b^2].
Since sigma S=o(1), the same bounds hold with the displacement in(151.37), by(x+y)^2>=x^2/2-y^2.

The sufficient integrated marked alias functional is

 \mathcal W=\sum_{\substack{b\le\mathfrak b,\ (p,b)=1\\p\ne0}}

Using(151.42), the uniform integral of |P_C|, and the numerator tail just proved yields, with conservative numerical constants,

 \mathcal W\le C\mathfrak b^2(1+\rho^{-1})

Here rho^2N^2/mathfrak b^2>=10^6 V_R, so the second term pays R+2log mathfrak b and any fixed polynomial. The first term dominates their sum as well, since R=o(lambda) and log mathfrak b=o(Q). The common sufficient event is stronger than this integrated criterion but has already been proved without a growing raw-data union.

Combining(151.37–44), the zero-arc errors and its single reference tail gives

$$
 \max_{k\le2}\|\partial_u^k(f_{lat,u}-g_u)|_{u=0}\|_\infty
 \le CQ^{20}\{\mathcal W+e^{-2Q^2}
                 +e^{-cQ^{3600}}+e^{-c_1\kappa Q^{7/2}}\}
 \le CQ^{-400}.                                             \tag{151.45}
$$

This is an explicit sequencewise bound with fixed constants. All summation, inversion and real differentiation are justified by the displayed integrable envelopes. The power400 is a consequence of these exponential estimates, not an increase of a local expansion order. The only inverse-rho costs are the off-arc period sum and the weighted arc sum. No polynomial signed-mass error has been multiplied by inverse noise.

The physical comparison interfaces (149.47)–(149.54) are reused only after checking their hypotheses above. This identity is why exponentially small sigma does not amplify(151.46). It retains the exact physical output, including all outside energy, before comparing any moment density.

For the nonlinear term q_1^2/q_0 use
q_1^2/q_0=sup_z(2zq_1-z^2q_0), clipping |z|<=b. For two laws the integrated variance-density error is at most epsilon_2+2b epsilon_1+b^2epsilon_0 plus their fourth W moments divided by b^2. ### 151.10 实分母、外部能量平移与全部输出

For h_out=sqrt(100nu log Q), the original continuous-J reference g_u with exact E and noncentrality satisfies g_0>=cQ^-60 and |g_1|+|g_2|<=CQ^4 on |y|<=h_out, where g_k=partial_u^k g_u at0. Let Delta_k=partial_u^k(f_lat,u-g_u) at0 and F=f_lat,u/g_u. At fixed physical y, exact real differentiation gives

$$
 F-1=\Delta_0/g_0,\qquad

The maximal coefficient is CQ^188. Equation(151.45) establishes the real denominator F>=1/2 BEFORE taking its log, and then |partial_u^2 log F|<=CQ^-200 on moderate outputs. No complex log or zero-free neighborhood is asserted. Posterior surprise is W plus a y-only constant, whereas Var(W)=Vprior+1/2. Therefore the exact Bayes identity is

It follows that D_lat-D_g=partial_u^2 log F on these outputs. Only identical finite coefficients cancel in this intermediate difference.

For the complement use the original real exponential moment estimate on the FULL scalar. Completing each lattice square for |z|<=C sqrt(log Q) has normalization1+O(exp(-c d_j)), uniformly in its real shifted mean. The continuous comparison log mgf is

The large trace cancels the original intercept. Its remaining mean is O(a_x^2/sqrt(delta))+O(Q^7202/mathcal B), its variance tends to nu, and its higher terms are bounded by
C[epsilon|z|^3+a_x^2z^2+sigma^2z^2+|z|Q^7202/mathcal B]. The lattice normalization product is1+O(Q^2exp(-cQ^3600)). All low-group energy and surprise remain. Chernoff then gives

Conditional Jensen and Cauchy–Schwarz with EW^4<=CQ^4 bound posterior-variance tails by CQ^-18. Exact prior and finite coefficient payments have vanishing tails by the same fixed moments. This step has no inverse-noise factor or tail denominator.

To return the continuous reference to the original physical expression, condition on all outside counts/Gaussians and the SAME G. Every growing parameter has now been displayed. When R=o(Q^3), the potentially dangerous quantities2R,6L,log m and log mathfrak b are all little-o of the fixed positive Q^3 margins. This is the common reason the arithmetic, sparse occupancy and smoothing estimates coexist on the SAME realization. The proof does not claim uniform convergence over arbitrary sequences with no specified modulus of their little-o; it proves every such sequence using the displayed finite inequalities. That is exactly the stated quantifier, not a diagonal construction.

At R comparable Q^3, neither the selected-score displacement nor log m is automatically lower order than log q/log M, and the curvature and rational-spacing comparisons require new inequalities among fixed constants. Nothing here proves success or failure there. The former lcm precision obstruction was a proof representation cost; its removal supplies no original-model necessity statement.

### 151.12 方法归属与结论范围

有限 Gauss 和、Gaussian Fourier 积分、Poisson 求和、Dirichlet 逼近与既约分数分离是经典工具。第 149 章给出这里复用的显式确定性估计；第 68、120、132、134、138、147 章提供实际行律、共同条件槽位核、固定偏移展开、保留全部原像的互素投影与共同有理目标。第 101、111、142、145、147、149 章的有符号矩及原始物理回接，只在其逐项假设已经核对的范围内使用。

Cellarosi–Osman 的 *Bounds for Smooth Theta Sums with Rational Parameters* 给出共同模群轨道远离两个整数尖点集合时的统一 theta 界；其常数依赖轨道距离、维数、权重及移位。固定移位的界不能直接提供这里随 $Q$ 变化的经验中心估计，具体奇数有理对条件也没有由原始模型保证。本章以 (151.26)–(151.31) 的实际数据事件和 (151.33)–(151.44) 的精确混合展开履行这些不同的义务。原始文献的适用条件、版本与文本缺陷见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。第 149 章对 Cellarosi–Marklof 及 Chung–Dadush–Liu–Peikert 的使用边界保持不变。

新增的模型内关系是：用增长的既约分母取代公共倍数表示，在非零频区只展开指数占据块；再将 $L=o(Q^3)$ 的可测选池和整段频带共享的至多九个有理值接到同一实现上。完整结论仍涉及两个实温度导数、原始计数惊异、共用 Gaussian 残差、条件均值平方、所有输出及精确 $C_xm_x$。这里没有原始后验的整体 Gaussian 替换，也没有从未加标记的全变差收敛推出无界后验矩。

本章的逐序列结论不声称对所有未指定收敛模数的次立方序列一致收敛。$R\asymp Q^3$、零噪声、必要阈值、锐性与原环境期望收敛仍未由本章解决；充分估计的失效也不构成原始信道的反例。有限文献核对不构成全球原创性证明。

## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）

## 152. 原始有限计数的复零点与实条件响应

第 148、150 章分别控制实际两区域质量与实场响应。本章把这些结果接到同一有限计数和的复零点上：先用一个精确的实场平移建立带指数标记的区域矩界，再对整函数作紧复域上的展开。该平移保留全部计数、中心、支持和观测，只改变同一权重中的外场。

在实际等区域质量外场附近，每个固定奇数 $\pi i$ 位置对应一个简单零点。有限位移同时包含区域均值差的虚部修正与区域方差差的实部修正；与第 150 章独立给出的实条件敏感度峰相比，两个相对于实际等质量中心的实位移之比趋于 $12/\pi^2$。结论保留 $\eta\to0$、$t=\eta/\sqrt\delta\to\infty$ 的任意慢速率和原始噪声严格指数余量，属于普通数学推导，未作 Lean 形式化认证。

### 152.1 原始有限和与紧复域上的零点结论

**定理 152.1（原始选择计数的局部复零点及有限位移）。** A uniform original-count exponential-mark bound follows from an exact shift to a nearby real field. This avoids any assumption about a complex energy saddle or a complex logarithm of the partition function.

Let h0=h_equal^P(y,xi) be Chapter 148's ACTUAL selected equal-region-mass field for an allowed separator xi. At that real field, condition on D<0, write R_c=-D, and let b,i be its actual boundary and interior means, v_B,v_I the corresponding variances, d=i-b, and Delta_v=v_I-v_B. All these are finite selected-count quantities at the same data realization and physical output. Define the entire function
$$
 \Phi_Q(z;y,\xi)=
 e^{bz/d}\frac{N_P^-(h_0+z/d,y)}{N_P^-(h_0,y)}.
 \tag{152.1}
$$
The denominator is positive and d>0. For every fixed M<infinity,
$$
 \sup_{|z|\le M}
 \left|\Phi_Q(z)-\frac12\left[
 1+\frac{v_Bz^2}{2d^2}
       +e^{-z}\left(1+\frac{v_Iz^2}{2d^2}\right)\right]\right|
       =O_{\mathrm{Prob}}(t^{-3})=o_{\mathrm{Prob}}(t^{-2}).
 \tag{152.2}
$$
The O bound holds uniformly on each inherited tight-constant good-data class. It is a genuine locally uniform analytic expansion on every fixed compact in the z plane. In particular it is stronger than a real function-value or fixed-moment assertion.

For each fixed integer k, put z_k=(2k+1)pi*i, with the i in this expression the imaginary unit, not the interior mean. There is exactly one zero, counted with multiplicity, in any sufficiently small fixed scaled disk about z_k, for sufficiently large levels on the good events. It is therefore simple, and its complex FIELD location is
$$
 h_k=h_0+\frac{z_k}{d}
             +\frac{\Delta_v z_k^2}{2d^3}
             +O_{\mathrm{Prob}}\!\left(\frac1{d t^3}\right).
 \tag{152.3}
$$
All statements are simultaneous for any fixed finite set of k. The proof also excludes zeros on every fixed compact subset of the scaled plane disjoint from the odd-pi*i sites, and counts zeros in bounded domains whose boundary avoids those sites. No growing-k assertion is made.

Here is the predictive exact-profile form. All subscript W quantities below are evaluated at the EXACT finite noisy-profile field Lambda(h_W,y)=0, and
$$
 c_W=(C_I-C_B)(h_W,y),\qquad
 a_{I,W}=\frac{F'''(r_W;h_W,y)}{2K_W^2},\qquad
 g_W=a_{I,W}-1/h_W.
$$
Then
$$
 h_k=h_W+\frac{z_k}{r_W}+\frac{c_W}{r_W}
             -\frac{z_k g_W}{r_W^2}
             +\frac{z_k^2}{2K_Wr_W^3}
             +o_{\mathrm{Prob}}\!\left(\frac1{r_Wt^2}\right).
 \tag{152.4}
$$
This retains both the imaginary gap correction and the real variance correction, as well as the real equal-mass correction. The finite-profile quantities are not replaced by limiting quartic values when defining the center.

The original objects and their probability scope are as follows. Q denotes the original level, Q_x the auxiliary product COUNT law, and P_x the actual full-q selected count law:
$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q\delta^5,\quad
 Q_x(n)=\prod_j {C_j\choose n_j}p_j^{n_j}(1-p_j)^{C_j-n_j},
 \quad v_j=C_jp_j(1-p_j)/B^2,
$$
$$
 V=\sum_jv_j,\quad C_2=\delta^{-1}\sum_jv_j^2,\quad
 x_j=(n_j-\mu_j)/B,\quad e_j=(\mu_j-C_jp_j)/B,
$$
$$
 E=\sum_jx_j^2,\quad D=\sum_j(x_j+e_j),\quad
 T=(E-V)/\sqrt\delta,\quad a=(2V)^{-1}+\eta.
 \tag{152.5}
$$
The finite entire sum in this contribution is exactly
$$
 N_P^-(h,y)=\sum_{D(n)<0}P_x(n)
       \exp\{aD(n)^2+hD(n)-(T(n)-y)^2/(2\sigma^2)\}.
 \tag{152.6}
$$
Every original count multiplicity, floor, low tuple, outside label, full center mu and noncentral e is retained. No substitution of Q_x for P_x, total-count constraint D=0, or unconditioned partition function is made.

Retain eta=eta_Q>0 tending to zero, t=eta/sqrt(delta) tending to infinity ARBITRARILY slowly, and sigma>0 tending to zero subject only to
$$
 \limsup\frac{\log(1/\sigma)}{Q^3}<c_q/2,\qquad
 \log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),\qquad c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta.
 \tag{152.7}
$$
Write m=sqrt(2V^4/C2), w0=sqrt(2/3), r_sc=m sqrt(eta/delta), h_sc=eta r_sc. The empirical m need not converge deterministically. For xi in a fixed compact [xi0,xi1] contained in(0,w0), set B_xi={0<R_c<=xi r_sc} and I_xi={R_c>xi r_sc}; N_P^B,N_P^I are their raw sums in(152.6). Their sum is exactly N_P^- and is separator-independent. The prior full support and the inherited count return give positivity of each region. Their exact ratio decreases strictly in real h, because its log derivative is -i+b<0. The theorem in Chapter 148 supplies the unique local equal-mass field h0 and its finite correction.

Precisely, for each fixed M,R and separator compact, the suprema in(152.2), multiplied by t^2, tend to zero in ORIGINAL actual-data probability uniformly over deterministic size-q supports, separately in the pair and path experiments. The analogous supremum of r_Wt^2 times the residual in(152.4), for any fixed finite k set, tends to zero with the same scope. The stronger O in(152.2)--(152.3) means bounded constants on each tight-constant common class, followed by exhaustion of those classes. All field choices are covered simultaneously on one actual realization; a data-dependent h0 or h_W is not treated as independent. This is an assertion for each admissible sequence, not a universal rate over all sequences.

### 152.2 精确有限剖面与实场输入

For clarity the exact comparator quantities in(152.4) are specified before use. Choose l,zeta with log(1/sigma)<=lQ^3 eventually, l<c_q/2 and 2zeta<c_q-l, and retain the high set H={j:C_j>=exp(zeta Q^3)}. Every low tuple is retained exactly in the count return. Let V_H=sum_H v_j, C_H=diag(v_j), b_H=(v_j), d_H=b_H/V_H, and A0=C_H-b_Hb_H^T/V_H. Conditional on its charge r, the centered Gaussian high vector has mean r d_H and covariance A0. Its energy plus Gaussian noise of variance delta sigma^2 has exact transform
$$
 \mathcal K(w,R_0)=-\tfrac12\log\det(I-2wA_0)
        +R_0 w d_H^T(I-2wA_0)^{-1}d_H
        +\tfrac12\delta\sigma^2w^2.
 \tag{152.8}
$$
Here R_0 is squared charge. At the FULL physical H_y=V+sqrt(delta)y, let f_r^0(H_y) be the resulting density and define
$$
 g_y^0(r)=e^{\gamma r^2}f_r^0(H_y),\quad
 \gamma=\eta-\{(2V_H)^{-1}-(2V)^{-1}\},\quad
 \ell_y(R_0)=\log g_y^0(\sqrt{R_0}).
 \tag{152.9}
$$
Only this analytic comparator is centered; the original finite law(152.6) keeps e. For real h,
$$
 F(r;h,y)=\ell_y(r^2)-\ell_y(0)-hr,\quad
 F_r(r_-;h,y)=0,\quad K=-F_{rr}(r_-;h,y)>0,\quad A=F(r_-;h,y),
$$
$$
 \Lambda=A+\log h+\tfrac12\log(2\pi/K),\quad
 C_B=2\ell_y'(0)/h^2,\quad
 C_I=F''''/(8K^2)+5(F''')^2/(24K^3).
 \tag{152.10}
$$
The branch is Chapter 146's unique real local maximum in its fixed neighborhood of w0 r_sc. All derivatives of F in C_I are charge derivatives at that branch; ell' is a squared-charge derivative. Its exact finite sigma, high-block defect and full empirical V are retained. We never continue this saddle or its logarithm into a complex field.

The real statements in Chapters 148 and 150 used below, uniformly on each fixed bounded Lambda window, are
$$
 N_P^B(h,y)=\frac{M_0(y)}h[1+C_B+o(t^{-2})],\quad
 N_P^I(h,y)=\frac{M_0(y)}h e^\Lambda[1+C_I+o(t^{-2})],
$$
$$
 M_0(y)=\sigma\sqrt{\delta/V_H}\,g_y^0(0)\asymp\sigma,\quad
 r_-/r_{\rm sc}\longrightarrow w_0,\quad K/(2\eta)\longrightarrow1,
 \tag{152.11}
$$
and the genuine finite derivative identities
$$
 r_h=-1/K,\quad K_h=F'''/K,\quad
 \Lambda_h=-r_-+1/h-F'''/(2K^2)=-r_-[1+O(t^{-2})].
 \tag{152.12}
$$
Every fixed moment of X=hR_c within B and Z=sqrt K(R_c-r_-) within I is bounded, on the ORIGINAL selected real laws. Their first two precise moments are
$$
 b=h^{-1}[1+2C_B+o(t^{-2})],\quad
 v_B=h^{-2}[1+6C_B+o(t^{-2})],
$$
$$
 i=r_-+\frac{F'''}{2K^2}+o(1/(\sqrt Kt^2)),\quad
 v_I=K^{-1}[1+O(t^{-2})+o(t^{-2})].
 \tag{152.13}
$$
The statement about every fixed moment includes absolute moments by bounding them with adjacent even powers; it is not an exponential-moment assertion by itself.

These inputs include
$$
 h_0=h_W+c_W/r_W+o(1/(r_Wt^2)),\quad
 h_0r_{\rm sc}\asymp t^2,\quad
 d\asymp r_{\rm sc},\quad K_0d^2\asymp t^2,
 \tag{152.14}
$$
where K0=K(h0,y). The profile derivative bounds give F'''/K^(3/2)=O(t^-1). All real inputs are applied to the SAME data and full physical likelihood; none permits extrapolation to an unbounded Lambda range.

### 152.3 同一原始计数律的实场平移与指数矩

Fix M<infinity. For any real u with |u|<=M set h_u=h0-u/d. From(152.14),
$$
 h_u/h_0=1+O_M(t^{-2})>0,\quad
 |\Lambda(h_u,y)|\le L_M,\quad
 |r_-(h_u)-r_-(h_0)|\le C_M/(K_0d),\quad
 K(h_u)/K_0=1+O_M(t^{-2}).
 \tag{152.15}
$$
These follow by integrating the exact derivatives(152.12) along an interval of length M/d. That interval lies inside the real branch neighborhood because its scaled kappa length is O_M(t^-2). The constant L_M is fixed, so Chapters 148 and 150 apply there with no change of noise or eta assumptions. The actual empirical d is between fixed class multiples of r_sc; the estimates hold simultaneously for every such d.

The real region mass ratios are bounded above AND below:
$$
 C_M^{-1}\le N_P^J(h_u,y)/N_P^J(h_0,y)\le C_M,
                     \qquad J=B,I,\quad |u|\le M.
 \tag{152.16}
$$
Indeed(152.11) cancels the identical h-independent M0; h0/h_u is bounded, C_B,C_I=O(t^-2), and the interior exponential ratio is exp(Lambda(h_u)-Lambda(h0)) with bounded exponent by(152.15). Each denominator is its OWN region mass, comparable to sigma/h0. There is no inverse positive-sign or minority-probability factor.

For any nonnegative function f of the original tuple the following identity is EXACT:
$$
 E_{P,J,h_0}\{f\,e^{uR_c/d}\}
  =\frac{N_P^J(h_u,y)}{N_P^J(h_0,y)}E_{P,J,h_u}f.
 \tag{152.17}
$$
This is obtained by multiplying the same finite weights exp(-h0 R_c), without changing their prior, centers, observation, support or separator. It is not analytic continuation of a real theorem or a claim that fixed polynomial moments determine a moment-generating function.

Let mu_B=b, mu_I=i, and put s_B=1/h0, s_I=1/sqrt K0. The real bounds(152.13)--(152.16), followed by the exact identity(152.17) with u=M, prove, for every fixed integer p>=0,
$$
 E_{P,J,h_0}\left[
 \left|\frac{R_c-\mu_J}{s_J}\right|^p
       \exp\{M|R_c-\mu_J|/d\}\right]\le C_{M,p},
                 \qquad J=B,I.
 \tag{152.18}
$$
Here is the centering check needed for this implication. Since R_c>=0 and mu_J>=0,
exp(M|R_c-mu_J|/d)<=exp(Mmu_J/d)exp(MR_c/d).
The first factor is bounded: b/d=O(t^-2) and i/d=1+O(t^-2). In B, h0(R_c-b) has bounded moments under h_M because h0/h_M is bounded and h0 b=O(1). In I, write
$$
 \sqrt{K_0}(R_c-i)=
 \sqrt{K_0/K(h_M)}\,Z_M+
              \sqrt{K_0}\{r_-(h_M)-i\}.
 \tag{152.19}
$$
The last shift is O_M(t^-1): (152.15) pays the saddle change and(152.13) pays i-r_-(h0). All fixed moments of Z_M are bounded under the SAME original selected real law. Equations(152.16)--(152.19) give(152.18), including p=3. Thus the absolute third moments with exponential marks have their correct local scales, not merely some crude polynomial-Q bound.

For B the bounded interval itself also makes exp(MR_c/d) uniformly bounded. For I it does not; the exact shifted-law identity is essential. This identifies the logical addition beyond Chapter 150's unmarked or polynomial-moment convergence. Neither real positivity alone nor a power-series summation of all fixed moments is being used.

### 152.4 指数标记下的计数、非中心与尾部回接

For completeness we verify that the shift bridge retains the original quantitative returns with complex marks, rather than hide a large-tail cost inside(152.17). For |z|<=M the modulus of exp[-z(R_c-mu_J)/d] is bounded by C_M exp(MR_c/d). The latter is exactly the real shift h_M. All following statements therefore take place on the real field strip(152.15), on ONE realized original energy/charge array.

The literal selected-law density is
$$
 P_x(n)=L_x(k)Q_x(n),\quad BD=k-m_J,\quad
 L_x(k)=\frac{[w^{q-k}]\prod_{l\notin J}(1-p_l+p_lw)}
                  {[w^q]\prod_l(1-p_l+p_lw)}.
 \tag{152.20}
$$
Here J in the products denotes the union of original count groups, not the B/I region index, k=sum_j n_j and m_J=sum_j C_jp_j. The outside Bernoulli labels supply q-k. Let d_c be their variance, epsilon=B^2/(2d_c)=O(delta^5). The whole-tuple bound in Chapter 143 is
$$
 0\le L_x\le1+C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}),\qquad
 |L_x-1|\le C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\epsilon D^2).
 \tag{152.21}
$$
Full support is retained; this is not a separate full-q Gaussian approximation.

The common classes have c<=V,C2<=C, v_*<=Cdelta, n_g<=Cdelta^-4 and a block of at least c/delta variances comparable to delta. Noncentrality obeys ||e||<=Cdelta^5 and (sum|e_j|)^2<=Cdelta^6. At the SAME centered real energy saddle, the resolvent interpolation in Section 148.5 from mean r d_H to r d_H-e_H gives
$$
 \sup_{|r|\le M_1\sqrt{\eta/\delta},|y|\le R}
          |f_r^e(H_y)/f_r^0(H_y)-1|\le C_{M_1}\delta^4.
 \tag{152.22}
$$
The proof bounds its real exponent change by Cdelta^4 and its normalized Fourier-prefactor change by Cdelta^(9/2), using the same variance-block envelope at every interpolated mean. The vertical resolvent uses the REAL energy saddle; no complex field enters it. Multiplication by the present complex mark costs only its modulus. On this moderate charge compact that modulus is bounded uniformly since d is comparable to sqrt(eta/delta); thus(152.22) remains an O_M(delta^4) relative-to-unmarked-region error. With local polynomial marks one integrates their bounded moments under h_M. This is the quantitative actual-e control, and t^2delta^4=eta^2delta^3 tends to zero.

For centered AND actual-e Gaussian charge profiles, the global density bound from Chapter 146 is
$$
 \frac{g_y^\circ(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}\,u)}{g_y^\circ(0)}
 \le C\exp\left[t^2\left\{u^2-
                   \frac{c u^4}{1+\eta u^2}\right\}\right],
                         \qquad |u|\ge M_1.
 \tag{152.23}
$$
A circle denotes either specified profile. For fixed large M1, then small eta, the braces are <=-B0 u^2 for any prescribed fixed B0. The added mark is at most exp(C_M|u|); it is absorbed into this SAME bound. Local Gaussian well tails use exp(-cZ^2+C_M|Z|/t); endpoint tails use exp(-cX+C_M X/t^2). For example, truncate local integration at |Z|<=t^(1/10) and X<=t^(1/4); beyond those growing cutoffs within the fixed local neighborhoods these envelopes give superpolynomially small t tails. On the separator gap the mark is bounded and the action loss is exp(-ct^2). Consequently every fixed polynomial times the exponential mark has omitted tails smaller than every fixed inverse power of t after normalization by its region's own mass. The scaled Jacobians cost powers of t, not powers of Q. This is important for arbitrarily slow t.

For the high-count cell lift, uniformly in EVERY exact low tuple, retain
$$
 |\log(\text{lifted density}/\phi_C)|\le\mathcal E_Q,\quad
 |D-D_G|\le\mathcal E_Q,\quad
 |T-T_G|/\sigma\le\mathcal E_Q,\quad
 \mathcal E_Q=P(Q)e^{-bQ^3}.
 \tag{152.24}
$$
Here T_G uses full V and e. The complex linear mark changes across a cell by a factor whose absolute error is bounded by C_M mathcal E_Q/d times its positive exponential envelope. Local polynomial marks have the same derivative payment as Chapter 150. The effective REAL field h_M satisfies h_M/h0=1+O_M(t^-2), so
$$
 h_MD\le\eta D^2+h_M^2/(4\eta),\qquad h_M^2/(4\eta)=O_M(t^2).
 \tag{152.25}
$$
The joint energy-Fourier bound of Chapter 137 at a_+=(2V)^-1+2eta controls normalized likelihood-score and fixed charge insertions with cost sigma P(Q)exp(C_Mt^2). For b0=(T-T_G)/sigma and u0=(T_G-y)/sigma, the likelihood log change is -b0u0-b0^2/2. Young's inequality absorbs it into a nearby real noise width, and the exact log-width score pays that change. There is no inverse-sigma derivative. The resulting absolute cell error, with this exponential mark and any fixed local polynomial, is
$$
 \sigma P_p(Q)\exp[-bQ^3+C_{M,p}t^2].
 \tag{152.26}
$$
The positive strict payments remain c_q/2-l, c_q-2zeta-l and the high Stirling margin. Low tuples and their original probabilities are summed only after this uniform estimate, without selecting a different tuple or center.

For excluded tuples, D^2<=2n_gE+2(sum e_j)^2 and(152.25) give, by completing the square in this SAME E,
$$
 e^{aD^2+h_MD-(E-H_y)^2/(2\delta\sigma^2)}
 \le e^{C_Mt^2+2a_+(\sum e_j)^2+2a_+n_gH_y+
                       4a_+^2n_g^2\delta\sigma^2}
       e^{-(E-H_y)^2/(4\delta\sigma^2)}.
 \tag{152.27}
$$
The prefactor logarithm is O(Q^(7/2))+O_M(t^2); the excluded binomial tail is P(Q)exp(-cQ^4). Fixed count/local polynomials cost at most exp(C_pQ^3), and division by sigma costs only O(Q^3) under(152.7). Hence excluded contributions remain exp(-c'Q^4) after region normalization. This pays extreme finite-count charges even though exp(MR_c/d) is unbounded there. A finite polynomial moment alone would not do so.

Each region denominator is comparable to sigma/h0, by(152.11),(152.15)--(152.16). Factors h0,d and their needed inverses are polynomially bounded in Q, while t^2=o(Q^(1/2)); thus(152.26) remains exponentially small after normalization and multiplication by t^2. Cut disagreement at D=0 occupies width mathcal E_Q with mark bounded near one. At the separator it has the additional exp(-ct^2) loss, with bounded exponential mark and only fixed powers of t from local polynomials. The charge lattice spacings h0/B and sqrt K0/B are exponentially small. No inverse minority or inverse complex normalizer has been introduced.

Finally, at h_M, integrate(152.21) with each local polynomial. Using the same-region two higher moments gives the bounds
$$
 E_{Q,B,h_M}(1+|X|^p)|L_x-1|
 \le C_{M,p}\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\delta^6/\eta^3\},
$$
$$
 E_{Q,I,h_M}(1+|Z|^p)|L_x-1|
 \le C_{M,p}\{\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\eta\delta^4+\delta^5/\eta\}.
 \tag{152.28}
$$
Transforming back to h0 with the exact unnormalized real shift multiplies these by bounded OWN-region mass ratios. The same argument applies to complex marks by modulus. Each bound times t^2 tends to zero; the nontrivial products are delta^5/eta, eta^3delta^3 and eta delta^4. Actual selection normalizers stay positive and comparable to one. Thus the complete region-relative exponential-mark comparison has error bounded by
$$
 C_{M,p}\{\delta^4+\delta^5+q^{-1/2}
          +\delta^6/\eta^3+\eta\delta^4+\delta^5/\eta\}
       +P_p(Q)e^{-bQ^3+C_{M,p}t^2}+o(t^{-A})
       =o(t^{-2}),
 \tag{152.29}
$$
where any fixed A>2 may be used for the profile tails by choosing the fixed tail bounds accordingly. This is a bound relative to the positive REAL region masses, not relative to a complex numerator that may vanish. The real-shift identity proves(152.18) directly on the original finite law; (152.22)--(152.29) exhibit its full original-model tail and comparison payments. All are simultaneous for the empirical d and field choices.

### 152.5 实际区域中心矩给出的整函数展开

Because(152.6) is a finite sum, it is entire in h and has real coefficients in its exponential representation. For real h0, N_P^-(h0)>0. At the equal-mass field, the actual conditional region weights are EXACTLY one half. Therefore
$$
 \Phi_Q(z)=\tfrac12\{M_B(z)+e^{-z}M_I(z)\},\qquad
 M_J(z)=E_{P,J,h_0}e^{-z(R_c-\mu_J)/d}.
 \tag{152.30}
$$
This is an exact finite identity on the whole complex plane. The common factor removed from N_P^- is precisely N_P^-(h0)exp(-bz/d), which is nonzero everywhere; no additional phase normalization or complex logarithm is hidden.

For every complex w,
$$
 |e^w-1-w-w^2/2|\le |w|^3e^{|w|}/6.
 \tag{152.31}
$$
Apply this with w=-z(R_c-mu_J)/d. Exact centering eliminates the linear term. By(152.18),
$$
 M_B(z)=1+\frac{v_Bz^2}{2d^2}+O_M((h_0d)^{-3})
          =1+\frac{v_Bz^2}{2d^2}+O_M(t^{-6}),
$$
$$
 M_I(z)=1+\frac{v_Iz^2}{2d^2}+O_M((\sqrt{K_0}d)^{-3})
          =1+\frac{v_Iz^2}{2d^2}+O_M(t^{-3}).
 \tag{152.32}
$$
All estimates hold uniformly for |z|<=M and the original probability/parameter sets. The means and variances here are EXACT selected-count ones, so(152.32) has no hidden approximation error from replacing them by a Gaussian. Equations(152.30)--(152.32) prove(152.2).

The analytic remainder is the difference of entire functions. On any smaller compact, Cauchy's integral formula bounds each fixed z derivative of that remainder by the same O(t^-3), using(152.2) on a slightly larger disk. This is a legitimate analytic consequence of a proved complex-uniform bound, not differentiation of a real C0 approximation. No zero-free premise is needed to use Cauchy's formula for these entire functions.

### 152.6 简单零点的计数与有限位移

Let f0(z)=(1+exp(-z))/2. Its zeros are exactly z_k=(2k+1)pi*i and f0'(z_k)=1/2. Write the displayed correction in(152.2) as
$$
 q_Q(z)=\frac{z^2}{4d^2}(v_B+e^{-z}v_I).
 \tag{152.33}
$$
On every fixed disk, q_Q and its first derivative are O(t^-2), because v_I/d^2=O(t^-2), v_B/d^2=O(t^-4). The remainder is O(t^-3).

Take a fixed finite set of sites, and disjoint fixed disks of radius rho<pi around them. The minimum modulus of f0 on their boundaries is strictly positive. Equation(152.2) makes |q_Q+remainder| smaller than that minimum eventually. Rouché's theorem then gives exactly ONE zero in each disk, counting multiplicity. Thus each zero is simple. The theorem applies to entire functions on neighborhoods of the closed disks, and its strict boundary inequality has just been verified.

Let the zero in the k disk be z_k+u_k. The same nondegenerate f0 bound first gives |u_k|<=C t^-2. Expanding the explicit f0 and q_Q at the fixed site, while using the already proved uniform remainder, gives
$$
 0=\tfrac12u_k-\frac{\Delta_v z_k^2}{4d^2}
                      +O(u_k^2+t^{-2}|u_k|+t^{-3}).
 \tag{152.34}
$$
Consequently
$$
 u_k=\frac{\Delta_v z_k^2}{2d^2}+O(t^{-3}).
 \tag{152.35}
$$
The signs in(152.34) are worth making explicit: exp(-z_k)=-1, so q_Q(z_k)=(v_B-v_I)z_k^2/(4d^2), whereas f0'(z_k)=+1/2. Equation(152.35) follows with the PLUS coefficient Delta_v. Since z_k^2 is negative real and Delta_v>0 eventually, this moves the zero to the negative real side relative to h0. Dividing by the real d proves(152.3), with absolute field residual O(1/(d t^3)).

More generally, on any fixed compact set avoiding every z_k, |f0| has a positive minimum; (152.2) excludes zeros there. If Omega is a bounded domain with piecewise smooth boundary and no z_k on its boundary, the same argument counts exactly as many zeros of Phi_Q in Omega as there are z_k there, including multiplicity. Uniformity holds for every fixed such domain and for the preceding finite collections, compact outputs and separator compacts. A boundary passing through a limiting site is intentionally excluded from this formulation.

Complex conjugation is exact for(152.6). The unique labels satisfy h_{-k-1}=conjugate(h_k). For example, for any fixed A with pi<A<3pi, the scaled disk |z|<A contains exactly the first conjugate pair and no other zeros eventually. A disk of radius less than pi contains none eventually. These are LOCAL conclusions in the proved scaled domain, not a global nearest-zero, circle or phase-diagram theorem.

### 152.7 保留虚部修正的精确剖面坐标

Now convert the ACTUAL quantities in(152.3), without losing the requested scale. From Chapters 148 and 150, applied at h0 and then compared to h_W using the exact field derivatives,
$$
 h_0-h_W=c_W/r_W+o(1/(r_Wt^2)),\quad
 r_-(h_0)-r_W=O(r_W/t^4)+o(r_W/t^4),
$$
$$
 b=1/h_W+o(r_W/t^2),\quad
 i=r_W+a_{I,W}+o(r_W/t^2),\quad
 d=r_W+g_W+o(r_W/t^2),
$$
$$
 \Delta_v=K_W^{-1}[1+o(1)],\quad g_W=O(r_W/t^2).
 \tag{152.36}
$$
For the saddle shift, r_h=-1/K and K_Wr_W^2 is comparable to t^2. In the mean formula the stronger error o(1/(sqrt K t^2)) from Chapter 150 is o(r_W/t^3), already smaller than needed. The boundary's 2C_B/h correction is O(r_W/t^4). The changes of a_I and K over h0-h_W have still smaller relative scales by Chapter 150's genuine derivatives. None of these assertions comes from differentiating an unknown error.

Ordinary algebra in(152.36) gives
$$
 d^{-1}=r_W^{-1}-g_W/r_W^2+o(1/(r_Wt^2)),\qquad
 \Delta_v/d^3=(K_Wr_W^3)^{-1}+o(1/(r_Wt^2)).
 \tag{152.37}
$$
Substituting(152.36)--(152.37) into(152.3) proves the exact-profile expression(152.4). The imaginary correction -z_k g_W/r_W^2 is the same scale as the real corrections and cannot be dropped.

Only after(152.4) is established may one interpret its coefficients by their empirical limits. The exact derivative scalings from Chapters 148 and 150 give
$$
 t^2c_W=-37/(8m^2)+o(1),\quad
 t^2g_W/r_W=-15/(4m^2)+o(1),\quad
 t^2/(K_Wr_W^2)=3/(4m^2)+o(1).
 \tag{152.38}
$$
The middle identity is the difference of t^2 a_I/r=-3/(2m^2)+o(1) and t^2/(hr)=9/(4m^2)+o(1). Hence a further finite-empirical coefficient form is
$$
 h_k=h_W+\frac{z_k}{r_W}
       +\frac{-37+30z_k+3z_k^2}{8m^2r_Wt^2}
       +o_{\mathrm{Prob}}(1/(r_Wt^2)).
 \tag{152.39}
$$
The large finite eta, noise and output corrections are still inside the EXACT h_W and r_W. Neither is replaced by its leading quartic approximation. In particular(152.39) is not a window expansion about bare kappa_c. Every coefficient uses the same full empirical array and requires no deterministic m limit.

The original sum and its zeros are independent of the separator. The centering h0 and actual d in(152.1) are separator-dependent coordinates only. Uniformly over permissible xi, their maps to w=r_W(h-h_W) differ by o(1) and the same fixed site disks overlap with unique zero counts. Equivalently, apply the proved expansion in the separator-independent w coordinate using(152.36)--(152.37); it has f0 as its limit. Thus the root with label k is the same zero for every such separator, and (152.4) supplies a common prediction with the same uniform residual. No independent re-selection of a realization is involved.

### 152.8 首对复零点与实条件敏感度峰

For the first conjugate pair, z0=pi*i and z_{-1}=-pi*i. Equations(152.3),(152.36)--(152.37) give
$$
 \operatorname{Re}h_0^{\mathrm{zero}}-h_{\rm equal}^P
       =-\frac{\pi^2}{2K_Wr_W^3}
                   +o_{\mathrm{Prob}}(1/(r_Wt^2)).
 \tag{152.40}
$$
The superscript distinguishes the upper-half-plane zero from the real equal-mass field h0. The conjugate zero has the same real part. Section 150.8 proves a locally unique maximum h_pk of the NEGATIVE-SIGN conditional susceptibility, with
$$
 h_{\rm pk}-h_{\rm equal}^P
       =-\frac6{K_Wr_W^3}+o_{\mathrm{Prob}}(1/(r_Wt^2)).
 \tag{152.41}
$$
We reuse that proved marked-third/fourth-cumulant result; zero locations alone would not prove a peak or its uniqueness.

Both displacements are negative. On each common data class,
$$
 \frac{r_Wt^2}{K_Wr_W^3}
       =\frac{t^2}{K_Wr_W^2}
       =\frac3{4m^2}+o(1)
 \tag{152.42}
$$
is bounded above and bounded away from zero. The errors in(152.40)--(152.41) are therefore small relative to the SAME nonzero leading scale. Division is justified and gives
$$
 \frac{h_{\rm pk}-h_{\rm equal}^P}
      {\operatorname{Re}h_0^{\mathrm{zero}}-h_{\rm equal}^P}
          \longrightarrow\frac{12}{\pi^2}
 \tag{152.43}
$$
uniformly in the original probability/parameter scope. This ratio is relative to the ACTUAL equal-region-mass field. It is not the ratio of displacements from h_W: the common c_W correction would survive that different comparison.

For explicit reference, relative to h_W the first zero has real displacement
-(37+3pi^2)/(8m^2r_Wt^2)+o(1/(r_Wt^2)), while Chapter 150's peak has displacement
-73/(8m^2r_Wt^2)+o(1/(r_Wt^2)). The leading imaginary location is pi/r_W, with the retained correction +15pi/(4m^2r_Wt^2). These statements are consequences of the exact-profile formulas and do not discard slow-noise shifts.

The equal-weight two-phase cancellation, Rouché stability and generic relation between zeros and competing means/variances are classical finite-phase geometry. The model-specific contribution is the original-count exponential-mark bridge, its quantitative return on the tiny-output coexistence fiber, and the resulting finite-profile zero positions linked to the separately established real response on that SAME realization. No Lee-Yang circle, global nearest pair, global zero-free region, thermodynamic analyticity radius, dynamics, or unconditioned susceptibility claim is made.

### 152.9 方法归属与未覆盖范围

两相振幅的等模与奇数相位差、Rouché 稳定性、指数族实场平移和局部累积量展开是经典工具。Biskup–Borgs–Chayes–Kleinwaks–Kotecký 的一般相变零点理论要求非退化相函数、适当区域上的解析非零有限体积近似，以及复分配函数与导数的指数误差；本模型没有因此取得格点轮廓或全局相图假设。本章只使用经典 Rouché 定理，并在 (152.30)–(152.35) 中直接核对所需的边界下界与解析余项上界。

这里新增的模型接口是 (152.17)–(152.29)：以实际区域自身的正质量归一化，控制原始完整选择计数的指数标记，再回接到同一经验数组和物理输出上的复零点。第 150 章的峰存在性与唯一性由第三、第四累积量另行证明；复零点的位置本身不替代该实响应证明。文献版本、原始条件及提取边界见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。

本章对固定有限编号集和固定缩放复域成立，不包含随 $Q$ 增长的零点编号、全局最近零点、Lee–Yang 圆定理、整个复平面零点排除、热力学解析半径、动力学亚稳态或未条件化敏感度。有限噪声与经验系数留在精确中心中，未把结论改写为围绕极限四次剖面的窄窗口展开。有限文献检索不构成全球原创性证明。

## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）

## 153. 精确联合大偏差预算与正立方带宽区间

第 151 章把后验方差熵极限推进到每个 $R=o(Q^3)$ 的对数带宽。本章进入 $R=cQ^3$：不再用宽窗口中的二次上界估算稀有池，而是预先固定两个总数的精确格点，保留 Poisson 率函数、取整代价与前因子。同一对总数同时决定选池代价和选择响应的曲率，因此能将概率、供给和算术精度放到一个共同可行集中。

结论是由原始参数明确决定的充分区间 $0<c<c_{\rm var}$，并附一个无需数值优化的正可行点。所有计数、低组、外部标签、有限校正和同一 Gaussian 残差均保留；原始 pair/path 两类实验分别成立，并在确定支持上一致。这里给出普通数学推导，未作 Lean 认证；区间端点不被宣称为物理阈值。

### 153.1 立方对数带宽下的完整原始后验结论

**定理 153.1（显式正立方区间上的完整方差熵极限）。** The original conclusion below holds on the explicit interval 0<c<c_var defined in Section 153.2. A closed-form positive subinterval 0<c<c_0 is also given there, with an explicit feasible construction. For

$$
 \lambda=Q^3,\quad 0<c_-\le\rho_Qe^{c\lambda}\le c_+<\infty,
 \qquad \rho_Q=\sigma\mathcal B,\quad\mathcal B=q/Q^{11/4},     \tag{153.1}
$$

the SAME original selected full-q posterior satisfies, separately for actual independent pairs and actual paths, uniformly over admissible deterministic true supports,

$$
 \int_{\mathbb R}f_x(y)|D_x(y)-R_*(y)|\,dy\longrightarrow0    \tag{153.2}
$$

in original raw-data probability. To fix every finite quantity, retain

$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q/Q^{5/2},\quad
 T=\mathcal B^{-1}\sum_j(R_j-\mu_j)^2-V/\sqrt\delta,\quad
 Y=T+\sigma G,
$$
$$
 A=V_H/\sqrt\delta,\quad\nu_0=2\sum_{j\in H}w_j^2,\quad
 \kappa_3=8\sum_{j\in H}w_j^3,\quad\Lambda=\nu_0+\sigma^2,
$$
$$
 C_x=A^2\kappa_3/\Lambda^3-2A\nu_0/\Lambda^2,\quad
 D_x(y)=Vpost_x(y)-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xy,
$$
$$
 R_*(y)=29/6-3\sqrt2+(3\sqrt2+8/\sqrt3-9)y^2/\nu,
 \qquad\nu=2g_0.                                          \tag{153.3}
$$

Here Vprior is the exact selected full-count prior surprise variance, m_x=E_xY is exact, and G is the SAME residual throughout. Thus also

$$
 \int Vpost_x(y)f_x(y)\,dy-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xm_x
                   \longrightarrow8/\sqrt3-25/6.           \tag{153.4}
$$

All counts, multiplicities, low/outside labels, physical H and scalar, empirical centers and legal floors are unchanged. We prove a sufficient interval, not all c>0, not necessity or a phase transition, and not zero noise. Chapter 151 retains its existing scope.

### 153.2 显式变分区间与正可行点

Write

$$
 a_0=(1+r)/2,\quad b_0=(1-r)/2,\quad
 v_+=2a_0,\ v_-=2b_0,\quad
 A_s=\log(1+r)>0,\quad B_s=\log(1-r)<0,
$$
$$
 \phi=a_0A_s+b_0B_s>0,\quad
 c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta,\quad c_M=\phi/\beta,\quad
 \kappa=\min(1,c_q,\phi)/1000.                              \tag{153.5}
$$

Thus log q=c_q lambda+O(1), log M=c_M lambda+O(1), q/M=exp(-phi lambda+O(1)), with the original model beta. A_s and B_s here are score coefficients, distinct from the physical A and B^2. Define two available rate budgets

$$
 \mathfrak p=\min(c_q,c_M/3)>0,\qquad
 \mathfrak h=\min\{\phi,c_q/2-5\kappa\}>0.                 \tag{153.6}
$$

For a fixed positive pair x=(x_+,x_-) set

$$
 J_v(z)=z\log(z/v)-z+v,\quad
 I(x)=J_{v_+}(x_+)+J_{v_-}(x_-),
$$
$$
 \ell(x)=\tfrac12\{A_s(x_+-v_+)+B_s(x_--v_-)\}.           \tag{153.7}
$$

The central sufficient joint budget is

$$
 \boxed{\quad I(x)<\mathfrak p,\qquad 2c<\ell(x)<\mathfrak h.\quad}
                                                               \tag{153.8}
$$

It compares the exact cost of a revealed-total score displacement to available lawful pools, while comparing that SAME displacement to rational spacing and curvature. Sections 153.3–153.9 prove its complete original-law sufficiency. These are not independently optimized random environments.

Here is an explicit one-dimensional variational description requiring no numerical optimization. Put

$$
 \Psi(s)=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+,-\}}
 v_\epsilon(e^{s d_\epsilon}-1-s d_\epsilon),\qquad
 d_+=A_s/2,\quad d_-=B_s/2,
$$
$$
 x_\epsilon(s)=v_\epsilon e^{s d_\epsilon},\quad
 \ell(s)=\Psi'(s),\quad F(\ell(s))=s\Psi'(s)-\Psi(s)
                      \quad(s\ge0).                        \tag{153.9}
$$

Since Psi''(s)=sum v_epsilon d_epsilon^2 exp(sd_epsilon)>0, ell(s) increases continuously from 0 to infinity. F increases continuously from 0 to infinity on ell>0: its derivative is s>0, and s tends to infinity with ell. For every positive x with ell(x)=ell(s), direct algebra gives

$$
 I(x)-I(x(s))=
       J_{x_+(s)}(x_+)+J_{x_-(s)}(x_-)\ge0.                \tag{153.10}
$$

Indeed the omitted linear term is s[ell(x)-ell(s)]=0. This proves the exact constrained minimum, not an asserted independence of score margins. Let s_p be the UNIQUE positive solution

$$
 s_p\Psi'(s_p)-\Psi(s_p)=\mathfrak p,
 \qquad \ell_p=\Psi'(s_p),\qquad
 \boxed{c_{var}=\tfrac12\min(\mathfrak h,\ell_p).}          \tag{153.11}
$$

Equations(153.5–6),(153.9),(153.11) define c_var entirely from original fixed parameters. For every 0<c<c_var choose any ell strictly between 2c and min(mathfrak h,ell_p), solve ell=Psi'(s), and take the fixed pair x(s). It satisfies(153.8). This is a deterministic proof choice before any data are revealed. Only the TOTALS are later tested against its predetermined integer values.

A closed-form positive certificate removes any reliance on an unspecified root being small. Define

$$
 \ell_0=\min\{\mathfrak h/2,\ A_s\sqrt{a_0\mathfrak p}/2,
                                  \ A_sa_0/4\}>0,\qquad
 \boxed{c_0=\ell_0/4>0.}                                   \tag{153.12}
$$

Use x_+=2a_0+2ell_0/A_s, x_-=2b_0, so ell(x)=ell_0 and x_+<=5a_0/2. Integrating J_v''(v+t)=1/(v+t)<=1/v for t>=0 gives

$$
 I(x)=J_{2a_0}(2a_0+2\ell_0/A_s)
       \le\ell_0^2/(a_0A_s^2)\le\mathfrak p/4.             \tag{153.13}
$$

Hence(153.8) holds for every0<c<c_0, with substantial strict margins. Also ell_p>ell_0, so c_var>=ell_0/2 and this explicit certificate lies inside the variational interval. No displayed number is a numerical optimum. The variational endpoint belongs to this sufficient method and is not asserted as an actual channel boundary.

### 153.3 保留取整和前因子的精确总数概率

Fix x satisfying(153.8). Put n_epsilon=floor(lambda x_epsilon). The favorable flag for a preselected two-label pool is the exact revealed-total event

$$
 K_+=n_+,\qquad K_-=n_-.                                  \tag{153.14}
$$

Using exact points rather than a moving sqrt(lambda)-window makes the score displacement ell lambda+O(1) and permits a polynomial overhead in the number of trials. No half-mean-window approximation is invoked.

For any fixed v,x>0, let

$$
 D_v(x)=\max\{|\log(x/(2v))|,|\log(x/v)|\},\qquad
 k_v(x)=e^{-D_v(x)}/(3\sqrt x).
$$

For lambda>=2/x, n=floor(lambda x)>=1, y=n/lambda in[x/2,x], and |lambda J_v(y)-lambda J_v(x)|<=D_v(x), by J_v'(y)=log(y/v). The elementary factorial upper bound n!<=3sqrt(n)(n/e)^n gives the uniform lower estimate

$$
 P\{Pois(v\lambda)=\lfloor x\lambda\rfloor\}
 \ge k_v(x)\lambda^{-1/2}e^{-\lambda J_v(x)}.               \tag{153.15}
$$

The corresponding elementary Stirling lower bound gives log probability=-lambda J_v(x)-one-half log lambda+O_{v,x}(1). Both are uniform as x ranges over any specified compact subset of(0,infinity). This proves the exact exponential rate, all rounding costs and the needed prefactor. It does not use a Q-dependent expansion order or a central Gaussian profile at a large-deviation point.

Set

$$
 k(x)=k_{v_+}(x_+)k_{v_-}(x_-)>0,\qquad
 m=\left\lceil k(x)^{-1}\lambda Q^2e^{I(x)\lambda}\right\rceil.
                                                               \tag{153.16}
$$

The product-Poisson flag probability is at least k(x)lambda^-1 exp(-I(x)lambda), so the m independent flags in that auxiliary comparison have no-success probability at most exp(-Q^2). The overhead is exactly lambda Q^2/k(x), with log m=I(x)lambda+5log Q+O_x(1). It is positive and sufficient; no positive rate overhead is hidden. Two fixed true labels per pool, all of the requisite original lawful class, are available eventually since2m/q=exp[-(c_q-I(x))lambda+O_x(log Q)] tends to zero. That class has a fixed positive fraction of the admissible true labels.

All n_epsilon are O_x(lambda), strictly positive, and much smaller than the original number of observation slots, of order Mlambda. Thus these are actual possible raw counts. They need not lie on the scalar's count line: the selected labels are retained in the full-q outside family or in their actual line membership. No physical H, count truncation or observation rule is changed. Equation (68.22) explicitly permits relative one/two-row estimates in any fixed multiple of lambda; its rate formula (68.26) handles the legal count-line floors separately. We use the exact Poisson point formula only in the comparison law of the revealed totals, never as a conditional law of actual rows.

### 153.4 实际共同槽位律与指数数量的可用池

For each fixed true support, choose these m disjoint lawful pairs before observing the data. Reveal the complete parity record, pool masks and totals, all outside labels, and the terminal path label or the pair arrivals. Under this ONE field H_0, the original slot disintegration gives

$$
 (k_i,l_i)_{i\le m}\mid\mathcal H_0\sim
 \bigotimes_{i\le m}\{Bin(K_{i,+},1/2)\otimes Bin(K_{i,-},1/2)\}.
                                                               \tag{153.17}
$$

This is the exact slot law in Chapters 147 and 151. In paths, conditional departure weights are1_{chi(i)=s_t}[1+b_S(i)s_{t+1}]/M. The class sums vanish, path parities are fair, and changing a departure within its class preserves the previous transition's parity. Within each chosen true pair the two weights agree. Conditioning the independent slot choices on their pool masks yields(153.17) jointly, for arbitrary finite m. Actual row counts themselves are not asserted independent. Pair departures obey the same conditional weights and their arrivals are uniform.

Choose the first index I with flag(153.14), using ONLY H_0, then reveal all other pools' internal allocations. Denote the resulting field by F. To verify the selected law, partition by the H_0-measurable events{I=i}; in each part integrate a bounded product test function using(153.17), first in all coordinates except i. The two factors at i remain unchanged. A monotone-class argument and the finite sum over i give the exact selected two-binomial kernel conditional on F, also for F-measurable candidate sets. This proof does not condition on favorable hidden splits and does not pay m times a selected-split failure.

The product Poisson comparison is used ONLY for the bounded no-flag event. Conditional on parity, one categorical slot with total selected probability p differs from independent Poisson coordinates with the same means by p(1-e^-p)<=p^2. Summing these couplings gives Cm^2lambda/M. The original1-dependent path parity-pattern counts have variance C times the slot count; the event of deviations greater than M^(2/3) has probability Clambda M^-1/3. Addition coupling of the Poisson means costs CmM^-1/3. Therefore in both actual experiments

$$
 P_S\{\text{no flag}\}\le e^{-Q^2}+\tau_Q,\qquad
 \tau_Q=C\{\lambda M^{-1/3}+mM^{-1/3}+m^2\lambda/M\}.       \tag{153.18}
$$

Its three rates, including the overhead in(153.16), are

$$
 -c_M/3,\quad I(x)-c_M/3,\quad 2I(x)-c_M
                                                               \tag{153.19}
$$

times lambda, plus O_x(log Q). By I(x)<mathfrak p they are all strictly negative; the last is redundant once I<c_M/3 but is displayed because it comes from a different actual coupling step. The supply condition I<c_q is also distinct. No total-variation estimate is divided by the exponentially small one-pool probability. Define the original score coefficients a_s=log((1+r)/(1-epsilon_M)), b_s=log((1-r)/(1+epsilon_M)), B_0=(M-q)/q. Equation(153.14), the legal floors and log B_0=phi lambda+O(1) give

 t_{raw}=(a_sK_++b_sK_-)/2-\log B_0

since the score defect O((q/M)lambda) tends to zero. Given F, put X=a_s(k-K_+/2)+b_s(l-K_-/2). Choose any fixed

$$
 0<h<\ell-2c;\qquad \text{for instance }h=(\ell-2c)/2.     \tag{153.21}

$$
 P_S\{|X|>h\lambda\mid F\}\le2e^{-2h^2\lambda/V_x}.       \tag{153.22}

This vanishes at a strictly positive cubic rate even for arbitrarily small fixed c in the stated interval. It is paid once. All total-dependent constants are fixed because x is fixed, with n_+/lambda and n_-/lambda in fixed positive compact intervals.

### 153.5 完整选择响应与精确分数曲率预算

Retain the original all-array regularity event with failure

$$
 b_{env}=C\{q^{-1/2}+(CQ^9/M)\sqrt q+M^{-8}q^{-3/2}
                      +Q^3/q+Q/M+M^{-9}\}=o(1).            \tag{153.23}

Delete only the chosen two labels and one central anchor for the response calculation. Every other pool remains in the outside coefficients. The derivative of the Bernoulli calibration mean in log multiplier is its variance, comparable q. Removing three terms changes its mean by at most3; variance changes by at most the exponential of the multiplier displacement. Thus the outside multiplier calibrated at mean q-1 differs from the full multiplier by O(q^-1), uniformly for every three-label deletion, regardless of m or of the selected odds. The associated outside conditions are F-measurable. The binomial kernel is used on this measurable enlargement, not conditioned on the nonmeasurable full-array good event.

Write t_o,D_o for outside multiplier and variance; p=t_oL_0/(1+t_oL_0), v=p(1-p), a_3=kappa_{3,o}/D_o. Then D_o asymp q, p in[1/4,3/4], |log(t_oB_0)|<=2q^-1/4, and outside central membership n_0 asymp q/Q^3. In terms of its elementary symmetric coefficients E_j, the EXACT anchor inclusion is

 p_*={L_0\sum_{z=0}^2c_zE_{q-1-z}\over
           \sum_{z=0}^2c_z(E_{q-z}+L_0E_{q-1-z})},\qquad
 (c_0,c_1,c_2)=(1,L_u+L_v,L_uL_v).                           \tag{153.24}
$$

The fixed-offset expansion in (132.14)–(132.16) and Section 147.7, only s in [-2,1], is 1-(s^2+a_3s)/(2D_o)+O(D_o^-2). Positive finite averaging makes the remainder uniform even when the pair odds are exponentially large. It implies

 p_*=p_{ref}-(v/D_o)f_t(X)+O(q^{-2}),\quad

This does not enlarge the number of deleted labels or the expansion order. Every possible central membership n in{n_0,n_0+1,n_0+2} is retained, with mu_0=np_* and d_0 asymp n.

For gcd(P,Q)=1 the original compensated defect |Qa_s+Pb_s|<=CQ(q/M+exp(-c_1Q^5)) gives, on the ENTIRE selected allocation support,

 H=Ql-Pk,\quad H^0=(QK_--PK_+)/2,\quad

 |X-\bar X|\le\Delta_X=C_x^{tot}Q^3(q/M+e^{-c_1Q^5}).      \tag{153.26}
$$

C_x^{tot} denotes here a fixed total-parameter bound, not the physical coefficient C_x.  \sup_zP_S(H=z\mid F)\le C_x^{tot}Q^{-5/2}.                \tag{153.27}

These constants require only K_epsilon/lambda bounded above and below, which holds for every fixed positive x here. There is no count-coordinate or projection-fiber discard.

On(153.22)'s good split, |bar X|<=h lambda+Delta_X and t=ell lambda+O(1). Since ell>h, cosh t>=2cosh(bar X) for large Q. Directly from the exact f_t,

the exact mode is

 {}\times\exp\left[-\tfrac12\sum_{\mathcal C}

This is finite rational Fourier inversion followed by real Gaussian Poisson integration. The residue r and Poisson index k combine into h=r-bk, so each mode is counted once. where P_C=product_C(1-2isw_j)^-1/2 and

### 153.8 无逆噪声损失的有符号计数回接

The original physical interfaces (151.46)–(151.53) remain applicable because J={d_j>=Q^3600}, E, H, empirical centers and the scalar have not changed. The exact finite payments Vprior=O(Q^2), A^2/Lambda=O(Q^(1/2)), C_x=O(Q^(1/4)), and quadratic R_* are covered by fixed output fourth moments.

For the original selected full-q law, the same-tuple density h obeys0<=h<=C and ||h-1||_2=a_x=O_P(Q^-5/2). Its exact log h surprise correction is retained. The common-kernel and clipping estimate in (101.9), (101.15), and (111.16)–(111.17) costs Ca_xQ^2=o_P(1), for every sigma>0. It follows that

### 153.9 实商、完整参考律与全部输出

For h_out=sqrt(100nu log Q), the complete continuous-J reference with exact E and noncentrality satisfies g_0>=c_1Q^-60 and |g_1|+|g_2|<=CQ^4 on |y|<=h_out. Here g_k=partial_u^k g_u at0.
