$$

The large trace cancels the ORIGINAL intercept. Remaining mean is O(a_x^2/sqrt(delta))+O(Q^7202/mathcal B); variance tends to nu; the higher terms are bounded by
C[epsilon|z|^3+a_x^2z^2+sigma^2z^2+|z|Q^7202/mathcal B].
The lattice correction product is1+O(Q^2exp(-c_1Q^3600)). All low/outside energy is still present. Chernoff gives P_lat(|Y|>h_out)+P_g(|Y|>h_out)<=CQ^-40. Conditional Jensen and Cauchy–Schwarz, with EW^4<=CQ^4, then give posterior-variance tails CQ^-18; prior and finite coefficient tails vanish by the same moments. There is no tail denominator or inverse-noise payment.

For the continuous reference, condition on all original outside counts/Gaussians and the SAME G. Translate outside ENERGY inside the independent core density BEFORE separating outside surprise. The derivative bound (101.19) Cdelta^-1/2 gives O(Q^-199.5) joint variation from the unchanged outside energy error; clipping at Q^10 costs O(Q^-7). Only then does outside surprise decouple and cancel its exact prior variance. The noncentral comparison (101.22) and clipping (101.23) costs O(Q^-1/4[1+(log Q)^(3/4)]). Both operations are sigma-free. The nonzero-arc unexpanded K did not redefine physical outside variables; the zero arc already returned the full J reference.

The reference computation (101.25)–(101.31), with EXACT Lambda=nu_0+sigma^2, gives integral g|D_g-R_*| tending to zero. Its former quantile-coupling lower-noise restriction is not a hypothesis of this signed-kernel route. Equations(153.46),(153.51–53) and the full tails transfer this to Q_lat; equation(153.50) returns it to the SAME original selected full-q law, proving(153.2). The weighted estimates also give E_xY^2 tending to nu. Integrating the explicit R_* proves(153.4), keeping the exact finite C_xm_x. No whole-law Gaussian replacement or TV-to-moment inference is used.

### 153.10 精确率可行集与旧充分界的比较

The old half-mean estimate may legitimately be used only for |z-v|<=v/2. On that domain it replaces J_v(z) by (z-v)^2/v. Indeed J_v''(z)=1/z<=2/v there, so integration yields

$$
 J_v(z)\le (z-v)^2/v,\qquad
 I(x)\le I_{quad}(x):=\sum_\epsilon(x_\epsilon-v_\epsilon)^2/v_\epsilon.
                                                               \tag{153.54}
$$

Consequently every pair in that domain satisfying I_quad<mathfrak p and the SAME geometric score conditions also satisfies the exact-rate budget. This is a proved inclusion of sufficient parameter sets, not an assertion that the final c interval is strictly enlarged for every original r,beta; another constraint may bind first.

On the positive-only displacement x_+=v_++2ell/A_s, x_-=v_-, the stronger inequality

$$
 J_{v_+}(v_++2\ell/A_s)\le {2\ell^2\over v_+A_s^2}
              ={\,\ell^2\over a_0A_s^2}                   \tag{153.55}
$$

holds for EVERY ell>=0, because J_v''(v+t)<=1/v on t>=0. Where the old half-mean estimate is applicable, its upper rate is4ell^2/(v_+A_s^2), twice the bound in(153.55). Exact I is strictly smaller than the latter bound for ell>0. Allowing both totals to tilt further reduces the minimum to F(ell), with exact identity(153.10). No quadratic Taylor approximation is used outside its justified domain, and no numerical optimizer is invoked.

The previous m construction paid exp(C_*L^2/lambda) from a convenient broad score window. At cubic L that coefficient would constrain both the pool supply and response curvature. Here the chosen EXACT totals have the exact rate I, overhead only 5log Q+O(1), and t=ell lambda+O(1). The response curvature loses ell lambda, not 6L. These improvements are joint: the same x controls both rate and score; it is not lawful to minimize I at one x while using the score or split law of another.

The dominant sufficient restrictions are now visible. Pool supply requires I<c_q. The chosen parity-count coupling requires I<c_M/3; its categorical part requires2I<c_M. Rational spacing requires ell-h>2c,2c<phi and2c+5kappa<c_q/2. Thin response requires ell<phi and ell+5kappa<c_q/2. Combining them yields(153.8), with a selectable h>0. The count-line rate controls a fixed occupied block, not the law of the rare selected pair. There is no inference that any failed inequality is necessary for the channel theorem.

In particular, the fixed-c quadratic theorem in Chapter 149 and the subcubic theorem in Chapter 151 remain valid as stated. This contribution adds an explicit cubic interval. It neither asserts an all-c cubic theorem nor interprets c_var as a physical transition.

### 153.11 同一实现上的联合速率条件

All rates below are log costs divided by lambda=Q^3; omitted terms are O_{c,x}(Q+log Q)/lambda or O_x(log Q)/lambda, as indicated in the proofs. Every relevant strict inequality follows from(153.8) and 0<h<ell-2c.

| Step | Exponential rate or explicit bound | Required payment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One favorable total pair | at least k(x)lambda^-1 exp(-I lambda) | exact compact-region Stirling, not Gaussian tails |
| Trial count | log m=I lambda+5log Q+O_x(1) | no-success<=exp(-Q^2) |
| True-label supply | I-c_q | negative |
| Parity failure | -c_M/3 | negative |
| Parity-mean addition coupling | I-c_M/3 | negative |
| Categorical-to-Poisson coupling | 2I-c_M | negative, displayed separately |
| Chosen hidden split tail | -2h^2/V_x | negative, paid once |
| Block minimum variance | c_q-kappa | positive; actual relative row law |
| Denominator cutoff | log mathfrak b=(2c/a)Q+O(1) | lower order than lambda |
| Arc width/spacing ratio | -(c_q-kappa)+O_c(Q/lambda) | negative |
| Numerator horizon | log N=c lambda+O_c(Q+log Q) | all numerators retained |
| Plateau target width times N^2 | 2c-(ell-h) | negative |
| Score-defect target width times N^2 | 2c-phi | negative |
| Full-q remainder target width times N^2 | 2c-c_q | negative |
| Energy target width times N^2 | 2c+5kappa-c_q/2 | negative |
| Energy tolerance divided by curvature | ell+5kappa-c_q/2 | negative |
| Prior remainder divided by curvature | ell-c_q | negative |
| Score/projection defect divided by curvature | ell-phi | negative |
| Common rational targets | at most9 values; at most54 integer H sites | no m-, b- or N-fold split union |
| Projected atom | C_x^{tot}Q^-5/2 | all preimages |
| Nonzero dual precision | at least exp[(c_q-3kappa)lambda] | full product grid sum<=2 |
| Zero dual precision | c_1Q^3600 | full-J reference, no shrinking-denominator loss |
| Displaced nonzero energy | at least exp(7kappa lambda)/4 | pays full retained band |
| Off-arc inverse-rho volume | CQ^20 exp(-2Q^2) | explicit eta contraction |
| Weighted rational arcs | C mathfrak b^2(1+rho^-1) | log cost c lambda+O_c(Q) |
| Numerator Gaussian tail | exp(-10000V_R) | pays previous row and fixed marks |
| Reference Fourier tail | exp(-c_3kappa Q^(7/2)) | once, no inverse rho |

| Conditional-mean-square clipping | O(Q^-16)+O(Q^-424) | fourth W moments<=CQ^4 |

The rare selection, complete calibration, central membership and arithmetic are events on the SAME raw array. The hybrid identity and all physical returns use that array. The only dependence on chosen rate parameters in probability prefactors is through fixed x,h,c; support/floor uniformity is unchanged.

### 153.12 方法归属与尚未解决的边界

Poisson 率函数、指数倾斜、Legendre–Fenchel 对偶、格点 Stirling 前因子与 Gaussian／Gauss–Poisson Fourier 工具均为成熟理论。本章的模型内构造是把精确取整总数的率函数与同一分数位移联立，并用实际槽位的共同条件律将指数数量的预选池接回原始实验；后续有理值约束、标记积分和全部输出回接使用同一实现。

Féray–Méliot–Nikeghbali 的 mod-$\phi$ 精确偏差定理要求共同复带上的局部一致生成函数逼近、适当的非零残差、最小格点和定量逼近速度。单个比较 Poisson 变量履行这些条件，但实际受约束的多池向量不自动满足它们。本章直接证明 (153.15) 的带取整格点界，并用 (153.17)–(153.19) 的共同事件比较支付实际路径依赖；具体原文版本、条件和未使用的印刷缺陷见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。

条件 (153.8) 同时支付可用真实标签、实际占据近似、有理值间隔和薄条曲率。它是充分条件，不是必要条件。第 149、151 章的结论保持原范围；本章不声称端点、所有正 $c$、零噪声、最优速率、物理相变或原环境期望收敛。精确率可行集包含旧二次上界允许的集合，并不自动证明每组原参数的最终区间都严格扩大；其他几何约束可能先达到边界。有限原文检索不构成全球原创性证明。

## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）

## 154. 增长编号复零点的弯曲轨迹与统一相位修正

第 152 章控制固定编号的原始有限计数零点。本章同时处理 $|2k+1|\le ct$ 的增长编号集，其中 $c$ 为任意固定有限常数，$t=\eta/\sqrt\delta\to\infty$。局部内点坐标的频率仍有界，但缩放外场的虚部已增长到 $O(t)$；此时二次修正造成有限实位移，第三累积量与二次分支的迭代共同造成 $t^{-1}$ 级虚位移。

证明先在同一原始数组上建立带复振幅的区域积分估计，再证明两个区域变换在指定矩形内非零。解析相位的统一余项给出简单零点定位、精确计数和额外零点排除。有限噪声、经验中心、低计数和完整选择约束均保留，结论属于普通数学推导，未作 Lean 认证。

### 154.1 增长编号零点的统一定位

**定理 154.1（原始选择计数的增长编号复零点）。** An original-count bounded-frequency complex-amplitude expansion gives an O_Prob(t^-2) scaled-field residual. It is obtained by integrating a local density expansion with an exponential mark; fixed polynomial moments alone do not establish this expansion.

At the ACTUAL selected equal-region-mass field h0=h_equal^P(y,xi), let R_c=-D>0. Write b,i for the actual means in the boundary and interior regions, v_B,v_I for their variances and kappa3,B,kappa3,I for their third cumulants. Set

$$

 d=i-b,\qquad A_Q=(v_I-v_B)/d^2,\qquad
 B_Q=(\kappa_{3,I}-\kappa_{3,B})/d^3.
 \tag{154.1}

$$

The symbols A_Q and B_Q here are complex-field coefficients; B_Q is not the original count normalization B. On the common tight-constant data classes,

$$

 d\asymp r_{\rm sc},\quad A_Q>0,\quad
 A_Q=O(t^{-2}),\qquad B_Q=O(t^{-4}).
 \tag{154.2}

$$

For z_k=(2k+1)pi*i, where i in z_k denotes the imaginary unit, define

$$

 z_{G,k}=\frac{2z_k}{1+\sqrt{1-2A_Qz_k}},\qquad
 p_k=z_{G,k}-
 \frac{B_Qz_{G,k}^3}{6(1-A_Qz_{G,k})}.
 \tag{154.3}

$$

The square root is the analytic branch near1. Uniformly for |2k+1|<=c t with each fixed 0<c<infinity, |2A_Qz_k|=O_c(t^-1), so this branch and the denominator in(154.3) are unambiguous. In particular
z_G-A_Q z_G^2/2=z_k. The relevant root is the one near z_k, not the second root of that quadratic.

There is a uniquely labeled simple zero h_k of the EXACT original selected negative-sign finite sum, with

$$

 \sup_{|2k+1|\le ct}
 \left|d(h_k-h_0)-p_k\right|=O_{\rm Prob}(t^{-2}).
 \tag{154.4}

$$

Consequently the supremum of t times the left side tends to zero in probability, and the absolute field error is o_Prob(1/(d t)). The zero count, labeling and boundary conventions are specified in Section 154.7; they exclude additional zeros in the specified rectangles. No union bound over independent realizations is used: the entire growing set is controlled on ONE realized array.

For every fixed 0<L,C<infinity, let

$$

 {\cal S}_{L,C}(t)=\{z:|\operatorname{Re}z|\le L,\quad
                                      |\operatorname{Im}z|\le Ct\}.
 \tag{154.5}

$$

Define the exact centered regional transforms

$$

 M_J(z)=E_{P,J,h_0}e^{-z(R_c-\mu_J)/d},
 \quad \mu_B=b,\quad\mu_I=i,\qquad
 \Phi(z)=e^{bz/d}\frac{N_P^-(h_0+z/d,y)}{N_P^-(h_0,y)}.
 \tag{154.6}

$$

They are entire finite sums, and exactly

$$

 \Phi(z)=\tfrac12[M_B(z)+e^{-z}M_I(z)].
 \tag{154.7}

$$

On(154.5) both regional transforms are nonzero for sufficiently large levels on the good events. Their analytic logarithms H_J, normalized by H_J(0)=0, satisfy

$$

 H_J(z)=\frac{v_Jz^2}{2d^2}
             -\frac{\kappa_{3,J}z^3}{6d^3}
             +O_{\rm Prob}(t^{-2}),\qquad J=B,I,
 \tag{154.8}

$$

uniformly on(154.5). For B alone the remainder is O_Prob(t^-4). Thus, with the exact analytic phase

$$

 \Psi(z)=z-H_I(z)+H_B(z),

$$

$$

 \Psi(z)=z-\tfrac12 A_Qz^2+\tfrac16B_Qz^3
                                    +O_{\rm Prob}(t^{-2}),
 \qquad
 N_P^-(h_0+z/d,y)=
 \frac{N_P^-(h_0,y)e^{-bz/d}M_B(z)}2[1+e^{-\Psi(z)}].
 \tag{154.9}

$$

Every factor outside the last brackets is proved nonzero on the strip. Equation(154.9) is the required analytic approximation and exact normalization; it never divides an error by a vanishing full normalizer.

All suprema and O/little-o statements in this chapter are simultaneous for compact physical y and xi in any fixed permitted separator compact, separately in original actual pair and path data probability and uniformly over deterministic size-q supports. They hold for every admissible sequence, with no universal convergence rate across sequences. Constants are bounded on each inherited tight-constant data class, followed by exhaustion of those classes. Measurable empirical h0,d and other coefficients are covered by the simultaneous bounds, not regarded as independent of the data.

### 154.2 原始计数律与精确有限剖面

To make the law explicit, Q is the original level and Q_x denotes the calibrated auxiliary product COUNT law:

$$

 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q\delta^5,\quad
 Q_x(n)=\prod_j{C_j\choose n_j}p_j^{n_j}(1-p_j)^{C_j-n_j},
 \quad v_j=C_jp_j(1-p_j)/B^2,

$$

$$

 V=\sum_jv_j,\quad C_2=\delta^{-1}\sum_jv_j^2,\quad
 x_j=(n_j-\mu_j)/B,\quad e_j=(\mu_j-C_jp_j)/B,

$$

$$

 E=\sum_jx_j^2,\quad D=\sum_j(x_j+e_j),\quad
 T=(E-V)/\sqrt\delta,\quad
 a=(2V)^{-1}+\eta,\quad t=\eta/\sqrt\delta.
 \tag{154.10}

$$

The original full-q selected prior is P_x. With J0 the union of original observed count groups, k=sum_j n_j and m_J0=sum_j C_jp_j, its LITERAL density relation is

$$

 P_x(n)=L_x(k)Q_x(n),\quad BD=k-m_{J0},\quad
 L_x(k)=
 \frac{[w^{q-k}]\prod_{l\notin J0}(1-p_l+p_lw)}
 {[w^q]\prod_l(1-p_l+p_lw)}.
 \tag{154.11}

$$

Outside Bernoulli labels supply the residual q-k; no D=0 constraint is substituted. All full counts, floors, low tuples, original mu and e, and count boundaries remain present. Our normalizer is exactly

$$

 N_P^-(h,y)=\sum_{D(n)<0}P_x(n)
       e^{aD(n)^2+hD(n)-(T(n)-y)^2/(2\sigma^2)}.
 \tag{154.12}

$$

Retain eta>0 tending to zero, t tending to infinity arbitrarily slowly, and sigma>0 tending to zero under ONLY

$$

 \limsup\frac{\log(1/\sigma)}{Q^3}<c_q/2,\qquad
 \log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),\quad c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta.
 \tag{154.13}

$$

Set m=sqrt(2V^4/C2), r_sc=m sqrt(eta/delta), w0=sqrt(2/3) and h_sc=eta r_sc. The empirical m is bounded above/below on the common classes and is not assumed to converge deterministically. For xi in a compact subset of(0,w0), the boundary region is 0<R_c<=xi r_sc and the interior region is R_c>xi r_sc. Their raw masses are N_P^B,N_P^I, and h0 is their actual local equal-mass field from Chapter 148. Positivity and uniqueness are retained; their exact log-odds derivative is -(i-b)<0.

We retain the SAME exact centered Gaussian noisy profile only as a comparator, never as a replacement for(154.12). Choose the previously admissible high cutoff H={j:C_j>=exp(zeta Q^3)} with log(1/sigma)<=lQ^3 eventually, l<c_q/2 and 2zeta<c_q-l. Let V_H=sum_H v_j, C_H=diag(v_j), b_H=(v_j), d_H=b_H/V_H and A0=C_H-b_Hb_H^T/V_H. Conditional high Gaussian energy at charge r has cumulant transform

$$

 {\cal K}(w,R_0)=-\tfrac12\log\det(I-2wA_0)
   +R_0w d_H^T(I-2wA_0)^{-1}d_H
   +\tfrac12\delta\sigma^2w^2.
 \tag{154.14}

$$

At the full H_y=V+sqrt(delta)y, denote its noisy density by f_r^0(H_y), and put

$$

 g_y^0(r)=e^{\gamma r^2}f_r^0(H_y),\quad
 \gamma=\eta-\{(2V_H)^{-1}-(2V)^{-1}\},\quad
 \ell_y(R_0)=\log g_y^0(\sqrt{R_0}),

$$

$$

 F(r;h,y)=\ell_y(r^2)-\ell_y(0)-hr,\quad
 F_r(r_-;h,y)=0,\quad K=-F_{rr}(r_-;h,y)>0.
 \tag{154.15}

$$

The branch is the retained real local maximum near w0 r_sc. Write

$$

 \Lambda=F(r_-)+\log h+\tfrac12\log(2\pi/K),\quad
 C_B=2\ell_y'(0)/h^2,\quad
 C_I=F''''/(8K^2)+5(F''')^2/(24K^3).
 \tag{154.16}

$$

All quantities in(154.14)--(154.16) retain finite noise, high-block defect, physical output and the full empirical spectrum. No complex energy saddle is used.

The real inputs from Chapters 148 and 150, on every fixed bounded Lambda window, include the raw masses

$$

 N_P^B=\frac{M_0(y)}h[1+C_B+o(t^{-2})],\quad
 N_P^I=\frac{M_0(y)}h e^\Lambda[1+C_I+o(t^{-2})],
 \quad M_0=\sigma\sqrt{\delta/V_H}\,g_y^0(0)\asymp\sigma.
 \tag{154.17}

$$

They also include r_-/r_sc->w0, K/(2eta)->1, h r_sc comparable to t^2; the exact derivatives r_h=-1/K, K_h=F'''/K and Lambda_h=-r_-+1/h-F'''/(2K^2); and interval bounds

$$

 |F^{(j)}|/K^{j/2}\le C_jt^{2-j},\quad 3\le j\le6.
 \tag{154.18}

$$

These come from the exact real Fourier/resolvent representation, including prefactor derivatives, not differentiation of a C0 limit. At real h, put X=hR_c, Z=sqrt K(R_c-r_-), b3=F'''/K^(3/2), b4=F''''/K^2. The retained ORIGINAL selected moments give

$$

 b=h^{-1}(1+O(t^{-2})),\quad v_B=h^{-2}(1+O(t^{-2})),
 \quad \kappa_{3,B}=O(h^{-3}),

$$

$$

 i=r_-+\frac{F'''}{2K^2}+o(1/(\sqrt Kt^2)),\quad
 v_I=K^{-1}(1+O(t^{-2})),\quad
 \kappa_{3,I}=K^{-3/2}\{b3+o(t^{-2})\}.
 \tag{154.19}

$$

Every fixed local polynomial moment is bounded. These facts alone do not prove(154.8); the exponential-amplitude integration follows next.

### 154.3 实内点鞍点上的有界频率展开

Work first at real h in a fixed bounded Lambda window, on the SAME realized array. The exact derivative bounds(154.18) give, for |x|<=t^(1/12),

$$

 F(r_-+x/\sqrt K)-F(r_-)
   =-x^2/2+(b3/6)x^3+O(t^{-2}x^4+t^{-3}|x|^5).
 \tag{154.20}

$$

Thus the full density is exp(-x^2/2)(1+b3 x^3/6) with an integrated error O(t^-2) against any fixed polynomial times exp(C0|x|/t). Indeed on this band the remainder in the full density is bounded by C t^-2 times a fixed polynomial in |x| times exp(-x^2/4). Outside the growing band but within a fixed fractional well neighborhood the exact local concavity gives exp(-c x^2). The complementary moderate-charge band has action loss exp(-ct^2).

For the remaining charges use the SAME centered and actual-e global bound from Chapters 146, 148 and 150:

$$

 g_y^\circ(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}\,u)/g_y^\circ(0)
 \le C\exp\left[t^2\left\{u^2-\frac{c u^4}{1+\eta u^2}\right\}\right]
 \quad(|u|\ge M_1).
 \tag{154.21}

$$

For fixed sufficiently large M1, then sufficiently small eta, this dominates exp(-B0 t^2u^2) for any prescribed fixed B0. The added amplitude below costs only exp(C|u|); it is absorbed in this bound. Since exp(F(r_-))sqrt(2pi/K)=exp(Lambda)/h and F(r_-)=-log t+O(1), normalized tails cost only fixed powers of t, not powers of Q. All omitted tails are smaller than every fixed inverse power of t. This pays arbitrarily slow t.

Let w range over |Im w|<=C0 and |Re w|<=L0/t. Unlike a growing real Laplace argument, this is a bounded local frequency with a vanishing real envelope. For the normalized centered comparator,

$$

 E_I^0e^{-wZ}
 =e^{w^2/2}\left[1-\frac{b3}{6}(w^3+3w)\right]+O_{L0,C0}(t^{-2}).
 \tag{154.22}

$$

To derive it, integrate(154.20) against e^-wx. Its modulus is at most exp(L0|x|/t), so the preceding integrated remainder is uniform. The normalizing correction is O(t^-2), since the first odd Gaussian integral vanishes. The classical exact Gaussian integrals are

$$

 E_ge^{-wG}=e^{w^2/2},\quad
 E_g[G^3e^{-wG}]=-(w^3+3w)e^{w^2/2}.
 \tag{154.23}

$$

They hold for complex w by absolute integrability (or the entire Gaussian transform). We have integrated a proved density remainder; we have not summed moments or differentiated a real asymptotic formula.

### 154.4 原始选择计数的统一复标记回接

We now return(154.22) to the original selected regions with the exponential amplitude still present. This is the additional interface beyond Chapter 150's polynomial marked theorem. The comparison is relative to each POSITIVE REAL region mass, not to a potentially zero characteristic function.

At h0 define, for fixed real |u|<=L, h_u=h0-u/d. The exact derivatives and(154.19) imply

$$

 h_u/h_0=1+O_L(t^{-2}),\quad |\Lambda(h_u,y)|\le L_1,\quad
 |r_-(h_u)-r_-(h_0)|\le C_L/(Kd),\quad K(h_u)/K=1+O_L(t^{-2}).
 \tag{154.24}

$$

The raw same-region ratios N_P^J(h_u)/N_P^J(h0) are bounded above/below by fixed class constants, by(154.17). For every nonnegative tuple function f, exactly

$$

 E_{P,J,h_0}[f e^{uR_c/d}]
 =\frac{N_P^J(h_u)}{N_P^J(h_0)}E_{P,J,h_u}f.
 \tag{154.25}

$$

This gives the exponential-polynomial bounds of Chapter 152:

$$

 E_{P,J,h_0}
 \left[\left|\frac{R_c-\mu_J}{s_J}\right|^p
 e^{L|R_c-\mu_J|/d}\right]\le C_{L,p},
 \quad s_B=1/h_0,\quad s_I=1/\sqrt K.
 \tag{154.26}

$$

For I, the shift of its saddle in sqrt K units is O_L(t^-1); for B, h_u/h0 is bounded. The same real-shift argument applies before selection to the product/comparator masses. It is an exact same-law identity on the full tuple, not an independence assertion.

On the mesoscopic strip(154.5), the complex mark e^{-z(R_c-mu_J)/d} has modulus at most exp(L|R_c-mu_J|/d). Its imaginary part costs NO exponential factor. For the interior saddle variable it is e^-wZ with

$$

 w=z/(d\sqrt K),\quad |\operatorname{Im}w|\le C_0,\quad
 |\operatorname{Re}w|\le L_0/t,
 \tag{154.27}

$$

because d sqrt K is comparable to t. The real mass envelope is still(154.24), regardless of the growing number of frequencies.

Here are the quantitative original-law payments. On each moderate charge compact, the SAME real resolvent interpolation from r d_H to r d_H-e_H gives

$$

 \sup_{|r|\le M_1\sqrt{\eta/\delta},\,|y|\le R}
 |f_r^e(H_y)/f_r^0(H_y)-1|\le C_{M_1}\delta^4.
 \tag{154.28}

$$

In Chapters 148 and 150 this was proved by the exact mean derivative at the same real energy saddle: the exponent change is O(delta^4), and the normalized vertical Fourier-prefactor change is O(delta^(9/2)), under the common variance-block envelope (1+c delta xi^2)^(-c'/delta). This retained quantitative bound can be multiplied by our amplitude: on the moderate compact its modulus is bounded, while local polynomial factors are paid by the shifted real moments. Outside that compact use(154.21) with the SAME actual-e profile. Thus it contributes O(delta^4) with no inverse sigma or inverse oscillatory integral.

Uniformly in EVERY exact low tuple, the retained high-cell estimates are

$$

 |\log(\text{lifted density}/\phi_C)|\le{\cal E}_Q,\quad
 |D-D_G|\le{\cal E}_Q,\quad |T-T_G|/\sigma\le{\cal E}_Q,\quad
 {\cal E}_Q=P(Q)e^{-bQ^3}.
 \tag{154.29}

$$

Here T_G retains full V and e. The exponential mark changes across a cell by at most
C |z|calE_Q/d times its real exponential envelope. Now |z|/d=O(t/d)=O(sqrt eta), so even the growing imaginary frequency creates no new exponential cost. With local polynomial marks, the derivative is a fixed polynomial times this same bound. This is the new cell-frequency check; a bounded-mark claim without this check would not control lattice evaluation.

At the real envelope field h_L=h0-L/d,

$$

 h_LD\le\eta D^2+h_L^2/(4\eta),\qquad h_L^2/(4\eta)=O_L(t^2).
 \tag{154.30}

$$

The joint energy-Fourier estimate of Chapter 137 at a_+=(2V)^-1+2eta controls fixed modal, charge and normalized likelihood-score insertions by sigma P(Q)exp(Ct^2), uniformly for widths in[sigma/2,2sigma]. For b0=(T-T_G)/sigma and u0=(T_G-y)/sigma, the likelihood log difference is -b0u0-b0^2/2. Young's inequality absorbs its exponential factor into a nearby REAL width; its exact log-width score inserts u0^2. Consequently the complex-mark cell error is bounded in absolute value by

$$

 \sigma P_{L,C,p}(Q)e^{-bQ^3+C_{L,C,p}t^2}.
 \tag{154.31}

$$

No inverse-sigma derivative is taken. The original positive margins c_q/2-l, c_q-2zeta-l and the high Stirling margin stay unchanged. Exact low-tuple probabilities are summed only after this uniform estimate.

For excluded tuples, retain D^2<=2n_gE+2(sum|e_j|)^2 and n_g<=Cdelta^-4. Completing the square in the SAME E, together with(154.30), bounds the full weight by

$$

 \exp\{Ct^2+2a_+(\sum|e_j|)^2+2a_+n_gH_y
                   +4a_+^2n_g^2\delta\sigma^2\}
             e^{-(E-H_y)^2/(4\delta\sigma^2)}.
 \tag{154.32}

$$

The first exponent is O(Q^(7/2))+O(t^2), whereas the excluded binomial probability is P(Q)exp(-cQ^4). A fixed polynomial costs at most exp(C_pQ^3); division by sigma costs O(Q^3) under(154.13). The excluded marked error stays exp(-c'Q^4) after each region normalization. Thus extreme finite-count charges are actually paid, rather than dismissed as a bounded-frequency observable.

Each region mass on(154.24) is comparable to sigma/h0. Dividing(154.31) loses only a fixed Q polynomial, since all relevant scales and their inverses are polynomially bounded and t^2=o(Q^(1/2)). Cut disagreement at zero has width calE_Q with a bounded mark; at the separator there is an extra exp(-ct^2) action loss. Charge spacings h0/B, sqrt K/B, and the present frequency spacing |z|/(dB) are exponentially small. This explicitly retains the lattice and floor effects without adding a noise rate.

Finally use the exact full-q selection envelope from Chapter 143, with epsilon=B^2/(2d_c)=O(delta^5):

$$

 0\le L_x\le1+C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}),\qquad
 |L_x-1|\le C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\epsilon D^2).
 \tag{154.33}

$$

Under the real shifted product region law, its expectations with fixed local polynomial marks are at most

$$

 C_p(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\delta^6/\eta^3)\quad(B),
 \qquad
 C_p(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}+\eta\delta^4+\delta^5/\eta)\quad(I).
 \tag{154.34}

$$

These follow from D=-X/h in B and D^2<=2r_-^2+2Z^2/K in I, using two extra SAME-region moments. Multiplying by the complex mark is paid by(154.25) at h_L and bounded same-region mass ratios. All terms in(154.34), and delta^4, are o(t^-2). For example their nontrivial products with t^2 are delta^5/eta, eta^3delta^3 and eta delta^4, all tending to zero for every admitted eta=t sqrt delta.

Together the original count return has uniform absolute normalized error at most

$$

 \epsilon_Q=C_{L,C,p}\{\delta^4+\delta^5+q^{-1/2}
       +\delta^6/\eta^3+\eta\delta^4+\delta^5/\eta\}
       +P_{L,C,p}(Q)e^{-bQ^3+C_{L,C,p}t^2}+o(t^{-A})
       =o(t^{-2})
 \tag{154.35}

$$

for any fixed A>2, with the tail truncations as above. It applies to e^-wZ and any fixed local polynomial times that mark, uniformly over(154.27), BEFORE normalizing either marked integral. The analogous endpoint statement holds. This proof uses real envelopes on the SAME realization throughout; it does not compare independent energy/charge optima or divide a total-law error by a minority mass.

### 154.5 实际累积量、区域非零性与解析余项

Apply(154.22),(154.35) at h0, and let a_Z=E_{P,I,h0}Z. From the retained marked means,
a_Z=b3/2+o(t^-2), Var Z=1+O(t^-2), kappa3(Z)=b3+o(t^-2). Since w is bounded on(154.27),

$$

 M_I(z)=e^{w a_Z}E_{P,I,h0}e^{-wZ}
 =e^{w^2/2}\left[1-\frac{b3}{6}w^3+O_{L,C}(t^{-2})\right].
 \tag{154.36}

$$

The linear 3w term in(154.22) cancels against exact actual centering; an uncentered transform would give a wrong phase correction. The Gaussian factor has modulus bounded above and bounded AWAY from zero on(154.27). Since b3=O(t^-1), the bracket is uniformly within O(t^-1) of1. Thus M_I has no zeros on the whole rectangle(154.5), and its analytic logarithm with value0 at0 exists. Expanding log of that bracket and using the actual variance and third cumulant gives

$$

 H_I(z)=\frac{v_Iz^2}{2d^2}
          -\frac{\kappa_{3,I}z^3}{6d^3}+O_{L,C}(t^{-2}).
 \tag{154.37}

$$

Replacing the local variance1 by Var Z costs O(t^-2), not a hidden order-one variance substitution. No claim that M_I is globally nonvanishing is made.

For the endpoint use the exact complex Taylor remainder

$$

 \left|e^u-\sum_{j=0}^3u^j/j!\right|
 \le |u|^4e^{\max(0,\operatorname{Re}u)}/24.
 \tag{154.38}

$$

This integral-remainder bound depends on Re u in the exponential, not |u|. Taking u=-z(R_c-b)/d and using(154.26) with p=4 gives a remainder
O(|z|^4/(h0 d)^4)=O(t^-4) on(154.5), since h0 d is comparable to t^2. Hence

$$

 M_B(z)=1+\frac{v_Bz^2}{2d^2}
       -\frac{\kappa_{3,B}z^3}{6d^3}+O(t^{-4}).
 \tag{154.39}

$$

Here the quadratic term is O(t^-2) and the cubic is O(t^-3). Thus M_B is uniformly close to1 and nonzero; taking the normalized analytic logarithm proves its sharper version of(154.8). This use of(154.26),(154.38) does not demand a real field shift of order t/d.

Equations(154.37),(154.39) prove(154.8)--(154.9). They are uniform analytic assertions on every fixed-width strip of height Ct, not only on its imaginary axis. Enlarge L by2 and the height by2 before applying Cauchy's formula on unit disks. On the inner rectangle the analytic error E_Q(z)=Psi(z)-[z-A_Q z^2/2+B_Q z^3/6] and each fixed derivative satisfy

$$

 |E_Q(z)|+|E_Q'(z)|\le C_{L,C}t^{-2}.
 \tag{154.40}

$$

This derivative bound follows from a proved complex-uniform remainder, not formal differentiation of a real approximation. In particular

$$

 \sup_{{\cal S}_{L,C}(t)}|\Psi'(z)-1|=O_{L,C}(t^{-1}).
 \tag{154.41}

$$

On each such convex rectangle Psi is injective eventually: integration on the straight segment gives
|Psi(z)-Psi(w)-(z-w)|<|z-w|/2 for distinct z,w. This supplies uniqueness without an unproved logarithmic branch or root-separation premise.

### 154.6 二次分支与首个偏度修正

Let P3(z)=z-A_Q z^2/2+B_Q z^3/6. For |2k+1|<=ct, the branch z_G in(154.3) satisfies

$$

 |z_G-z_k|=O_c(1),\quad |z_G|=O_c(t),\quad
 |1-A_Qz_G|\ge1/2.
 \tag{154.42}

$$

The cubic displacement is q_k=-B_Q z_G^3/[6(1-A_Qz_G)]=O_c(t^-1).
Expanding the EXPLICIT polynomial P3 at z_G, using its quadratic equation, gives

$$

 P3(p_k)-z_k=O_c(t^{-3}).
 \tag{154.43}

$$

Indeed the term B_Q z_G^3/6 cancels (1-A_Qz_G)q_k; the remaining leading product is B_Q z_G^2 q_k/2=O(t^-3), and A_Q q_k^2=O(t^-4). This independently checks the MINUS sign of the skewness correction.

Equation(154.40) now gives Psi(p_k)-z_k=O(t^-2). Uniformly on a circle |z-p_k|=C1/t^2, P3(z)-z_k has modulus at least C1/(2t^2) after increasing the fixed class constant C1, whereas |E_Q(z)| is smaller. First compare P3-z_k with P3'(p_k)(z-p_k): the constant residual is O(t^-3), the quadratic remainder is O(t^-6), and P3'(p_k)=1+O(t^-1). Rouché therefore gives exactly one polynomial root in the disk. A second comparison with Psi-z_k gives one zero of that function there. The disks are disjoint because their centers have spacing2pi*i+O(t^-1), while their radii tend to zero. The exact factorization(154.9) and(154.41) imply that each is a SIMPLE zero of N_P^-.

Every inequality is a single uniform one over the full strip and all eligible indices. There is no accumulation of O(t) separate error probabilities. Dividing the location residual C1/t^2 by d proves(154.4). This is an O_Prob(t^-2) residual with actual cumulants, not only an o(1) location from leading phase cancellation.

### 154.7 精确零点计数与边界约定

We state a convenient count domain explicitly. On a common data class let a_max be a fixed upper bound for A_Q t^2 (distinct from the penalty a_+ in Section 154.4). Given the target c, choose C>pi*c+3 and a fixed

$$

 L>2+a_{\max} C^2/2.
 \tag{154.44}

$$

The analytic proof holds on a still larger rectangle. For any integer N>=1 with 2pi N<=Ct-2, consider

$$

 \Omega_N(t)=\{z:|\operatorname{Re}z|<L,\quad
                                  |\operatorname{Im}z|<2\pi N\}.
 \tag{154.45}

$$

There are exactly 2N zeros there, all simple, one for each k=-N,...,N-1, and no boundary zeros. This is simultaneous for every such N on that realization.

For detail, if z=x+iy with |x|<=L, |y|<=Ct, the explicit real coefficients and(154.40) imply

$$

 \operatorname{Im}\Psi(z)=y+O_{L,C}(t^{-1}),\qquad
 \operatorname{Re}\Psi(z)=x+\tfrac12 A_Qy^2+O_{L,C}(t^{-2}).
 \tag{154.46}

$$

On x=L the real part is positive; on x=-L it is negative by(154.44). On the horizontal sides, the imaginary part is within O(t^-1) of an EVEN multiple of pi, so it cannot be an odd multiple. Thus no boundary zero is possible. Any zero inside must satisfy Psi(z)=z_k for one of k=-N,...,N-1. Injectivity(154.41) permits at most one for each. The predictions(154.3) for all these k lie inside with fixed horizontal and vertical margins, and Section 154.6 supplies one for each. This proves the exact count and excludes any unlisted zeros.

For the index set of Theorem 154.1 take N_Q=floor(c t/2)+1. It obeys(154.45) eventually and contains every index |2k+1|<=ct. The rectangle can intentionally include at most the extra boundary labels dictated by this rounding; its exact count remains2N_Q. This is not an assertion that a rectangle cut at an arbitrary height Ct always encloses an integer number prescribed by an unrounded threshold.

For other domains contained in the proved rectangle, the same localization gives the precise boundary rule: if the distance from the boundary to every relevant prediction p_k is much larger than t^-2 on the common class, the count is exactly the number of predictions inside, including multiplicity. A fixed positive margin, or t^-3/2, suffices. No count is asserted when the boundary is allowed to pass through an actual zero or approach its prediction at the unresolved remainder scale. Outside the union of the O(t^-2) disks about the listed p_k there are no zeros in(154.45).

The label respects exact conjugation: h_{-k-1}=conjugate(h_k). Choice of separator changes h0 and d only as allowed by Chapters 148 and 150, while the entire function(154.12) is separator-independent. The predictive exact-profile form below is common to all separators and has an o(1/t) scaled error; its disks for neighboring labels remain disjoint. Thus the labeled zeros refer to the same finite sum for every permitted separator, not to unrelated coordinate-specific roots.

These are mesoscopic LOCAL statements in fixed real widths and imaginary heights O(t). They imply no global nearest-zero, circle, thermodynamic analyticity-radius or maximal-index assertion.

### 154.8 有限剖面预测与弯曲零点轨迹

Actual cumulants in(154.3) already give the stated accuracy. A prediction using exact finite profile quantities is also available at the required accuracy. Let h_W solve Lambda(h_W,y)=0, and evaluate r_W,K_W,F'''_W,C_B,C_I there. Set

$$

 c_W=(C_I-C_B)_W,\quad
 g_W=F'''_W/(2K_W^2)-1/h_W,\quad
 d_* =r_W+g_W,

$$

$$

 A_*=(K_W d_*^2)^{-1},\qquad
 B_* =F'''_W/(K_W^3d_*^3).
 \tag{154.47}

$$

For large levels d_*>0. Define z_G,* and p_k,* by(154.3) with A_*,B_* in place of A_Q,B_Q. Then uniformly over |2k+1|<=ct,

$$

 h_k=h_W+\frac{c_W}{r_W}+\frac{p_{k,*}}{d_*}
                       +o_{\rm Prob}(1/(r_Wt)).
 \tag{154.48}

$$

Every quantity on the right is an EXACT finite noisy-profile quantity. In particular h_W and r_W have not been replaced by their bare quartic limits.

Here are the error payments for(154.48). The real results from Chapters 148 and 150 and exact field derivatives give

$$

 h_0-h_W=c_W/r_W+o(1/(r_Wt^2)),\quad
 r_-(h_0)-r_W=O(r_W/t^4),\quad
 d-d_*=o(r_W/t^3)+O(r_W/t^4).
 \tag{154.49}

$$

The last assertion uses the sharper interior mean error in(154.19); the boundary 2C_B/h correction is O(r_W/t^4). Further,

$$

 v_I-v_B=K_W^{-1}[1+O(t^{-2})],\quad
 \kappa_{3,I}-\kappa_{3,B}
   =F'''_W/K_W^3+o(K_W^{-3/2}t^{-2})+O(h_W^{-3}).
 \tag{154.50}

$$

It follows that A_Q-A_*=O(t^-4) and
B_Q-B_*=o(t^-5)+O(t^-6). In the quadratic inverse, a change Delta A moves z_G by O(|Delta A|t^2), hence O(t^-2). The skewness error contributes o(t^-2), and its response to Delta A is smaller. Finally |p_k|=O(t), so the change from d to d_* in the field location is o(1/(r_Wt^2)), already below the stated scale. This proves(154.48) with all common slow-noise terms retained.

For a geometric interpretation, set omega_k=(2k+1)pi, w_k=omega_k/t, and retain the EXACT actual coefficients

$$

 \alpha_Q=t^2 A_Q,\qquad \beta_Q=t^4 B_Q.

$$

Expanding only the explicit prediction(154.3), uniformly on bounded w_k, gives

$$

 d(h_k-h_0)=i\omega_k-\frac{\alpha_Q w_k^2}{2}
   +\frac{i w_k^3}{t}\left(\frac{\beta_Q}{6}
                                  -\frac{\alpha_Q^2}{2}\right)
   +O_{\rm Prob}(t^{-2}).
 \tag{154.51}

$$

The real locus curves to the negative side because the interior conditional amplitude damps like exp(-v_I omega^2/(2d^2)) and the boundary amplitude has much smaller damping. Equal modulus in(154.7) therefore requires a negative real field shift. The term -alpha_Q^2/2 is the iteration of the quadratic root, and beta_Q/6 is the first non-Gaussian phase correction. Omitting either loses order1/t at indices of order t. At fixed k these effects have different smaller orders, which explains why Chapter 152's fixed-index formula cannot simply be substituted at growing k.

The finite-empirical derivative scalings give

$$

 \alpha_Q=\frac3{4m^2}+o(1),\qquad
 \beta_Q=-\frac9{4m^4}+o(1).
 \tag{154.52}

$$

For the second identity, kappa3,I=F'''/K^3 to the needed leading precision, F'''=-12delta r_-/m^2[1+o(1)], K=2eta[1+o(1)], and r_-^2=(2/3)m^2 eta/delta[1+o(1)]. Direct substitution yields t^4 kappa3,I/d^3=-9/(4m^4)+o(1); the endpoint term vanishes on this scale. Thus(154.51) also implies

$$

 \operatorname{Re}\{d(h_k-h_0)\}
       =-\alpha_Q w_k^2/2+O_{\rm Prob}(t^{-2}),\qquad
 \operatorname{Im}\{d(h_k-h_0)\}
       =\omega_k-\frac{21w_k^3}{32m^4t}
                                  +o_{\rm Prob}(t^{-1}).
 \tag{154.53}

$$

One must NOT replace alpha_Q in the first formula by3/(4m^2) when claiming o(1/t) precision: its unspecified o(1) error could be larger. Likewise(154.52) gives no deterministic m limit. Formula(154.48), or the exact actual coefficients in(154.3),(154.51), is the predictive statement at the full stated accuracy. Equations(154.52)--(154.53) separate interpretation from a stronger unjustified limiting-quartic substitution.

### 154.9 方法归属与范围

Gaussian 变换恒等式、局部 Edgeworth／Hermite 展开、非零解析函数的对数以及 Rouché 零点稳定性均为经典方法。本章的模型接口是 (154.24)–(154.35)：在相同区域的实正质量下归一化，保留复标记在格点单元内的频率变化，并支付原始完整选择律、非中心性与尾部误差。区域特征变换的非零性由 (154.36)–(154.40) 另行证明，实质量为正本身不保证这一点。

Song 的一致 Edgeworth 定理要求独立三角阵与所有充分高频上的共同弱 Cramér 常数，不能直接用在此处经能量和选择条件化的格点电荷上。Biskup–Borgs–Chayes–Kleinwaks–Kotecký 的两相零点理论另需其解析非零有限体积相近似与复余项控制，本章未借用这些未经履行的格点相图假设。原始版本、定理条件与读取范围见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。

结论在固定实宽、虚高 $O(t)$ 的缩放矩形内成立，并明确区分预测误差尺度与计数边界的距离。精确系数不能在未控制收敛速度时替换为极限四次剖面；经验参数 $m$ 也未被假定有确定极限。第 148、150、152 章结论保持原范围。本章不包含增长实宽、更快编号、全复平面零点、全局最近零点、Lee–Yang 圆定理、热力学解析半径或未条件化响应；有限检索不构成全球原创性证明。

## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）

## 155. 抽样比例控制联合占据误差，几何上限决定现有带宽端点

第 153 章把稀有总数、分数位移和后验带宽写成同一个可行性问题。本章证明两个不同的结果：整个增长维占据向量的 Poisson 比较可以只支付抽样比例及其平方根，从而扩大可用的稀有总数集合；但原始参数关系使旧率约束已被更严格的几何上限遮住，因此这一改进不扩大现有充分带宽区间。

所有结论分别适用于原始独立配对与平稳路径实验，对确定真支撑和原有合法取整一致。选池只是证明中的揭示操作；物理数组、完整选择后验、低计数组、经验中心和同一残余噪声均保留。以下为普通数学推导，未作 Lean 认证。

### 155.1 联合近似与带宽端点的不同结论

**定理 155.1（增长计数向量的共同近似）。** For m predetermined disjoint lawful true-label pairs, the entire4m-dimensional departure-count vector has an independent-Poisson comparison with error

$$
 \tau_m\le {8m\over M}+\sqrt{{48m\over M}}.                 \tag{155.1}
$$

The assertion holds for all sufficiently large Q and every2m<=q, including exponentially large m. It also holds jointly with the actual parity record and terminal/arrival labels in the precise sense of Section 155.4. It is NOT an assertion of independence of actual rows, and is not used after conditioning on pool masks or outside labels. The latter revealment has its own EXACT product-binomial kernel, proved in Section 155.5.

Consequently Chapter 153's sufficient joint rate condition can be replaced by

$$
 I(x)<c_q,\qquad 2c<\ell(x)<\mathfrak h,                  \tag{155.2}
$$

removing c_M/3 and the old quadratic-in-m coupling cost. Sections 155.5–155.8 prove sufficiency for the same full original weighted-L1 theorem.

**命题 155.2（保留几何约束时的带宽端点）。** Under the geometric and physical obligations of Chapter 153, improving this coupling does not enlarge the sufficient bandwidth interval. In fact, for EVERY originally admissible parameter choice, the old and new variational intervals are IDENTICAL:

$$
 c_{\rm old}=c_{\rm new}=c_*={\mathfrak h\over2}
             ={c_q\over4}-{5\kappa\over2}>0.             \tag{155.3}
$$

Section 155.6 proves this by analytic inequalities under the original amplitude relation. Thus the theorem at rho comparable exp(-cQ^3) holds for every0<c<c_*, but this bandwidth range was already implicit in Chapter 153. The new substantive facts are the growing-vector actual-law approximation, the expanded set of lawful rare-total targets, and the proof that the former coupling constraint was already masked by the geometric cap.

To state the original conclusion exactly, retain

$$
 \lambda=Q^3,\quad\delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q/Q^{5/2},
 \quad\mathcal B=q/Q^{11/4},\quad \rho=\sigma\mathcal B,
$$
$$
 T=\mathcal B^{-1}\sum_j(R_j-\mu_j)^2-V/\sqrt\delta,\quad
 Y=T+\sigma G,\quad A=V_H/\sqrt\delta,\quad
 \nu_0=2\sum_{j\in H}w_j^2,\quad
 \kappa_3=8\sum_{j\in H}w_j^3,\quad\Lambda=\nu_0+\sigma^2,
$$
$$
 C_x=A^2\kappa_3/\Lambda^3-2A\nu_0/\Lambda^2,\qquad
 D_x(y)=Vpost_x(y)-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xy,
$$
$$
 R_*(y)=29/6-3\sqrt2+(3\sqrt2+8/\sqrt3-9)y^2/\nu,
 \qquad \nu=2g_0.                                      \tag{155.4}
$$

For fixed positive bounds on rho exp(cQ^3), c in(0,c_*), we obtain in support-uniform original raw-data probability

$$
 \int_{\mathbb R} f_x(y)|D_x(y)-R_*(y)|\,dy\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad E_xY^2\longrightarrow\nu,                        \tag{155.5}
$$
$$
 \int f_x(y)Vpost_x(y)\,dy-Vprior_x+A^2/\Lambda-C_xm_x
                  \longrightarrow8/\sqrt3-25/6,
 \qquad m_x=E_xY.                                      \tag{155.6}
$$

Vprior_x and m_x are exact finite selected full-count quantities. All counts, multiplicities, low/outside terms, original physical H and scalar, empirical centers, full-q prior and SAME residual G are retained. Pool selection is solely a proof operation on the raw array. There is no new physical selection, phase randomization or replacement posterior. No endpoint, sharpness, necessity, all-c or phase-transition statement follows.

### 155.2 原始参数关系和共同率函数

Definition 68.1 retains fixed beta in(1/2,1). It specifies

$$
 d_1=1,\quad d_{n+1}=10^{5d_n},\quad Q_n=10^{d_n},\quad
 P_n=\sum_{l\le n}10^{d_n-d_l},\quad
 \alpha=\sum_{l\ge1}10^{-d_l}
       ={\log(1+r)\over-\log(1-r)}.                      \tag{155.7}
$$

The original r is tied to its original Liouville score relation. An arbitrary amplitude or beta outside (1/2,1) would describe a different experiment. The masking proof below holds for every0<r<1 and every beta>1/2, so it covers the actual restricted amplitude without changing it.

Use Chapter 153's notation

$$
 a_0=(1+r)/2,\ b_0=(1-r)/2,\quad v_\pm=1\pm r,\quad
 A_s=\log(1+r),\ B_s=\log(1-r),
$$
$$
 \phi=a_0A_s+b_0B_s,\quad
 c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta,\quad c_M=\phi/\beta,\quad
 \kappa=\min(1,c_q,\phi)/1000,
$$
$$
 \mathfrak h=\min(\phi,c_q/2-5\kappa),\qquad
 \mathfrak p_{\rm old}=\min(c_q,c_M/3).                  \tag{155.8}
$$

Then log q=c_q lambda+O(1), log M=c_M lambda+O(1), and q/M=exp(-phi lambda+O(1)), with every original legal floor retained. Since beta>1/2, c_q<phi, so h=c_q/2-5kappa>=0.495c_q>0. Here and below h written as mathfrak h is the geometric cap; a separate h_s denotes a hidden-split cutoff.

For fixed positive total limits x=(x_+,x_-), define

$$
 J_v(z)=z\log(z/v)-z+v,\quad
 I(x)=J_{v_+}(x_+)+J_{v_-}(x_-),\quad
 \ell(x)=\tfrac12[A_s(x_+-v_+)+B_s(x_--v_-)].             \tag{155.9}
$$

Rate and score always use the same pair x. The exact constrained minimum from (153.9)–(153.10) is

$$
 \Psi(s)=\sum_\pm v_\pm(e^{sd_\pm}-1-sd_\pm),\quad
 d_+=A_s/2,\ d_-=B_s/2,\quad
 x_\pm(s)=v_\pm e^{sd_\pm},
$$
$$
 \ell=\Psi'(s),\qquad F(\ell)=s\Psi'(s)-\Psi(s),\quad s\ge0.
                                                               \tag{155.10}
$$

F is continuous, strictly increasing on positive ell, and tends to infinity. This follows from Psi''>0 and F'(ell)=s. For any x with the same ell, I(x)-I(x(s))=sum J_{x_\pm(s)}(x_\pm)>=0. For p>0 write ell_p=F^{-1}(p). The old and proposed new endpoints are respectively
c_old=one-half min(h,ell_pold) and c_new=one-half min(h,ell_cq). Section 155.6 proves their equality.

### 155.3 一个总数控制整个分类向量

We use event total variation dTV(P,Q)=sup_E|P(E)-Q(E)|, half the L1 norm. Classical binomial/Poisson approximation has an order-p bound uniform in the number of trials. For clarity a sufficient explicit bound, including its proof, is given here:

$$
 dTV(Bin(n,p),Pois(np))\le2p,\qquad n\ge0,\ 0\le p\le1/4.
                                                               \tag{155.11}
$$

The constant2 is not claimed optimal. The order in p, rather than np^2, is the essential point. The proof is the likelihood-ratio maximum method in Le Cam's original Section 5, specialized to integer n; it needs no asymptotic n or bounded np.

If n=0 or p=0 the distance is zero. If theta=np<=2, independently couple each Bernoulli(p) with Pois(p). Their exact distance is p(1-e^-p)<=p^2. Summation is a probability kernel, so dTV<=np^2<=2p.

Suppose theta>2. On0<=k<=n the mass ratio to Pois(theta) is
R(k)=(n)_k n^-k (1-p)^(n-k)e^(np), and
R(k+1)/R(k)=(n-k)/(n(1-p)).
Its maximum occurs at k=ceil(theta), with the adjacent tie allowed if theta is integral. Here u=k/n<=p+1/n<3p/2<=3/8, so k<n. The classical finite Stirling inequalities

$$
 \log(j!)=(j+\tfrac12)\log j-j+\tfrac12\log(2\pi)+e_j,
 \qquad0<e_j<1/(12j)\quad(j\ge1)
$$

give, by direct cancellation,

$$
 \log R(k)=-nJ_{1-p}(1-u)-\tfrac12\log(1-u)+e_n-e_{n-k}.
$$

Since J>=0,1/n<p/2, and -log(1-u)<=u/(1-u),

$$
 \log R(k)\le {u\over2(1-u)}+{1\over12n}
 \le {6p\over5}+{p\over24}={149p\over120}<{5p\over4}.
$$

Also e^(5p/4)<=e^(5/16)<3/2: log(3/2)>=1/3>5/16 follows by integrating1/(1+t) on[0,1/2]. Thus R(k)-1<=e^(5p/4)(5p/4)<15p/8<2p. Summing only the positive part of Bin-Pois bounds event total variation by max R-1. This proves(155.11) in all cases. Its constants are uniform even when the conditional sample size is zero or extremely large.

Now take n categorical trials with selected-cell probabilities p_1,...,p_D, total p<=1/4, and one unselected category of probability1-p. The selected vector Z has total K~Bin(n,p). Conditional on K=k it has distribution Mult(k;p_1/p,...,p_D/p). Independent Poisson coordinates with means np_i have total Pois(np) and EXACTLY the same conditional allocation kernel. The fibers{sum Z_i=k} are disjoint. Summing absolute masses on each fiber therefore proves the identity, not just an inequality,

$$
 dTV(\mathcal L(Z),\bigotimes_{i\le D}Pois(np_i))
       =dTV(Bin(n,p),Pois(np))\le2p.                     \tag{155.12}
$$

For p=0 both are point masses at the zero vector. The identity has no D-dependent constant, no hidden np^2 and no lower bound on any p_i. It is the new representation used here: all selected cells share ONE total-count comparison.

For later use, the exact affinity of finite independent Poisson vectors is

$$
 \operatorname{Aff}\left(\bigotimes_iPois(\mu_i),
                         \bigotimes_iPois(\nu_i)\right)
       =\exp[-D(\mu,\nu)/2],\quad
 D(\mu,\nu)=\sum_i(\sqrt{\mu_i}-\sqrt{\nu_i})^2.           \tag{155.13}
$$

Indeed summing the square root of the two one-coordinate masses gives
exp[-(mu+nu)/2]sum_k(sqrt(mu nu))^k/k!=exp[-(sqrt mu-sqrt nu)^2/2], including zero means; multiply over coordinates. Cauchy–Schwarz applied to
|P-Q|=|sqrt P-sqrt Q|(sqrt P+sqrt Q) gives
dTV<=sqrt(1-Aff^2)<=sqrt D.
For random mean vectors, convexity of total variation under a common mixture and Jensen give E dTV<=sqrt(E D). It is not legitimate to replace that common mixture by independently chosen marginal means. These identities are classical; Section 155.9 gives their source and zero-intensity scope.

### 155.4 实际奇偶槽位上的联合均值比较

Let T_obs=2Mlambda denote the original number of observations, distinct from the physical scalar T in(155.4). The actual aligned transition kernel is

$$
 P_S(i,j)={1+b_S(i)\chi(j)\over2M},\quad
 b_S=r1_S-\epsilon_M1_{C_+\setminus S},\quad
 b_S|_{C_-}=0,\quad\epsilon_M=rq/(M-q).
                                                               \tag{155.14}
$$

The sum of b_S in each parity class is zero. For a stationary path, its full density is a product of these factors with uniform initial law. Conditional on its entire parity record s_0,...,s_T, it factors into independent departure-label choices with probabilities

$$
 1_{\{\chi(i)=s_t\}}[1+b_S(i)s_{t+1}]/M\quad(t<T_obs),
$$

and an independent terminal label uniform on its specified class. Summing the departure weights in each class gives1, so the parity record is exactly iid fair. Changing a departure label within its class does not change its predecessor's parity argument. This verifies the exact conditional factorization for paths rather than treating dependent rows as independent. For independent pairs, each parity pair is iid uniform; conditional departures have the same weights and arrivals are independent uniform labels in the indicated classes. This is the conditional disintegration of Chapters 147 and 153, obtained here directly from its density.

Fix S and choose2m distinct true labels by deterministic ordering, paired into m pools. All lie in the lawful original C_+ true-label class. Conditional on parity, only two types can hit them:
(s_t,s_{t+1})=(+,+) and(+,-).
Let N_+,N_- be their slot counts. Their means equal
n_bar=T_obs/4=Mlambda/2. In both experiments Var(N_epsilon)<=3T_obs is a uniform conservative bound. For pairs use independent indicators. For paths each indicator depends on two consecutive iid parity bits; nonadjacent indicators are independent, each variance and each absolute adjacent covariance are at most1/4, which in fact gives3T_obs/4. The weaker displayed bound suffices. N_+ and N_- need not be independent.

For type epsilon, each selected label has probability v_epsilon/M, so its total selected probability is
p_epsilon=2m v_epsilon/M. Since2m<=q and q/M tends to zero, both p_epsilon<=1/4 eventually, uniformly over every such m. Apply(155.12) CONDITIONALLY on the one common parity record. The two type-arrays are independent given that record because they use disjoint independent slot choices. Their joint conditional comparison costs at most

$$
 2(p_++p_-)=8m/M.                                      \tag{155.15}
$$

It compares the entire4m selected count vector with independent Poisson coordinates of random means
mu_{i,epsilon}=v_epsilon N_epsilon/M, i<=2m.
It is uniform in every parity record, including N_epsilon=0.

We next remove the random means jointly, not one coordinate at a time by addition coupling. The target means are
nu_{i,epsilon}=v_epsilon n_bar/M=v_epsilon lambda/2.
Equation(155.13) gives

$$
 D=\sum_{\epsilon=\pm}{2m v_\epsilon\over M}
                       (\sqrt{N_\epsilon}-\sqrt{n_{\rm bar}})^2
 \le\sum_{\epsilon=\pm}{2m v_\epsilon\over M}
                       {(N_\epsilon-n_{\rm bar})^2\over n_{\rm bar}}.
$$

The inequality is valid at N_epsilon=0 and uses only n_bar>0. With sum v_epsilon=2 and Var N_epsilon<=3T_obs,

$$
 ED\le48m/M,\qquad E\,dTV(Pois(\mu),Pois(\nu))
                       \le\sqrt{48m/M}.                \tag{155.16}
$$

No high-probability parity event is introduced, and no probability of a zero/small count is discarded. Combining(155.15–16) proves(155.1). More precisely the bound holds between the joint law of (parity,selected counts) and the law obtained by sampling the same parity record and then a deterministic-mean product-Poisson vector independent of it. Conditional terminal labels or pair arrivals can be adjoined using their common original kernel, so the same bound holds with those variables too. Conditional independence follows from the original density, not from this total-variation estimate.

For the original T_obs=2Mlambda there is no deterministic mean defect. The floors in M,q and the count-line center do not change the true-label slot probability v_epsilon/M. If one separately considers a bounded integer rounding T_obs=2Mlambda+Delta with |Delta|<=C, the same calculation with n_bar=T_obs/4 followed by(155.13) costs an additional C_r sqrt(m)/(M sqrt(lambda)), since the sum of squared square-root mean errors is O_r(m/(M^2lambda)). This is a stated optional rounding bound, not a new rate condition. It is not needed for the authorized exact T_obs.

Uniformity is explicit: the fixed true weights do not depend on the identities of S; the parity law and variance bound are independent of S; dimension appears only through m/M. In particular for all m<=q/2 the bound is at most C exp(-phi lambda/2+O(1)). This is much stronger than a family of marginal row approximations. It is a bounded-event tool on the original raw data, not an approximation of the posterior or its surprise.

We do NOT assert(155.1) conditionally on all outside labels or pool masks. Those refinements can determine the selected totals and would invalidate that assertion. The next section uses the actual refined conditional kernel instead. Keeping these two roles distinct is essential.

### 155.5 稀有总数选池和精确隐藏条件律

Fix x with I(x)<c_q and2c<ell(x)<h. In each predetermined pool flag exactly
K_+=floor(lambda x_+), K_-=floor(lambda x_-).
For v,x>0 define
D_v(x)=max(|log(x/(2v))|,|log(x/v)|),
k_v(x)=exp(-D_v(x))/(3sqrt x).
For lambda>=2/x, the finite Stirling upper bound n!<=3sqrt n(n/e)^n and J_v'(z)=log(z/v) give

$$
 P\{Pois(v\lambda)=\lfloor x\lambda\rfloor\}
       \ge k_v(x)\lambda^{-1/2}e^{-\lambda J_v(x)}.       \tag{155.17}
$$

To check the floor, n/lambda lies in[x/2,x] and
|lambda J_v(n/lambda)-lambda J_v(x)|<=D_v(x).
The matching Stirling lower bound gives the same exponential rate and a fixed O_{v,x}(1) logarithmic remainder. These are exact compact-region large-deviation estimates, not half-mean or Gaussian-window approximations.

Set k(x)=k_{v_+}(x_+)k_{v_-}(x_-), and take

$$
 m=\left\lceil k(x)^{-1}\lambda Q^2e^{I(x)\lambda}\right\rceil,
 \qquad\log m=I(x)\lambda+5\log Q+O_x(1).                \tag{155.18}
$$

Under the single product-Poisson comparison, pooling the two labels yields independent Pois(v_+lambda), Pois(v_-lambda) totals in every pool, and flags of different pools are independent. The no-flag probability is at most exp(-Q^2). Since I<c_q,2m/q tends to zero, so the original true-label supply suffices. The actual no-flag probability is therefore at most

$$
 e^{-Q^2}+{8m\over M}+\sqrt{{48m\over M}}=o(1).          \tag{155.19}
$$

The two new coupling exponents are I-c_M and (I-c_M)/2, plus O_x(log Q). They are strictly negative because I<c_q<c_M. There is no division by the single-pool probability and no m-fold hidden-split union.

Here is the exact revealment that permits subsequent calibration. Reveal parity, all pool membership masks of departure slots, all labels outside their union, and the terminal path label or pair arrivals. This is one sigma-field H_0, and every flagged TOTAL is measurable in it. Within a chosen true pair the two conditional slot weights coincide. Hence conditional on H_0 the full allocation strings for all pools are jointly independent fair-bit strings. Their count projections have law

$$
 \bigotimes_{i\le m}
       [Bin(K_{i,+},1/2)\otimes Bin(K_{i,-},1/2)].         \tag{155.20}
$$

Choose the first flagged index I using only H_0; use index1 and keep the no-flag event if none exists. Then reveal all other pools' internal allocations and call the resulting field F. For a bounded test of the selected allocation, partition by{I=i}. On that event the conditional product kernel(155.20) integrates all other coordinates separately, leaving the two factors at i. A monotone-class argument over tests measurable in H_0 joined with those other coordinates, followed by summing the finite partition, proves that conditional on F the selected pair still has exactly those two binomial factors. This holds for F-measurable target sets too. Although m grows, it is finite for each Q and the identity has no dimension constant.

No favorable split was used to choose I. The product-Poisson approximation has finished its role before this revealment and is not conditioned forward. The calibration and candidate targets may depend on all other revealed allocations, but the chosen pair's conditional kernel remains exact.

With the original compensated scores
a_s=log((1+r)/(1-epsilon_M)), b_s=log((1-r)/(1+epsilon_M)),
B_0=(M-q)/q, the exact flagged totals give

$$
 t_{\rm raw}=(a_sK_++b_sK_-)/2-\log B_0
                  =\ell(x)\lambda+O_x(1).              \tag{155.21}
$$

The error O(lambda q/M) tends to zero; all original floors contribute only O_x(1). Given F let
X=a_s(k-K_+/2)+b_s(l-K_-/2). For any fixed
0<h_s<ell-2c, with V_x=2(A_s^2x_++B_s^2x_-+1), the fair-binomial exponential moment and cosh z<=exp(z^2/2) yield

$$
 P(|X|>h_s\lambda\mid F)\le2e^{-2h_s^2\lambda/V_x}.      \tag{155.22}
$$

This is paid once, tends to zero for every allowed fixed x,c, and covers the entire selected conditional law. Both totals remain in fixed positive compact multiples of lambda, however large their fixed shift. No growing-deletion expansion or growing local expansion order appears.

### 155.6 几何上限掩盖旧率约束的解析证明

Weak inclusion is immediate because p_old<=c_q. To settle whether it is strict at the bandwidth level, it is enough to evaluate F at the retained geometric cap. We prove the stronger uniform estimates

$$
 F(\mathfrak h)<{9\over16}c_q,\qquad
 F(\mathfrak h)<{27\over32}(c_M/3).                     \tag{155.23}
$$

These constants are analytic bounds, not numerical fits.

First, for0<r<1,
phi=one-half[(1+r)log(1+r)+(1-r)log(1-r)]
=sum_{k>=1}r^(2k)/[2k(2k-1)].
The positive coefficients sum to log2<1, by taking r upwards to1, so phi<r^2. Next
log(1+r)>=2r/(2+r), since the derivative of their difference is
r^2/[(1+r)(2+r)^2]>=0. Consequently

$$
 a_0A_s^2\ge {2(1+r)r^2\over(2+r)^2}\ge {4r^2\over9},
 \qquad {\phi\over a_0A_s^2}<{9\over4}.                 \tag{155.24}
$$

The last rational inequality follows from
18(1+r)-4(2+r)^2=2(1-r)(2r+1)>=0. Thus it also holds at the actual fixed Liouville amplitude.

For any ell>=0 the positive-only total pair
x_+=v_++2ell/A_s, x_-=v_- has score ell and

$$
 I(x)=J_{2a_0}(2a_0+2\ell/A_s)
       \le {\ell^2\over a_0A_s^2},                     \tag{155.25}
$$

by integrating J_v''(v+t)<=1/v on t>=0. This bound does not require the old half-mean window. Since F is a constrained minimum and h<c_q/2,
F(h)<=h^2/(a_0A_s^2)<c_q^2/(4a_0A_s^2).
Dividing by c_q and using c_q<phi proves the first inequality in(155.23).
For the second, divide by c_M/3 and write the resulting coefficient as
3phi(1-beta)^2/[4beta a_0A_s^2].
On beta>1/2,(1-beta)^2/beta<1/2 (its derivative is1-beta^-2<0). Equation(155.24) then bounds this coefficient strictly by27/32. This proves(155.23).

It follows that F(h)<p_old and F(h)<c_q, so both ell_pold and ell_cq exceed h. Equation(155.3) follows. Thus no actually admissible parameter example can give a strict interval enlargement by changing ONLY this rare-pool constraint while retaining Chapter 153's cap. This bounds the improvement available from changing only the rare-pool constraint; it supplies neither an actual-law counterexample nor optimality of h/2.

There is an explicit feasible construction for EVERY0<c<c_*. Take

$$
 \ell=c+\mathfrak h/2,\qquad
 x_+=v_++(2c+\mathfrak h)/A_s,\quad x_-=v_-,
 \qquad h_s=(\ell-2c)/2=(\mathfrak h/2-c)/2.             \tag{155.26}
$$

Then2c<ell<h, h_s>0, and(155.23–25) show
I(x)<p_old<=c_q. This supplies a positive feasible point in closed form without solving the variational problem. For instance c=h/4 and ell=3h/4 are an explicit fixed interior choice for every original admissible parameter. The full interval has endpoint c_q/4-5kappa/2>0.

The improved JOINT rate theorem nonetheless has a strictly larger domain of raw-total targets whenever1/2<beta<2/3. In that case p_old=c_M/3<c_q. Fix any score ell in(2c,h), start with its minimizing positive pair x(ell), and move along
x(t)=x(ell)+t(|B_s|,A_s), t>=0.
The score remains exactly ell, both coordinates remain positive, and I(x(t)) is continuous, starts below p_old by(155.23), and tends to infinity. By the intermediate value theorem it attains any prescribed rate in(p_old,c_q). These are legal fixed compact-region total parameters once a finite t is chosen. They are covered by(155.19) but not by Chapter 153's old sufficient coupling budget. This strict enlargement of the selection theorem does not imply a strict enlargement of the already capped bandwidth interval. For beta>=2/3 the two rate budgets themselves coincide.

### 155.7 同一数组的响应、有理值分组与曲率

We now prove that(155.2), without I<c_M/3, still meets the original-law interfaces. These checks also identify why the new number of trial pools does not enter the physical array.

On (153.23)'s original uniform environment, with failure
b_env=C[q^-1/2+(CQ^9/M)sqrt q+M^-8q^-3/2+Q^3/q+Q/M+M^-9]=o(1),
delete only the selected pair and ONE central anchor. Every other pool is retained in the outside elementary-symmetric coefficients. Removing three Bernoulli terms changes the calibration mean by at most3, and the derivative of this mean in log multiplier is its variance, comparable q. The outside multiplier calibrated at mean q-1 therefore differs by O(q^-1), uniformly over the deletion choice. No m terms are deleted and no union over m deletions is required.

Write t_o,D_o for that multiplier and variance, p=t_o L_0/(1+t_o L_0), v=p(1-p), a_3=kappa_{3,o}/D_o. The exact anchor ratio is

$$
 p_*={L_0\sum_{z=0}^2c_zE_{q-1-z}\over
                  \sum_{z=0}^2c_z(E_{q-z}+L_0E_{q-1-z})},
 \qquad(c_0,c_1,c_2)=(1,L_u+L_v,L_uL_v).                \tag{155.27}
$$

The fixed-offset prior expansion of Chapter 153 for offsets[-2,1], using positive finite averaging of those terms, gives uniformly even for exponentially large selected odds

$$
 p_*=p_{\rm ref}-(v/D_o)f_t(X)+O(q^{-2}),\quad
 p_{\rm ref}=p+v(a_3-1)/(2D_o),\quad
 f_t(X)={\sinh t\over\cosh t+\cosh X},\quad
 t=\ell\lambda+O_x(1).                                 \tag{155.28}
$$

D_o asymp q, p in[1/4,3/4], and all three central memberships n=n_0,n_0+1,n_0+2, n_0 asymp q/Q^3, are retained. The conditions on the outside array are F-measurable enlargements of the full-array good event. Applying the exact kernel on those enlargements and charging b_env afterwards avoids conditioning it on a hidden-split-dependent regularity event.

The original score compensation and gcd(P,Q)=1 give, for EVERY preimage in the selected two-binomial support,
H=Ql-Pk, H^0=(QK_--PK_+)/2,
bar X=(b_s/Q)(H-H^0), and

$$
 |X-\bar X|\le\Delta_X=C_x^{tot}Q^3(q/M+e^{-c_1Q^5}),
 \qquad\sup_zP(H=z\mid F)\le C_x^{tot}Q^{-5/2}.          \tag{155.29}
$$

The atom bound sums all preimages: positive-binomial mass in one residue modulo Q is at most Q^-1(1+C exp(-cQ)), and the negative-binomial maximum mass is C Q^-3/2. Their hypotheses are exactly K_\pm/lambda in fixed positive compact intervals, verified by the flags. C_x^{tot} is a fixed total-parameter constant, not the physical C_x.

On |X|<=h_s lambda, ell>h_s and direct differentiation of f_t gives

$$
 |f_t(\bar X)-1|\le C_x^{tot}e^{-(\ell-h_s)\lambda},\quad
 -\partial_H^2f_t(\bar X)\ge c_x^{tot}Q^{-2}e^{-\ell\lambda}.
                                                               \tag{155.30}
$$

Keep Chapter 153's occupied block C={|j|<=floor(aQ^2)}, where
H_I=2/a_0+2alpha^2/b_0 and
a=min(1/4,a_0/4,b_0/(4alpha),sqrt(kappa/(4H_I))).
The exact original count-line rate and actual relative row laws give
d_j>=d_*=q exp(-kappa lambda) on C, with failure
b_occ<=C Q^2[q^-1 exp(kappa lambda/4)+Q^9/M].
This uses neither independent actual rows nor a central Gaussian extrapolation. The original low and endpoint groups remain in the physical law.

Use EXACTLY Chapter 153's rational-arc parameters

$$
 \eta=e^{-(cQ^3+2Q^2)/(aQ^2)},\quad
 \mathfrak a=(400/\eta)^2,\ \mathfrak b=\lceil\mathfrak a\rceil,\quad
 U=e^{10\kappa\lambda},\quad
 V_R=c\lambda+\log\mathfrak b+\log Q,
$$
$$
 N=\lceil1000\mathfrak b\rho^{-1}\sqrt{V_R}\rceil,\quad
 \mathcal E(p)={4\pi^2\over\mathfrak b^2}
            \sum_{j\in C}d_j\,dist(2p\mu_j,\mathbb Z)^2. \tag{155.31}
$$

There is no lcm grid; log b=O_c(Q) and log N=c lambda+O_c(Q+log Q). All numerators, both signs and every denominator<=b are kept.
For each of the three memberships and three coarse plateau candidates
p_z=p_ref-vz/D_o, z=-1,0,1,
the central low-energy condition places k/(2p) in an F-measurable interval of width w_Q satisfying (153.32). Multiplication by(2N)^2 has exponential rates

$$
 2c-(\ell-h_s),\quad2c-\phi,\quad2c-c_q,\quad
                       2c+5\kappa-c_q/2.               \tag{155.32}
$$

All are strictly negative under(155.2) and0<h_s<ell-2c. Their lower-order logarithmic costs are O_{c,x}(Q+log Q), not functions of m. Distinct rational VALUES with denominators<=2N have separation at least(2N)^-2 independently of numerator size. Thus at most nine rational values cover the entire band. The plateau is used only for this location step.

For each retained value, the EXACT response(155.28) constrains f_t(bar X) to radius
epsilon_Q=C_x^{tot}[b Q^(9/2)exp(5kappa lambda)/sqrt q+q^-1+Delta_X].
Dividing by the curvature lower bound in(155.30) has rates

$$
 \ell+5\kappa-c_q/2,\qquad\ell-c_q,\qquad\ell-\phi,       \tag{155.33}
$$

again strictly negative, with lower-order O_{c,x}(Q+log Q).
Three integer H sites in one such interval contradict strong concavity: the middle point lies above the chord by at least one-half the curvature lower bound, whereas all three response values differ by at most2epsilon_Q. The conservative54-site allowance from Chapter 153 covers all candidates. Hence on ONE original realization

$$
 P_S\{\min_{1\le|p|\le N}\mathcal E(p)\le U\}
 \le e^{-Q^2}+\tau_m+2e^{-2h_s^2\lambda/V_x}
       +b_{\rm env}+b_{\rm reg}+C_x^{tot}Q^{-5/2}=o(1). \tag{155.34}
$$

b_reg is the same once-paid original regularity localization. Intersecting b_occ afterwards does not alter the selected conditional law. No m-, N-, numerator- or denominator-fold probability union is hidden. This is the exact location in Chapter 153's arithmetic proof where(155.19) replaces its former tau_Q; every other rate remains unchanged.

### 155.8 完整物理回接为什么不新增选池数量成本

(155.34) 是第 153 章有理值排除所需的同一数组事件。新的 $m$ 只进入该事件的失败概率 $\tau_m$；实际物理数组没有删除这 $m$ 个池，第 155.7 节的有限阶系数只删除选中二元组和一个锚点。因此第 153 章余下的确定性比较可以使用相同数组和相同参数。下面列出这一应用的条件及误差，而不重复其已经给出的全频率证明。

第一，保留 $J=\{j:d_j\ge Q^{3600}\}$ 和 $E=J^c$。在非零有理弧只展开原占据块 $C$，块外坐标全部精确保留；在零弧展开整个 $J$，$E$ 仍为原二项律。第 153 章 (153.37)–(153.46) 的线性相位一致二次和界、有限 Gauss 反演与 Poisson 求和适用，因为 $\log\mathfrak b=O_c(Q)$，而 $\log d_*=(c_q-\kappa)\lambda+O(1)$。弧宽与弧距之比仍为 $\exp[-(c_q-\kappa)\lambda+O_c(Q)]$。新的试验池数没有进入这些条件。

第二，(155.34) 在整个分子带上同时保证原始对偶能量大于 $U$。原来的非中心位移至多为 $\sqrt U/4$，分母损失至多为 $e^{3\kappa\lambda}$；故所有非零弧上平移后的能量至少为 $e^{7\kappa\lambda}/4$。格点 Gaussian 乘积的平移精度至少为 $e^{(c_q-3\kappa)\lambda}$，求和不产生 $\mathfrak b^{|C|}$ 因子。两阶标记使用同一个规范化实倾斜 $e^{uW}$，其中 $W=s_{\rm lat}+G^2/2$，并在固定物理输出 $y$ 处微分。原始截距、所有经验中心相位、块外二次相位及 Gaussian 残余均保留。

全频率积分唯一的逆带宽体积支付为

$$
\begin{aligned}
 CQ^{20}(1+\rho^{-1})\eta^{aQ^2}
 &\le CQ^{20}e^{-2Q^2},\\
 \mathcal W
 &\le C\mathfrak b^2(1+\rho^{-1})
 \left[e^{-e^{7\kappa\lambda}/32}
       +e^{-\rho^2N^2/(100\mathfrak b^2)}\right],\\
 \rho^2N^2/\mathfrak b^2&\ge10^6V_R.
\end{aligned}
\tag{155.35}
$$

原始数据上的 $\tau_m$ 是坏事件概率，没有乘以 $\rho^{-1}$。零弧上非零模的误差为 $CQ^{14}e^{-cQ^{3600}}$，补回参考密度尾部的误差为 $e^{-c_1\kappa Q^{7/2}}$。这些条件恰给出第 153 章的统一估计

$$
\max_{0\le k\le2}
\left\|\left.\partial_u^k(f_{{\rm lat},u}-g_u)\right|_{u=0}\right\|_\infty
\le CQ^{-400}.
\tag{155.36}
$$

第三，格点参考只用于比较。$J$ 上原二项计数的固定阶带符号惊异测度误差仍至多为 $CQ^{-444}$；$E$ 完全精确保留。使用同一个物理核

$$
K_r(n,y)=\left(\frac{y-T(n)}{\sigma}\right)^{2r}
                   \varphi_\sigma(y-T(n)),\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}K_r(n,y)\,dy=\mathbb E G^{2r},\quad 0\le r\le2
\tag{155.37}
$$

得到与 $\sigma$ 无关的带符号 $L^1$ 收缩。令 $q_k(y)\,dy=\mathbb E[W^k;Y\in dy]$，则 $W=s+G^2/2$ 的有限二项展开将这一步直接用于 $q_0,q_1,q_2$。条件平方项使用
$q_1^2/q_0=\sup_z(2zq_1-z^2q_0)$，先截断 $|z|\le Q^{10}$，再用 $\mathbb E W^4\le CQ^4$ 支付尾部，误差为 $O(Q^{-16})+O(Q^{-424})$。完整选择律的同元组密度满足 $0\le h\le C$ 和 $\|h-1\|_2=a_x=O_{\Pr}(Q^{-5/2})$；保留其精确 $\log h$ 惊异修正后，同核比较成本为 $Ca_xQ^2=o_{\Pr}(1)$。

第四，在 $|y|\le\sqrt{100\nu\log Q}$ 内，原完整连续参考仍满足 $g_0\ge cQ^{-60}$、$|g_1|+|g_2|\le CQ^4$，因为本章带宽满足 $\sigma\le\mathcal B^{-1}$ 且 $\sigma\to0$。对实比值 $F=f_{{\rm lat},u}/g_u$ 使用第 153 章给出的精确两阶商式，最大系数为 $CQ^{188}$；(155.36) 先给出 $F\ge1/2$，再控制 $\partial_u^2\log F$。同一规范化倾斜的恒等式

$$
V_{\rm post}(y)-V_{\rm prior}
 =\frac12+\left.\partial_u^2\log f_u(y)\right|_{u=0}
\tag{155.38}
$$

因此合法，未以零阶比较代替二阶比较。全输出尾部沿用原始实平方配方和 Chernoff 界，概率至多为 $CQ^{-40}$；条件 Jensen 与上述四阶矩给出 $CQ^{-18}$ 的后验方差尾部。原始外部能量先在独立核心密度内平移，之后才分离外部惊异并抵消其精确先验方差；这一参考回接与非中心比较均不支付逆噪声因子。

这些应用的物理对象和有限系数均与第 153 章相同。因此 (155.36)–(155.38)、同核选择回接以及原完整参考计算给出 (155.5)。带权密度比较同时给出 $\mathbb E_xY^2\to\nu$，积分 $R_*$ 得到 (155.6)，其中 $C_xm_x$ 保留精确有限值。扩大的稀有总数集合只改变证明中选取哪个二元组，未改变此处的后验、噪声或输出范围。

### 155.9 方法归属与仍需突破的条件

Binomial–Poisson 的质量比值和 Stirling 方法来自经典 Poisson 近似；共同总数条件下的多项分配核、Hellinger 亲和度及其乘积恒等式也属成熟工具。第 155.4–155.5 节的模型推导把它们用于同一个实际奇偶记录，保留路径端点和增长计数向量，再以独立的精确条件律处理揭示后的隐藏分配。Le Cam 和 Leskelä 的原始版本、规范化及可迁移条件见 [Library 补充](../../../Library/Dynamics/iyer2025empirical.md)。

旧条件 $I<\min(c_q,c_M/3)$ 与新条件 $I<c_q$ 的可行目标集在 $1/2<\beta<2/3$ 时严格不同；但第 155.6 节证明两个集合投影到现有带宽轴后相同，端点均为 $c_q/4-5\kappa/2$。这个端点是保留证明约束的充分端点，未证明是原模型的必要边界。继续扩大带宽需要改进响应曲率、有理值分组或带标记别名控制中的实际约束，单独提高选池近似精度无法达到这一目的。第 153 章原结论及其较窄选池接口保持有效；本章不主张端点成立、全 $c$ 结论或全局原创性。

## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）

## 156. 衰减复振幅下的递增频率零点与相对误差边界

第 154 章处理局部频率有界、编号为 $O(t)$ 的零点。本章将编号推进到 $t\sqrt{\log t}$：局部内点振幅已按 $t$ 的负幂衰减，因此需要先给出明确的振幅下界，才能将绝对积分误差转成相对误差。新的固定局部指数包络在原始选择计数律上建立，并保留每个区域自己的实正归一化质量。

结论保持原来的 $\eta\to0$、$t=\eta/\sqrt\delta\to\infty$ 和严格噪声裕量，不限制 $t$ 的发散速度，不把经验参数替换为确定极限。固定正比例的 $t^2$ 编号仍未解决；本章给出它与现有方法之间的具体误差缺口。以下为普通数学推导，未作 Lean 认证。

### 156.1 递增局部频率下的统一结论

**定理 156.1（原始选择计数的递增频率零点）。** The original selected-count zeros admit simultaneous localization through indices of order t sqrt(log t), with a vanishing error in the unscaled phase coordinate. The range exceeds every fixed multiple of t but is o(t^2). The new ingredient is a quantitative exponential-mark return on each real region, combined with the second-order local density expansion. It controls a slowly growing local frequency even when the corresponding characteristic amplitude tends to zero.

At the ACTUAL selected equal-region-mass field h0=h_equal^P(y,xi), put R_c=-D>0. The boundary and interior regions, denoted B and I, are separated at xi r_sc, with xi in a fixed compact subset of (0,w0), w0=sqrt(2/3). Let b,i be the actual regional means, v_B,v_I their variances, and kappa3,B,kappa3,I their third cumulants. Write
$$
 d=i-b,\qquad A=(v_I-v_B)/d^2,\qquad
 B_3=(\kappa_{3,I}-\kappa_{3,B})/d^3.
 \tag{156.1}
$$
B_3 is a phase coefficient, not the original count scale B. All these quantities are evaluated on the SAME realized count array and at the SAME real h0 and physical output. Retain the exact real profile branch r=r_-(h0,y), K=-F''(r;h0,y)>0, defined below. Set
$$
 \mathcal D=d\sqrt K\asymp t,\quad
 Y_\rho=\mathcal D\sqrt{2\rho\log t},\quad
 L_\rho=(\rho+2)\log t,\qquad 0<\rho<3,
$$
$$
 \mathcal R_\rho(t)=(\log t)^3/t^2+t^{\rho-3}=o(1).
 \tag{156.2}
$$
Here rho is any fixed number in that interval; it does not change with Q. Every sufficiently large t is greater than one. For z_k=(2k+1)pi times the imaginary unit, define
$$
 z_{G,k}=\frac{2z_k}{1+\sqrt{1-2Az_k}},\qquad
 p_k=z_{G,k}-\frac{B_3z_{G,k}^3}{6(1-Az_{G,k})}.
 \tag{156.3}
$$
The square root is the branch near one. On the range below, |Az_k|=O(sqrt(log t)/t), so both that branch and the denominator are unambiguous.

There is one simple zero h_k of the EXACT original selected negative-sign normalizer for each |(2k+1)pi|<=Y_rho, and, simultaneously for all those indices,
$$
 \sup_{|(2k+1)\pi|\le Y_\rho}
 |d(h_k-h0)-p_k|=O_{\rm Prob}(\mathcal R_\rho(t))=o_{\rm Prob}(1).
 \tag{156.4}
$$
The absolute field error is O_Prob(R_rho/d). The count domains and exclusion of additional zeros are specified in Section 156.7. In particular this is not just convergence after dividing the phase by t^2. Taking rho=1 gives O_Prob((log t)^3/t^2) phase error through a fixed empirical multiple of t sqrt(log t).

Every probability assertion is uniform over compact physical y and the stated separator compact, separately in the ORIGINAL pair and path actual-data experiments, uniformly over deterministic size-q supports. Constants are uniform on each common tight-constant data class; exhausting those classes gives the displayed probability statements. The result holds for every admissible eta/noise sequence, including arbitrarily slow t divergence. No deterministic limit of the empirical m is assumed. There is one simultaneous analytic bound on each realization, not a separate probabilistic event for each zero or an independence assumption for empirical h0,d,K.

A fixed-positive-multiple-of-t^2 extension would require a fixed c_*>0 and |2k+1|<=c_*t^2 with o(1) phase error and a legitimate nonlinear complex-saddle description. Section 156.9 identifies the missing relative-amplitude estimate at that scale. The present theorem neither proves nor refutes that extension. The preceding chapters retain their stated scope.

### 156.2 原始选择计数与精确实剖面

The original level is Q; Q_x is the auxiliary product COUNT law. The unchanged definitions are
$$
 \delta=Q^{-1/2},\quad B^2=q\delta^5,\quad
 Q_x(n)=\prod_j{C_j\choose n_j}p_j^{n_j}(1-p_j)^{C_j-n_j},
$$
$$
 v_j=C_jp_j(1-p_j)/B^2,\quad V=\sum_jv_j,\quad
 C_2=\delta^{-1}\sum_jv_j^2,\quad
 x_j=(n_j-\mu_j)/B,\quad e_j=(\mu_j-C_jp_j)/B,
$$
$$
 E=\sum_jx_j^2,\quad D=\sum_j(x_j+e_j),\quad
 T=(E-V)/\sqrt\delta,\quad a=(2V)^{-1}+\eta,\quad
 t=\eta/\sqrt\delta,\quad m=\sqrt{2V^4/C_2},\quad
 r_{\rm sc}=m\sqrt{\eta/\delta},\quad h_{\rm sc}=\eta r_{\rm sc}.
 \tag{156.5}
$$
The full-q selected law is literally
$$
 P_x(n)=L_x(k)Q_x(n),\quad k=\sum_j n_j,\quad
 BD=k-m_{J0},\quad m_{J0}=\sum_jC_jp_j,
$$
$$
 L_x(k)=\frac{[w^{q-k}]\prod_{l\notin J0}(1-p_l+p_lw)}
 {[w^q]\prod_l(1-p_l+p_lw)}.
 \tag{156.6}
$$
J0 is the union of the original observed groups; the outside labels supply the residual q-k. No total-count constraint D=0 is introduced. The entire finite sum studied here is exactly
$$
 N_P^-(h,y)=\sum_{D(n)<0}P_x(n)
 \exp\{aD(n)^2+hD(n)-(T(n)-y)^2/(2\sigma^2)\}.
 \tag{156.7}
$$
It is entire in h because the count tuple is finite. Region B is 0<R_c<=xi r_sc; I is R_c>xi r_sc. Exact floors, low tuples, noncentral calibration e, outside labels, count boundaries and the original residual T-y remain in (156.7).

We keep eta>0 tending to zero, t tending to infinity, and sigma>0 tending to zero subject ONLY to
$$
 \limsup\log(1/\sigma)/Q^3<c_q/2,\qquad
 \log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),\quad c_q=\phi(1-\beta)/\beta.
 \tag{156.8}
$$
The common classes have c<=V,C2<=C, v_*<=C delta, n_g<=C delta^-4, a block of at least c/delta variances in [c delta,C delta], p_j in [1/4,3/4], sum C_j<=CB^2, ||e||<=C delta^5, and (sum|e_j|)^2<=C delta^6. These are inherited actual-data events, not deterministic assumptions imposed on a different model.

Choose the same admissible high block H={j:C_j>=exp(zeta Q^3)}, with log(1/sigma)<=lQ^3 eventually, l<c_q/2 and 2zeta<c_q-l. All low tuples are kept exactly. Write C_H=diag(v_j), b_H=(v_j), V_H=sum_H v_j, d_H=b_H/V_H and A0=C_H-b_Hb_H^T/V_H. The centered conditional Gaussian energy transform at squared charge R0 is
$$
 \mathcal K(w,R0)=-\tfrac12\log\det(I-2wA0)
  +R0w d_H^T(I-2wA0)^{-1}d_H+\tfrac12\delta\sigma^2w^2.
 \tag{156.9}
$$
At H_y=V+sqrt(delta)y let f_r^0(H_y) be its noisy energy density. Retain
$$
 \gamma=\eta-\{(2V_H)^{-1}-(2V)^{-1}\},\quad
 g_y^0(r)=e^{\gamma r^2}f_r^0(H_y),\quad
 \ell_y(R0)=\log g_y^0(\sqrt{R0}),
$$
$$
 F(r;h,y)=\ell_y(r^2)-\ell_y(0)-hr,\quad
 F_r(r_-;h,y)=0,\quad K=-F_{rr}(r_-;h,y),
$$
$$
 \Lambda=F(r_-)+\log h+\tfrac12\log(2\pi/K),\quad
 C_B=2\ell_y'(0)/h^2,\quad
 C_I=F''''/(8K^2)+5(F''')^2/(24K^3).
 \tag{156.10}
$$
This is an exact REAL comparator profile. We do not assume its logarithm continues to a useful complex neighborhood of squared charge. Finite sigma, full empirical V,C2, the high-block defect and physical y are retained before every limit.

Chapters 148 and 150 supply the unique positive branch near w0 r_sc, the equal-mass field h0, and, on bounded Lambda windows, r_-/r_sc->w0, K/(2eta)->1, h r_sc comparable to t^2, and
$$
 |F^{(j)}|/K^{j/2}\le C_jt^{2-j}\quad(3\le j\le6)
 \tag{156.11}
$$
on a fixed fractional well neighborhood. These are derivatives from the exact real resolvent/Fourier formula, including its prefactor, not derivatives of a C0 approximation. The real region masses satisfy
$$
 N_P^B=(M_0/h)[1+C_B+o(t^{-2})],\quad
 N_P^I=(M_0/h)e^\Lambda[1+C_I+o(t^{-2})],\quad
 M_0=\sigma\sqrt{\delta/V_H}\,g_y^0(0)\asymp\sigma.
 \tag{156.12}
$$
At h0 both are positive and equal. Hence Lambda(h0)=O(t^-2), h0 comparable to h_sc, and F(r_-;h0)=-log t+O(1). The retained actual moments give
$$
 b=h0^{-1}(1+O(t^{-2})),\quad v_B=h0^{-2}(1+O(t^{-2})),\quad
 \kappa_{3,B}=O(h0^{-3}),
$$
$$
 i=r_-+F'''/(2K^2)+o(1/(\sqrt Kt^2)),\quad
 v_I=K^{-1}(1+O(t^{-2})),\quad
 \kappa_{3,I}=K^{-3/2}\{b_3+o(t^{-2})\},\quad b_3=F'''/K^{3/2}.
 \tag{156.13}
$$
In particular d comparable to r_sc, A>0, A=O(t^-2), B_3=O(t^-4), and A mathcalD^2=(v_I-v_B)K=1+O(t^-2). Fixed polynomial moment control in (156.13) alone is not enough for our new complex range.

### 156.3 两个原始区域的固定指数包络

At h0 use X=h0 R_c in B and Z=sqrt K(R_c-r_-) in I. We first prove the new estimates
$$
 E_{P,I,h0}[(1+|Z|^p)e^{a_0|Z|}]\le C_{p,a_0}
       \quad\hbox{for each fixed }p\in\mathbb N_0,\ 0\le a_0<\infty,
$$
$$
 E_{P,B,h0}[(1+X^p)e^{\theta X}]\le C_p
       \quad\hbox{for some fixed }\theta>0.
 \tag{156.14}
$$
The endpoint theta is allowed to depend on the separator compact. We do not claim (156.14) for every theta<1. The estimates are proved with the marks inside the original-law return, not deduced by summing polynomial moments.

For the centered profile, local concavity at the interior branch gives exp(-cZ^2+a0|Z|) on a fixed fractional band. Outside it but inside a fixed moderate-charge compact, the unmarked gap is exp(-ct^2) and the added mark is exp(O(a0t)); this remains smaller than every fixed inverse power of t. For all remaining charges use the same-fiber bound of Chapter 146, for both centered and actual-e profiles,
$$
 g_y^\circ(\sqrt{\eta/\delta}\,u)/g_y^\circ(0)
 \le C\exp\left[t^2\left\{u^2-\frac{c u^4}{1+\eta u^2}\right\}\right]
 \quad(|u|\ge M).
 \tag{156.15}
$$
Choose a fixed sufficiently large M, then eta small: the braces are <=-B0u^2 for any desired fixed B0. Since |Z|<=Ct(1+|u|), this absorbs exp(a0|Z|) and every fixed local polynomial. Relative normalization uses exp(F(r_-))sqrt(2pi/K)=e^Lambda/h0; the scaled Jacobian and remaining normalization cost only powers of t. No polynomial Q factor is multiplied by exp(-ct^2) in this tail argument.

At the endpoint the anchored derivative estimate gives F(r)<=-c h0r for 0<=r<=d0 r_sc, with fixed small d0. On d0 r_sc<=r<=xi_1 r_sc, where xi_1<w0 bounds the separator compact, the limiting coexistence action is strictly negative. The ratio -F(r)/(h0r) therefore has a positive uniform lower bound on this interval for all sufficiently large levels. The denominator is bounded away from zero in the scaled variable, and the retained real finite-profile convergence is uniform there. Combining the two intervals yields F(r)<=-c_xi h0r on the whole boundary region. Choose 0<theta<c_xi/2. The endpoint normalized Jacobian is h0r_sc=O(t^2); the tails are then integrable against (1+X^p)e^{theta X}. This proves the comparator versions of (156.14), including their quantitative local tail payments.

Now return those envelopes on the SAME full count tuple. We give the details because the bounded-real-strip shift in Chapter 154 only supplied a much weaker e^{L|R_c-mu|/d} mark.

The exact real-resolvent interpolation from Chapter 150 of the noncentral mean r d_H-theta0 e_H, 0<=theta0<=1, gives
$$
 \sup_{|r|\le M\sqrt{\eta/\delta},\,|y|\le R}
 |f_r^e(H_y)/f_r^0(H_y)-1|\le C_M\delta^4.
 \tag{156.16}
$$
Its Fourier envelope is (1+c delta xi^2)^(-c'/delta); the real exponent change is O(delta^4) and the normalized prefactor change is O(delta^(9/2)). Multiplying (156.16) by either envelope in (156.14) and integrating costs a bounded comparator expectation. Taking a supremum of the exponential mark over the entire moderate compact would instead lose exp(Ct); we do NOT do that. Outside this compact (156.15) pays both profiles directly. The noncentral contribution is O(delta^4) relative to each own real region mass, with no inverse sigma.

Uniformly for EVERY exact low tuple, the high-cell estimates of Chapter 137 are
$$
 |\log(\hbox{lifted density}/\phi_C)|\le\mathcal E_Q,\quad
 |D-D_G|\le\mathcal E_Q,\quad |T-T_G|/\sigma\le\mathcal E_Q,
 \quad\mathcal E_Q=P(Q)e^{-b_0Q^3},\ b_0>0.
 \tag{156.17}
$$
T_G retains full V,e. An interior exponential mark has cell variation bounded by C sqrt K mathcalE_Q times its envelope, with an additional fixed polynomial for polynomial marks.
